rationale: This is a pure preprocessing wrapper (IND_ZSCORE) around the archive's existing best signal with no new economic content, i.e., exactly the kind of cosmetic single-knob variant the objective says to avoid, and the "is it a sector bet" question could be answered by a sector-attribution diagnostic rather than a new signal slot.
evidence: a pure preprocessing wrapper (IND_ZSCORE) around the archive's existing best signal

rationale: The MIN conjunction is a genuinely different functional form for testing whether profitability and asset-growth discipline interact rather than blend, though the two ingredient legs are both well-documented anomalies (Novy-Marx profitability, Cooper-Gulen-Schill asset growth) and it overlaps materially with profit_weighted_operating_asset_discipline, so any gain must come purely from the operator.
evidence: it overlaps materially with profit_weighted_operating_asset_discipline

rationale: The depreciation floor is a well-motivated fix for the small-denominator noise that plausibly killed the 3-year version's FMB slope, but bundling it with a window extension from 3 to 5 years confounds attribution and the change-in-earnings numerator makes this partly a slow-moving profitability-growth signal.

rationale: Scaling the internal-funding gap by liquid slack introduces a balance-sheet dimension the archive has not tested and the negative sign matches the expression's natural direction, though it is close in spirit to published external-financing-need/net-financing anomalies and mixes a flow numerator with a partly stock denominator, so a high correlation with cash_coverage_of_required_investment should be checked.
evidence: mixes a flow numerator with a partly stock denominator

rationale: Cumulative five-year acquisition spending is a distinct construct from the one-year goodwill change and the serial-acquirer hypothesis is economically coherent, but serial-acquirer underperformance is itself a published result and the profitability leg is unchanged, so this is an extension rather than a new mechanism.
evidence: this is an extension rather than a new mechanism

rationale: Replacing the raw hiring rate (a documented stand-alone anomaly) with hiring relative to realized sales growth is a defensible diagnosis-driven fix, but it reuses the exact "growth minus sales growth" template from the inventory-overbuild signal with a different input and inherits the emp-driven coverage and reporting-lag weaknesses that likely hurt the earlier labor test.
evidence: reuses the exact "growth minus sales growth" template

rationale: This is a mechanical ensemble of the archive's two best-performing signals rather than a new mechanism, and the two legs overlap substantially (both are cash-flow-versus-investment constructs, with the acquisition leg already paired with an oancf-based profitability rank), so the archive's own SUMRANK precedent (self_funding_plus_investment_payoff, alpha diluted to 0.029/t 1.96) predicts averaging-down rather than incremental insight.
evidence: the archive's own SUMRANK precedent predicts averaging-down rather than incremental insight

rationale: Re-deflating cumulative acquisitions by the firm's own cumulative organic investment instead of assets is a substantive composition-versus-scale test with a clear diagnostic payoff either way, though it remains a deflator refinement of an already-successful archive signal and the depreciation-floored denominator will behave erratically for asset-light acquirers.
evidence: the depreciation-floored denominator will behave erratically for asset-light acquirers

rationale: The COALESCE-to-zero plus MAX(.,dp) construction means the majority of firms with little or no goodwill are scored purely by oancf/dp, so the signal is a mixture of a cash-flow-to-depreciation profitability ratio (which will dominate the long leg) and a goodwill-intensity ratio, making the computed quantity inconsistent with the stated stale-acquisition-premium hypothesis and confounded with the known goodwill-to-assets anomaly.
evidence: the majority of firms with little or no goodwill are scored purely by oancf/dp

rationale: The diagnosis is legitimate and specific — an after-depreciation earnings numerator is mechanically depressed by the same capex sitting in the denominator — and substituting operating cash flow breaks that link while retaining the depreciation-floored cumulative denominator, making this a mechanism-driven fix rather than a horizon or scaling tweak.
evidence: making this a mechanism-driven fix rather than a horizon or scaling tweak

rationale: The transition dimension of this exact ratio was already tested and failed in the archive (own_history_position_of_funding_coverage), and a raw first difference of an unbounded, depreciation-floored ratio is scale-dependent and dominated by transitory capex/cash-flow noise, so the discretization diagnosis is plausible but not enough to make this substantively different rather than a re-transformation of a failed construct.
evidence: The transition dimension of this exact ratio was already tested and failed in the archive

rationale: Benchmarking five-year cumulative capex against five-year cumulative depreciation is an economically meaningful replacement-rate standard that is distinct from both the own-mean norm and the cross-sectional asset-growth channel already tested, and the null and positive outcomes carry different, informative interpretations — though the sub-replacement leg will be correlated with the classic investment/CMA factor and the profitability-minus-investment rank-difference form has repeatedly produced weak FF5 alphas in this archive.
evidence: the profitability-minus-investment rank-difference form has repeatedly produced weak FF5 alphas in this archive

rationale: This is algebraically almost the same object as the archive's cash_coverage_of_required_investment (oancf/max(capx+aqc, dp), alpha 0.041, t 3.36) — surplus cash deflated by depreciation is a reparametrization of that same coverage ratio using identical inputs — so it is a cosmetic re-scaling rather than a new mechanism, and free-cash-flow-to-capital-consumption is itself close to published FCF/investment-anomaly territory.
evidence: it is a cosmetic re-scaling rather than a new mechanism

rationale: The construct is coherent and sign-consistent, but it is essentially spanned by three existing archive signals (cash_generation_vs_acquisitive_expansion, cash_generation_vs_serial_acquisitiveness, unearned_goodwill_without_cash_flow_growth) and amounts to swapping one already-tested leg for another already-tested leg, i.e. a component recombination rather than a new economic channel.
evidence: a component recombination rather than a new economic channel

rationale: Economically sensible and internally consistent, but it differs from cash_flow_payoff_on_cumulative_investment only by adding aqc to the denominator — a single-term tweak with identical data requirements, so the claim that it will lift coverage above 0.064 is unfounded and the proposal reads as a robustness variant rather than a substantively different design.
evidence: a single-term tweak with identical data requirements

rationale: Extending the funding-gap numerator to a three-year cumulative deficit while holding the liquidity buffer contemporaneous is a legitimate persistence test (chronic external dependence vs a transitory capex spike) with a correctly signed expression, though the mixed flow/stock deflator MAX(che, TS_SUM(dp,3)) makes the units of the ratio firm-dependent and should be diagnosed if results diverge from the one-year version.
evidence: mixed flow/stock deflator MAX(che, TS_SUM(dp,3)) makes the units of the ratio firm-dependent

rationale: The hypothesis says the cash cow must be "not merely high but steady," yet the expression contains no cash-flow *level* at all — a firm with negligible but placid cash flow scores maximally — and the low-volatility leg largely rediscovers the known earnings/cash-flow-volatility and low-risk anomalies rather than adding a cross-theme interaction.
evidence: the expression contains no cash-flow level at all

rationale: The "mix" is not actually measured: firms with zero R&D score identically whether they are serial acquirers or pure non-investors, so for the bulk of the cross-section the second leg collapses to R&D/depreciation — i.e. the well-documented R&D-intensity anomaly stacked on a cash-profitability rank — rather than a build-versus-buy contrast.
evidence: The "mix" is not actually measured

rationale: This is a deflator swap on the archive's leading signal (internal_versus_purchased_growth_spending_mix, alpha 0.064/t 4.74) with an identical profitability leg and an identical R&D-minus-acquisition contrast, i.e. precisely the kind of cosmetic variant the objective warns against, and the program denominator itself contains aqc so the "sourcing tilt" and the deflator move together in a mechanically confounded way.
evidence: This is a deflator swap on the archive's leading signal

rationale: The stock-versus-flow reframing is a genuinely different horizon and investor error than the archive's spending-window tests and the sign is coherent for *purchased* (balance-sheet) intangibles, but the tangibility-minus-intangibility leg is heavily industry-determined and overlaps the known goodwill-intensity and asset-tangibility characteristics, so it should be industry-neutralized before it can be credited as novel.
evidence: the tangibility-minus-intangibility leg is heavily industry-determined and overlaps the known goodwill-intensity characteristics

rationale: This is a mechanical ensemble of two already-evaluated archive signals, and the stated justification is factually wrong — both legs are driven by aqc (it sits in the coverage denominator and is subtracted in the sourcing leg), so the claimed independence that motivates the attribution test does not hold.
evidence: both legs are driven by aqc

rationale: Revenue deflation of both legs is a scaling the archive has not used and reframes the mechanism as business-model capital intensity rather than balance-sheet harvesting, the sign convention (NEG on capital formation) matches the hypothesis, and using ΔPP&E-gross plus inventory rather than capex is a defensible refinement — though the cash-margin leg is close to published cash-based operating profitability and the sales deflator will carry strong industry tilts.
evidence: the cash-margin leg is close to published cash-based operating profitability

rationale: This is the third deflator applied to the same profitability-minus-acquisition-intensity construct already tested at asset scale (0.047/t 3.75) and program scale (0.048/t 4.01), and deflating acquisitions by the firm's own cash flow reintroduces oancf on both sides of the difference, making any improvement hard to attribute to the sourcing mechanism.
evidence: This is the third deflator applied to the same profitability-minus-acquisition-intensity construct already tested

rationale: The hypothesis is explicitly interactive ("acquiring *when* profitability peaks") but SUMRANK is additive, so a high-own-cycle-profitability non-acquirer is scored identically to a trough-cycle acquirer, and since the profitability leg on its own should predict returns positively it works directly against the stated negative sign, leaving the signal essentially a repackaged acquisition-intensity bet.
evidence: SUMRANK is additive, so a high-own-cycle-profitability non-acquirer is scored identically to a trough-cycle acquirer

rationale: This is a mechanical ensemble of the archive's two top performers built from the same underlying `xrd`/`aqc` series, so the "partly independent measurement error" claim is doubtful and the outcome will be largely bounded by the two parents — a cosmetic blend rather than a new mechanism.
evidence: a mechanical ensemble of the archive's two top performers built from the same underlying `xrd`/`aqc` series

rationale: A strict ablation of an already-evaluated signal and therefore low in novelty, but it is a cheap, decisive attribution test of whether the R&D leg carries any incremental content, and the expression matches the hypothesis; note the coarse 0–5 integer leg and that `COALESCE(aqc,0)` conflates missing with genuinely zero acquisition activity.
evidence: A strict ablation of an already-evaluated signal and therefore low in novelty

rationale: R&D-to-assets and capex-to-assets are both long-published anomalies and their difference plus a profitability level is close to a linear recombination of known factors, and the tangible/intangible mix is dominated by sector membership rather than capital-allocation choice, so the "falsification test" framing does not rescue it from being a rediscovery.
evidence: R&D-to-assets and capex-to-assets are both long-published anomalies

rationale: A defensible diagnosis-driven repair whose IND_ZSCORE genuinely alters the ordering rather than being monotone-neutral, though it remains one operator away from an already-failed archive signal and leaves the profitability leg un-neutralized, so the asymmetry may limit interpretability of a null result.
evidence: it remains one operator away from an already-failed archive signal

rationale: The two legs are conceptually and mechanically distinct from prior variants (margin *trend* rather than asset-yield level, paired with acquisition intensity), the sign follows naturally from the expression, and the substitution is motivated by an actual precision result in the archive; watch for instability of TREND on a sales-deflated ratio when sales are small or negative.
evidence: watch for instability of TREND on a sales-deflated ratio when sales are small or negative

rationale: Internally consistent — both legs load positively on the "failed acquirer," so the negative expected sign is correct — and the flow-based reformulation with a same-signed rank sum is a reasonable fix for the weak slope of the goodwill version, but it sits close to two existing archive signals (serial acquisitiveness and goodwill-validation) and to the published acquirer-underperformance literature, limiting how much genuinely new information it can deliver.
evidence: it sits close to two existing archive signals and to the published acquirer-underperformance literature

rationale: Industry-neutralizing the R&D-minus-acquisition leg is a substantive (not cosmetic) test of whether the archive's best signal is a firm-level allocation effect or a disguised pharma/software-versus-conglomerate sector tilt, and the precedent from the built-versus-bought stock signal shows the transform is not monotone in its effect.
evidence: Industry-neutralizing the R&D-minus-acquisition leg is a substantive (not cosmetic) test

rationale: The subsumption test is legitimately informative, but the claim that the legs are independent is overstated — asset-light R&D-intensive firms mechanically have small capex/dp denominators and therefore inflated payoff ratios, so the two legs are economically correlated even though they share no raw variable.
evidence: the claim that the legs are independent is overstated

rationale: Sign direction and construction are internally consistent and the peak-deal leg is a genuine measurement change, but it rebuilds an already-tested short-side signal from two archive legs, one of which (the five-year cash-margin trend) had an essentially zero cross-sectional slope on its own, so the hoped-for fmb improvement rests on thin evidence.
evidence: the five-year cash-margin trend had an essentially zero cross-sectional slope on its own

rationale: A difference of two three-year moving averages is close to a rescaled five-year OLS slope and will be highly correlated with the TREND version, so with an unchanged second leg this is a cosmetic estimator swap on an already-evaluated signal rather than a substantively different construction.
evidence: a cosmetic estimator swap on an already-evaluated signal

rationale: The expression contrasts a five-year cumulative R&D intensity against a single-year peak acquisition intensity, so the scale mismatch means the "contrast" will be dominated by the R&D sum and will mostly reproduce the existing mix signal rather than testing whether large deals are the locus of mispricing.
evidence: the scale mismatch means the "contrast" will be dominated by the R&D sum

rationale: Because cumulative depreciation exceeds cumulative R&D for the large majority of firms, MAX(xrd5, dp5) collapses to dp5 and the signal becomes acquisitions per dollar of capital consumption — a near-rediscovery of the already-tested acquisitive_share_of_investment_program — so the stated "build-versus-buy tilt" mechanism does not match what the expression computes.
evidence: MAX(xrd5, dp5) collapses to dp5

rationale: This is essentially the archive's best signal with one term added to the denominator, and the change is not innocuous — putting five-year capex in the denominator makes the "purchased share" mechanically decreasing in capital intensity, so the long leg tilts toward high-capex firms, directly opposing the investment-discipline direction the rest of the archive establishes and confounding the coverage gain with a new sector/capital-intensity exposure.
evidence: putting five-year capex in the denominator makes the "purchased share" mechanically decreasing in capital intensity

rationale: Despite the disclaimer, this is an averaging of the archive's two top-performing signals whose legs (purchased share of growth budget and count of acquisition years) are near-mechanically correlated, so it will almost certainly land between them and teach nothing about mechanism, with the arbitrary 1:2 nested-SUMRANK weighting adding a free parameter rather than an economic hypothesis.
evidence: legs are near-mechanically correlated, so it will almost certainly land between them

rationale: The self-accumulated-versus-purchased intangible comparison is a genuinely new and well-motivated framing of the accounting-mismeasurement story, though the R&D-to-assets leg risks reducing the result to the well-documented R&D-intensity anomaly and the absence of industry neutralization is a known weakness in this exact channel given the archive's earlier tangibility results.
evidence: the R&D-to-assets leg risks reducing the result to the well-documented R&D-intensity anomaly

rationale: This is a near-monotone reparameterization of the already-tested industry_neutral_built_versus_bought_stock (difference of intan/at and ppent/at recast as intan/(intan+ppent), same industry z-score, same cash-profit leg), i.e. a cosmetic deflator change to an evaluated signal rather than a new mechanism.
evidence: a cosmetic deflator change to an evaluated signal rather than a new mechanism

rationale: Replacing the raw asset-scaled acquisition intensity with the bounded purchased share is a defensible, specifically diagnosed fix to the weak Fama-MacBeth slope of the earlier failed-acquirer short, but the test should be interpreted cautiously since the three-year cash-flow-change leg is itself a strong standalone predictor and may carry most of the alpha.
evidence: the three-year cash-flow-change leg is itself a strong standalone predictor and may carry most of the alpha

rationale: Testing a change in the bounded allocation mix across non-overlapping windows is a substantively different (level versus transition) question and is properly motivated by why the raw-intensity version failed, though the share degenerates to a noisy 0/1 flip for non-R&D firms and is undefined for firms doing neither, so coverage and composition stability need checking before any positive result is believed.
evidence: the share degenerates to a noisy 0/1 flip for non-R&D firms

rationale: The "profitability per unit of profitability instability" ratio is a coherent quality-scaled profitability construct rather than a literal rediscovery, but it sits close to the published earnings-volatility/QMJ-stability literature and the raw ratio will be dominated by near-zero-denominator outliers, so it should be winsorized or rank-transformed before the FMB slope is believed.
evidence: the raw ratio will be dominated by near-zero-denominator outliers

rationale: Since the 0/1 indicator dominates the [0,1] rank, the sort effectively becomes "negative-accrual firms long, all positive-accrual firms short," making this a repackaging of the Sloan accruals anomaly rather than a genuine profitability-quality interaction.
evidence: the sort effectively becomes "negative-accrual firms long, all positive-accrual firms short"

rationale: A rank-product of high profitability and low leverage is the textbook profitability-plus-safety composite (QMJ), offers no mechanism beyond its two well-documented components, and is trivially constructed.
evidence: the textbook profitability-plus-safety composite (QMJ)

rationale: The 0–5 profitable-year count both dwarfs the [0,1] ROA rank (so the signal is mostly a coarse loss-history screen, a known effect) and saturates at 5 for most surviving firms, plus the window length is ambiguous if the panel is monthly with annual data carried forward.
evidence: the signal is mostly a coarse loss-history screen, a known effect

rationale: Pairing Novy-Marx gross profitability with the durability of the gross margin itself is an economically motivated moat proxy on a distinct (revenue-side) channel from ROA-volatility variants, though its incremental content versus the Operating Profit Sharpe proposal must be checked and the five-year window will cost coverage.
evidence: the five-year window will cost coverage

rationale: The ROE–ROA wedge equals ib·(at−ceq)/(ceq·at), so it flips sign for loss-makers (rewarding highly levered unprofitable firms) and explodes for near-zero or negative book equity; absent those pathologies it reduces to roughly "ROA rank minus leverage rank," i.e., the additive twin of the Unlevered Profit Strength proposal.
evidence: it flips sign for loss-makers and explodes for near-zero or negative book equity

target_name: Operating Income Net Of Debt Service
rationale: In Compustat `oibdp` is definitionally `revt − cogs − xsga`, so this is the archive winner "Profit Net of Debt Service Burden" re-expressed with a winsorizer — a cosmetic variant whose only genuine content is a data-availability/outlier robustness check, not a new mechanism.
evidence: the archive winner "Profit Net of Debt Service Burden" re-expressed with a winsorizer

rationale: The stock-solvency framing (working-capital slack plus one year of profit against total liabilities) is a defensible economic alternative to the flow-coverage archive signal, though it is close in spirit to the classic Altman Z-score components and the unwinsorized `lt` denominator will blow up for low-liability firms, so the outlier control should be inside the ratio rather than absent.
evidence: the unwinsorized `lt` denominator will blow up for low-liability firms

rationale: The MIN-of-ranks conjunction is a genuinely non-additive combination that neither parent sort reproduces and the expected sign matches the construction, but both legs are individually published anomalies (gross/operating profitability and retained-earnings-to-assets à la Ball–Gerakos–Linnainmaa–Nikolaev), so the incremental content rests entirely on the nonlinearity and should be benchmarked against a simple average of the same two ranks.
evidence: should be benchmarked against a simple average of the same two ranks

rationale: The trend-difference moves the interaction from levels to dynamics and is internally consistent in sign and units, but the leverage-trend leg is a slow-moving proxy for the well-documented net debt issuance/financing anomaly, and the unstandardized subtraction implicitly assumes the two trends have comparable cross-sectional dispersion — worth testing, but the decomposition into each leg should be reported to show the interaction adds anything.
evidence: the decomposition into each leg should be reported to show the interaction adds anything

rationale: Operating profit minus the change in net working capital, both scaled by assets, is essentially the Sloan (1996) accrual adjustment and reproduces cash-based operating profitability (Ball et al. 2016); the reasoning's claim that it is "distinct from the signed accruals anomaly" is not supported by the expression, which is exactly earnings-less-working-capital-accruals.
evidence: is essentially the Sloan (1996) accrual adjustment

rationale: This applies a single mechanical demeaning transform to an already-evaluated archive signal without changing the mechanism, which is precisely the kind of cosmetic variant the objective warns against; industry adjustment is better folded in as a standard preprocessing choice tested alongside a substantively new construct than proposed as a standalone signal.
evidence: a single mechanical demeaning transform to an already-evaluated archive signal

target_name: Trough Cash Flow Versus Fixed Claims
rationale: This is a single-input substitution (oancf for oibdp) inside the archive's existing winning expression, i.e. a cosmetic variant of "Trough Profit Versus Fixed Claims" rather than a substantively different mechanism, and it additionally imports a well-known cash-flow-coverage/distress measure while cutting sample depth (oancf availability plus a 5-year window) on already-thin 12% coverage.
evidence: a cosmetic variant of "Trough Profit Versus Fixed Claims"

target_name: Profit Not Funded By New Debt
rationale: Economically coherent and dimensionally consistent, but it is essentially an unweighted sum of two separately published anomalies (operating profitability and net debt issuance/asset growth), both of which are heavily spanned by RMW and CMA, so any FF5 alpha is likely to be small — and the equal-weight subtraction of legs with very different cross-sectional dispersion means whichever leg dominates variance will drive the sort.
evidence: it is essentially an unweighted sum of two separately published anomalies

rationale: The two legs are not commensurable — oibdp/at has a standard deviation of roughly 0.1 while dlc/act is fat-tailed and can exceed 1 — so the difference is dominated by the penalty term and the signal degenerates into a rescaled short-term-debt-to-current-assets liquidity ratio (a standard Altman-style distress input) rather than the claimed profit-net-of-rollover construct.
evidence: the difference is dominated by the penalty term

rationale: In raw asset-scaled units re/at is far more dispersed and far more often deeply negative than oibdp/at, so the MIN will equal re/at for the large majority of firms and especially throughout the short leg — the signal collapses into the known retained-earnings-to-assets anomaly and the stated "binding constraint" conjunction is illusory, which is precisely why the earlier rank version was constructed that way.
evidence: the MIN will equal re/at for the large majority of firms

rationale: A genuinely different statistic (frequency rather than depth of fixed-claim coverage) with a scale-free level-vs-level comparison and a clear diagnostic contrast against the trough version, though the six-valued support will likely pile most firms at 5 and yield a coarse, unstable top-quintile composition that caps its portfolio power.
evidence: the six-valued support will likely pile most firms at 5

rationale: Isolating the short leg is a legitimate and underexplored move, but "distance above own five-year profit trough × liability intensity" is close to the earnings-instability × debt-burden penalty term already tested as Distress Charged Profitability (fmb 1.74, ls_talpha 1.49), and the expected negative sign puts the level-of-profitability component of the interaction in direct opposition to the well-documented profitability premium, so the leverage interaction must carry essentially all of the signal.
evidence: the leverage interaction must carry essentially all of the signal

rationale: Internally consistent (subtracting a negatively-signed erosion leg yields the stated positive sign) and it deliberately pairs the archive's strongest long-side and short-side channels on a common scale, though the erosion leg's near-zero FMB slope means the cross-sectional gain may be diluted even if the portfolio alpha improves.
evidence: the erosion leg's near-zero FMB slope means the cross-sectional gain may be diluted

rationale: A legitimate and cleanly specified decomposition test of whether the erosion signal's alpha requires multiplicative co-occurrence, but half the composite (interest+current debt over assets) is essentially a standard leverage/debt-burden sort, so a negative result would be hard to attribute and a positive one partly rediscovers leverage.
evidence: a negative result would be hard to attribute and a positive one partly rediscovers leverage

rationale: The bounded-rank weighting genuinely implements "profitability premium concentrated among healthy firms" and avoids the two-negatives pathology as claimed, but note the construction pushes healthy-yet-unprofitable firms into the extreme short leg while compressing distressed firms toward the middle, which is a real economic bet the hypothesis never defends.
evidence: pushes healthy-yet-unprofitable firms into the extreme short leg

rationale: The hypothesis claims to measure the rate creditors charge, but xint/lt divides interest by total liabilities including non-interest-bearing payables and accruals, so the leg is dominated by debt intensity rather than debt price — a hypothesis/expression mismatch that also makes this a lightly restandardized rerun of the already-weak Return Spread Over Borrowing Cost.
evidence: xint/lt divides interest by total liabilities including non-interest-bearing payables

rationale: Retained-earnings-scaled-by-claims plus profitability is a near-rediscovery of the Altman RE/TA distress component combined with the standard profitability premium, and the only differences from the archive's two already-failed retained-earnings constructs are the denominator (lt vs at) and MIN→ADD, which is too thin a variation to justify a slot.
evidence: near-rediscovery of the Altman RE/TA distress component

target_name: Industry Relative Profit Less Rollover Risk
rationale: This is a one-knob preprocessing variant of the current leader rather than a new mechanism, which borders on cosmetic, but industry demeaning of both legs is a genuinely informative test of whether the leader's spread is a static sector tilt, and the result would discipline all subsequent constructs.
evidence: a one-knob preprocessing variant of the current leader

rationale: Internally consistent and correctly scaled, but it is a mechanical third-leg stack of two archive legs — and the erosion leg's near-zero FMB slope (-0.15) makes it likely to dilute the leader's cross-sectional t-stat while adding little independent alpha, so the informational payoff is modest.
evidence: erosion leg's near-zero FMB slope (-0.15) makes it likely to dilute

rationale: A defensible re-shaping of the skewed erosion leg into a bounded conditioner, but the structure inherits a real sign pathology already latent in Health Weighted Profitability — multiplying a signed z-score by a positive rank weight means unprofitable firms are penalized *more* for having low erosion — so any result will be hard to interpret as evidence for the stated conditional mechanism.
evidence: multiplying a signed z-score by a positive rank weight means unprofitable firms are penalized more

rationale: This is only a denominator swap on one leg of the leader, but act→lt changes the leg's economic content from liquidity backing to maturity concentration and yields a diagnostic the archive genuinely cannot currently resolve, so it is a legitimate if narrow anatomy test.
evidence: only a denominator swap on one leg of the leader

target_name: Industry Profit Less Absolute Rollover Risk
rationale: The asymmetric demeaning is the correct and specific implication of the observed slope-up/alpha-down divergence between the two gen-3 parents, the expected sign matches the expression's natural direction, and the test cleanly separates which leg's cross-industry variation is priced versus nuisance.
evidence: the test cleanly separates which leg's cross-industry variation is priced versus nuisance

rationale: It opens a genuinely untested earnings-quality channel and is not a bare accruals sort, but (ib − oancf)/at is exactly the Sloan cash-flow accrual measure so part of any result will be the known accruals premium, and the signed-z-score × positive-rank construction again perversely rewards weak cash conversion among negative-coverage firms; oancf availability may also cut coverage.
evidence: signed-z-score × positive-rank construction again perversely rewards weak cash conversion

rationale: This is a pure smoothing-window knob on the existing leader with no new economic content — precisely the cosmetic parameter variant the objective warns against — and three-year averaging of annual accounting ratios is very likely to produce a near-collinear signal rather than a diagnostic about durability.

rationale: The stock-versus-flow complementarity is a reasonable refinement of the strongest gate and the MIN structure is defensible, but the flow leg is close to the already-tested cash-return gates and the COALESCE fallback to accrual profitability partly defeats the stated "not burning cash" interpretation.
evidence: the COALESCE fallback to accrual profitability partly defeats the stated "not burning cash" interpretation

rationale: A legitimate and cheap parsimony ablation of the R&D addback against a gate that shares no accounting-mismeasurement theme with it, though with xrd coalesced to zero for most firms the numerator difference is small and a null result is the most likely and least informative outcome.
evidence: with xrd coalesced to zero for most firms the numerator difference is small

rationale: The expression is internally coherent and matches the hypothesis, but changing a single gate leg from a one-year to a three-year average is a pure horizon tweak on the archive's winning signal with no new economic content, and the archive's earlier smoothing precedent (NormalizedIntangibleEarningsYield, 3.7% at t 3.77 vs 4.4% at t 4.12) already suggests averaging dilutes rather than sharpens this family.
evidence: "earlier smoothing precedent ... suggests averaging dilutes"

rationale: Charging depreciation against the flow leg is a defensible tightening of "not burning cash" and the oiadp fallback is genuinely the post-depreciation analogue, but the archive's earlier oancf−dp gate was the weakest of the cash-strength gates (t 1.38), so expected incremental gain over the winning veto is modest.
evidence: the archive's earlier oancf−dp gate was the weakest of the cash-strength gates

rationale: The MIN-of-three construction is consistent with the stated substitutes logic and each leg is individually validated, but the accrual leg (oiadp−oancf) is mechanically anti-correlated with the cash-generation leg (oancf/at), so the third hurdle is likely largely redundant and the test's main value is diagnostic rather than incremental alpha.
evidence: "mechanically anti-correlated with the cash-generation leg"

rationale: This is a substantive capital-structure-neutrality test of the dominant veto signal rather than a cosmetic variant, the expression matches the hypothesis, and the proposal correctly pre-identifies the one real confound (cash appears in both the EV denominator and the cash leg), which makes the outcome interpretable either way.
evidence: "cash appears in both the EV denominator and the cash leg"

rationale: The debt-change leg is sign-safe, well-scaled and addresses a genuine loophole (source of the cash stock), but it is close to the well-documented net-debt-issuance/external-financing anomaly and the archive's one prior test of this financing channel produced near-zero alpha, so the incremental prior is weak even though the isolation of the debt term from the dividend term is a fair follow-up.
evidence: it is close to the well-documented net-debt-issuance/external-financing anomaly

rationale: Book-to-market screened on cash holdings and cash generation is essentially the long-published Piotroski-style fundamental-strength screen within value stocks, and the archive has repeatedly shown B/M legs here yield strong FMB slopes with zero FF5 alpha because HML spans them, so the proposal is a rediscovery whose expected outcome the author already concedes is null.
evidence: "essentially the long-published Piotroski-style fundamental-strength screen"

rationale: The conditional structure (cash-flow-to-debt coverage only within the levered subsample) is economically coherent and internally consistent, but cash-flow-to-total-debt is a long-standing distress/quality ratio, the indicator pins all low-leverage firms at exactly zero in the middle of the sort, and ADD(dltt,dlc) can be near zero even when lt/at>0.6, so the ratio needs tighter winsorization or a minimum-debt screen to avoid outlier-driven tails.
evidence: the ratio needs tighter winsorization or a minimum-debt screen to avoid outlier-driven tails

rationale: Leverage times earnings volatility is a crude but direct restatement of the published distress-risk / naive-Merton default-probability anomaly (Campbell-Hilscher-Szilagyi, Ohlson-type scores) with no refinement beyond the multiplicative form, so it is a rediscovery rather than a new cross-theme mechanism.
evidence: direct restatement of the published distress-risk / naive-Merton default-probability anomaly

rationale: The signal is internally consistent (sign carried by the trend, magnitude scaled by a bounded leverage rank so low-leverage firms are correctly near-neutral) and the "value transfer from creditors' risk premium to equity" channel is a genuine interaction rather than a level effect, though it partially overlaps Piotroski-style ΔCFO improvement signals and the five-year TREND will cost coverage among younger firms.
evidence: the five-year TREND will cost coverage among younger firms

rationale: This is mechanically the same design as LeveredCashCoverage (binary distress switch times a cash-flow-to-assets quality metric) and amounts to profitability-within-distress, a well-documented interaction; worse, the ~65-75% of firms with re>0 collapse to an exact zero mass that will make the middle sort buckets degenerate and inflate apparent coverage.
evidence: mechanically the same design as LeveredCashCoverage

rationale: The expression contradicts the stated hypothesis: dividing cash yield by lct/act makes the signal *lowest* for high-cash-flow firms under tight liquidity, exactly the group the hypothesis says is most underpriced, and the sign behavior is perverse for negative-oancf firms (their score improves as liquidity pressure rises).
evidence: dividing cash yield by lct/act makes the signal lowest for high-cash-flow firms

rationale: Because the positive-oancf count is bounded, heavily clustered at 4-5 for most firms, and never negative, the product's cross-sectional variation is dominated by leverage itself, so the signal is effectively a long-leverage bet whose historical sign contradicts the expected positive slope, and the short leg mixes debt-free firms with chronic cash burners; demeaning the count or interacting ranks would be needed to isolate the intended interaction.
evidence: signal is effectively a long-leverage bet

rationale: The construction is internally consistent (coverage carries the sign, the [0,1] net-debt rank only scales magnitude and correctly neutralizes debt-free firms), though the base leg is close to the well-known cash-flow-to-total-liabilities/profitability predictor so the incremental content rests entirely on the leverage-conditioning interaction.
evidence: base leg is close to the well-known cash-flow-to-total-liabilities/profitability predictor

rationale: Sign logic is coherent and the trend-versus-level contrast with the prior signal is informative, but the improving-profitability leg is essentially a Piotroski/ΔROA-style known effect and the five-annual-observation TREND on a lt-scaled ratio will be noisy, making this a modest rather than distinctive test.
evidence: improving-profitability leg is essentially a Piotroski/ΔROA-style known effect

rationale: Because the pretax-loss leg is z-scored (signed) while gross profit is almost always positive, the expression's short leg is high-gross-profit, high-pretax-income firms — i.e. it bets against the best-quality firms and against the documented profitability premium, which contradicts the stated "profitability premium concentrated among loss firms" hypothesis and makes the positive expected sign doubtful.
evidence: short leg is high-gross-profit, high-pretax-income firms

rationale: Sign, scaling and neutrality for unlevered firms all line up with the hypothesis, but (dp − oancf)/at is dominated by operating cash flow to assets, so the signal risks being a repackaged cash-flow-profitability effect and overlaps heavily with proposal 1's dp-based family.
evidence: the signal risks being a repackaged cash-flow-profitability effect

rationale: This is a single-leg level ratio, not a cross-theme interaction, and it is close to a rediscovery of the cash-holdings (cash-to-assets) premium combined with operating cash flow, with the only novelty being cogs as the deflator — which also introduces small-denominator instability for low-COGS and financial firms.
evidence: close to a rediscovery of the cash-holdings (cash-to-assets) premium

rationale: The product of a strictly non-positive volatility leg and a mean-centered working-capital leg inverts the intended ordering: the highest (long) scores accrue to volatile-margin, working-capital-rich firms rather than to stable-margin deficit firms, so the expression does not implement the stated hypothesis.
evidence: product ... inverts the intended ordering

rationale: This is the archived GrossProfitAmongLossMakers with an affine rescaling of one leg (WINSOR level → ZSCORE), i.e., the same mechanism and same two inputs, so it is a near-rediscovery whose only novelty is portfolio re-centering rather than a substantively different economic hypothesis.
evidence: archived GrossProfitAmongLossMakers with an affine rescaling of one leg

rationale: Internally consistent and a genuine level→change shift in the quality channel, though the change-in-gross-margin leg overlaps heavily with the published Piotroski ΔMargin component (a signal already known to work in distressed/value subsets) and DELTA of a revenue-scaled margin is noisy for small-revenue loss makers.
evidence: change-in-gross-margin leg overlaps heavily with the published Piotroski ΔMargin component

rationale: Swapping the conditioner from bottom-line loss intensity to a funding-structure state is a defensible distinct test with better coverage, but because the non-negative rank weight leaves the product highly correlated with raw gross profitability, the main risk is exactly the RMW spanning that sank the gen-1 coverage signals.
evidence: the main risk is exactly the RMW spanning that sank the gen-1 coverage signals

rationale: The chronic-versus-transitory distress distinction is economically substantive, but the stated mechanism ("firms with no loss years are correctly neutralized") likely fails because RANK of a discrete 0–5 count assigns tied never-loss firms a mid-range, non-zero weight, so the expression does not compute the neutralization the hypothesis relies on.
evidence: RANK of a discrete 0–5 count assigns tied never-loss firms a mid-range weight

rationale: The conversion ratio oancf/(ib+dp) has a denominator that is near-zero or negative for precisely the distressed, levered firms of interest, so the sign of the "quality" leg flips uninterpretably and winsorizing at 1% cannot repair it; the residual content is also close to the published accrual/cash-flow-quality anomaly.
evidence: the sign of the "quality" leg flips uninterpretably

rationale: The expression, hypothesis, and negative expected sign are mutually consistent, and a cost-versus-revenue growth wedge conditioned on cash scarcity is a deterioration channel plausibly outside FF5 span and clearly distinct from the archived level-based coverage signals.
evidence: clearly distinct from the archived level-based coverage signals

rationale: A clean, internally consistent conditioner-swap ablation on the archive's best signal that separates the quality-leg centering from the choice of distress variable, though it is incremental and leans on gross profitability (a well-known anomaly) as the quality leg so the incremental content rests entirely on the net-debt interaction.
evidence: it is incremental and leans on gross profitability

rationale: The stated premise is false as written — net-of-cash leverage has never been shown to interact with *gross profit* in the archive (only with uncentered cash-earnings coverage, which failed) — so blending it into a composite weight before the single-conditioner version is tested is premature and mostly a rank-averaging variant of the existing winner.
evidence: blending it into a composite weight before the single-conditioner version is tested is premature

rationale: The MA-minus-current construction correctly signs in the hypothesized direction and is a defensible noise-reduction response to the alpha/FMB disagreement, but it is a measurement-smoothing variant of an archived signal whose base leg is close to the negated working-capital accrual (Sloan), so novelty rests narrowly on the leverage conditioning.
evidence: “a measurement-smoothing variant of an archived signal”

rationale: A legitimate and well-posed attribution test of whether the archive's largest alpha comes from the release leg or the net-debt weighting, though the release leg is essentially an inverse working-capital accrual measure and the NEG(che/at) conditioner has repeatedly underperformed in this archive.
evidence: the NEG(che/at) conditioner has repeatedly underperformed in this archive

rationale: Introduces a genuinely new distress dimension (short-term debt net of cash, i.e., maturity/rollover exposure) paired with a centered per-sales cash-earnings margin, so it is not a restatement of the failed gen-1 asset-scaled coverage family and the sign logic is coherent.
evidence: “Introduces a genuinely new distress dimension”

rationale: Industry-demeaning the quality leg is a substantively motivated attack on the RMW-spanning risk in the archive's best signal and yields a clean decomposition of alpha into sector-margin versus within-industry distress discrimination, but it remains a robustness variant rather than a new mechanism.
evidence: “it remains a robustness variant rather than a new mechanism”

rationale: This is essentially a mechanical average of two already-evaluated archive signals (GrossProfitUnderNetDebt and the working-capital-change legs) sharing the identical net-debt conditioner, and it also embeds an unresolved contradiction — a fall in wcap/at is treated here as a *good* internal cash release while gen-3's GrossProfitAfterLiquidityDeterioration used the same quantity as a *bad* distress conditioner — so a positive result would be uninterpretable.
evidence: “a mechanical average of two already-evaluated archive signals”

rationale: The quality leg is the canonical Sloan/cash-flow accrual anomaly, so novelty is limited, but the leverage-conditioned form is a legitimate and clearly stated attribution test for whether the archive's alpha is working-capital-specific or generic accrual mispricing; the revenue deflator remains a real tail risk for low-revenue firms despite the claim to the contrary.
evidence: The revenue deflator remains a real tail risk for low-revenue firms

rationale: Shifting the question from cash generation to cash *use* is a genuinely new economic angle in this archive and both legs are flows, though the debt-reduction leg overlaps the known net-debt-issuance anomaly and the claim that debt-adders "sit in the middle" is wrong (they sit at rank≈0, which zeroes the signal rather than centering it).
evidence: “they sit at rank≈0, which zeroes the signal”

rationale: This is a conditioner swap on a leg that already produced a near-zero slope (fmb_tstat 0.254) and a wrong-signed alpha, paired with the one conditioner in the archive that carries its own strong standalone effect, so a positive result would most likely just reflect the conditioner rather than cost discipline.
evidence: “a positive result would most likely just reflect the conditioner”

rationale: The within-firm liquidity-trough conditioner is a substantively different construct from the archive's cross-sectional level and one-year-change conditioners and directly addresses the industry-structure confound flagged in gen 3, though the distance-to-min variable is non-negative with a large mass point at zero, so tie-handling in RANK needs checking before interpreting the spread.
evidence: “non-negative with a large mass point at zero”

rationale: The level-versus-flow reformulation is a reasonable and untested liability-side mechanism, but it sits close to the published external-financing/debt-issuance anomaly, and the motivating inference — that the gen-3 negative alpha proves the short-debt *level* is priced as risk — is loose, since that signal's quality leg (cash-earnings margin) is an equally plausible culprit.
evidence: that signal's quality leg is an equally plausible culprit

rationale: The composite is internally consistent (both legs are increasing in "good") and the diagnosis — pairing the slope-carrying gross-profit leg with the alpha-carrying cash-backing leg under the best-performing own-history trough conditioner — is a defensible consolidation rather than a rank-average duplicate, though the accrual leg's flat archived slope (fmb −0.23) and revenue scaling raise a real risk of diluting the strong GrossProfitAtOwnLiquidityTrough result rather than improving it.
evidence: “accrual leg's flat archived slope ... and revenue scaling raise a real risk”

rationale: This is a single-operator crossing (IND_ZSCORE swapped into the archive's best-Sharpe signal) and therefore only mildly novel, but the two design choices were each independently validated on different conditioners and the industry-demeaning rationale for reducing RMW/industry loading is economically articulated, so it is a legitimate, cheap test rather than a rediscovery.
evidence: “therefore only mildly novel”

rationale: Decomposing gross-profit-to-assets into margin and turnover under the same working-capital-deficit conditioner is a genuine diagnostic that the archive has half-completed (turnover tested, margin not), and it is internally consistent — the caution is that per-sales margin is the historically weaker half of the profitability anomaly, so a null here would be informative but unsurprising.
evidence: “per-sales margin is the historically weaker half of the profitability anomaly”

rationale: Despite a technically valid observation about tie mass at distance-to-minimum, this is a one-operator reparameterization of the conditioner in GrossProfitAtOwnLiquidityTrough with identical economics and near-certainly high correlation to it — exactly the cosmetic variant the objective warns against.
evidence: “exactly the cosmetic variant the objective warns against”

rationale: The expression matches the hypothesis and the cost-flexibility channel is untested in this archive, but depreciation-to-sales is dominated by industry capital intensity (no industry neutralization) and the expected sign runs against the documented operating-leverage premium, so the test is worthwhile only if interpreted as a conditional-on-distress reversal rather than a clean new channel.
evidence: “expected sign runs against the documented operating-leverage premium”

rationale: The metric-disagreement diagnosis (swap the balance-sheet leverage conditioner for an income-statement chronic-loss state) is a substantive rather than cosmetic move and is not an archived pair, but the count conditioner zeroes out most firms and revenue-scaled accruals are noisy for loss makers, so expect concentrated, unstable portfolio extremes — and note this sits close to the published finding that the accrual anomaly is strongest among distressed firms.
evidence: the count conditioner zeroes out most firms

rationale: This is essentially the arithmetic blend of two already-archived signals (GrossProfitAfterLiquidityDeterioration and GrossProfitAtOwnLiquidityTrough) with an unchanged quality leg, so it is a cosmetic conditioner-averaging variant whose result is near-mechanically predictable from the two parents.
evidence: “a cosmetic conditioner-averaging variant”

rationale: Swapping gross profit for pre-depreciation cash earnings on assets is a genuine diagnostic about which profitability construct carries the trough-state mispricing, though ib+dp scaled by assets is close to standard ROA-in-distress territory and the result may prove highly correlated with the archived leader.
evidence: “close to standard ROA-in-distress territory”

rationale: The expression is a rank-average of two existing archive entries sharing the identical net-debt conditioner (GrossProfitUnderNetDebt and WorkingCapitalReleaseUnderNetDebt), with only a denominator change on the release leg, so it adds diversification arithmetic rather than a new economic mechanism.
evidence: “a rank-average of two existing archive entries”

rationale: Conditioning on the cash-stock flow rather than the level is a substantively new and internally consistent test that directly probes whether the archive's mechanism is specific to operating working capital, with the main risk being that cash drawdown proxies for investment/growth rather than funding stress.
evidence: “cash drawdown proxies for investment/growth rather than funding stress”

rationale: Reversing which leg carries the sign is a legitimate asymmetry test and the expected negative sign is consistent with the expression's construction, but the signed leg is close to the documented net-debt-issuance/asset-growth anomaly and its interaction with low profitability is already implicit in q-theory evidence.
evidence: the signed leg is close to the documented net-debt-issuance/asset-growth anomaly

rationale: Replacing total assets with assets-minus-cash in the archived winner's denominator is a trivially correlated rescaling of an existing signal, and the stated motivation is weakened by the fact that firms at their own working-capital trough are precisely the low-cash firms for whom the adjustment barely bites.
evidence: a trivially correlated rescaling of an existing signal

rationale: The conditioner is internally consistent (rising non-cash working capital = cash absorbed = stress) and the payables-netting is an economically motivated correction, but since (act−che−lct) is just wcap−che the signal will be highly correlated with the archived EarningPowerDuringNonCashCurrentAssetBloat, and the proposal must also explain the archive's unresolved sign tension with GrossProfitAfterLiquidityDeterioration (which treats *falling* wcap as stress) rather than merely noting it.
evidence: the signal will be highly correlated with the archived EarningPowerDuringNonCashCurrentAssetBloat

rationale: The MIN operator does implement a genuine conjunction rather than a blend and the joint-necessity claim is falsifiable, but both conditioners are wcap-derived and already individually successful (0.050 and 0.045 alpha), so the expected information gain is modest and the near-zero weight for most firms raises decile-composition/stability concerns that should be diagnosed if the alpha falls between the parents.
evidence: the near-zero weight for most firms raises decile-composition/stability concerns

rationale: A change-in-earning-power leg on the asset deflator conditioned on the own-history liquidity trough is a genuinely untested and economically distinct (timing rather than level) channel, with the caveat that a one-year gross-profit difference is a noisy, RMW-adjacent quantity whose alpha should be compared directly against the level-based parent to establish incremental value.
evidence: alpha should be compared directly against the level-based parent to establish incremental value

rationale: Conditioning on the cumulative internal-capital stock (retained earnings plus cash, an Altman channel) identifies a different constrained population than the archive's flow/one-year states and should raise coverage, though retained-earnings/assets is itself a mechanical accumulation of past profitability, so the test must confirm the interaction is not simply a nonlinear re-expression of the profitability leg.
evidence: confirm the interaction is not simply a nonlinear re-expression of the profitability leg

rationale: The "lender certification" reading is broken by the construction itself — DELTA((dltt−che)/at) rises just as much from a cash drawdown as from new term borrowing — and the positive expected sign contradicts the well-documented net-debt-issuance/external-financing anomaly, making this look like a data-driven re-run of the archive's already-observed sign reversal in NetLiabilityBuildInLowEarningPower rather than a clean test of a credit-supply mechanism.
evidence: rises just as much from a cash drawdown as from new term borrowing

rationale: This is a weighting-scheme variant of the archived GrossProfitUnderNegativeWorkingCapital (rank replaced by a hard indicator) rather than a new mechanism, and the resulting large mass of exact zeros makes the middle of the cross-sectional sort arbitrary, so any alpha difference will be difficult to attribute to the claimed "leakage removal" rather than to tie-breaking and coverage artifacts.
evidence: a weighting-scheme variant of the archived GrossProfitUnderNegativeWorkingCapital

rationale: The unsigned |ΔWC/at| conditioner is a genuinely new and diagnostically useful test of whether the archive's working-capital results reflect constraint intensity rather than direction, and the expression matches the hypothesis, though it should be interpreted cautiously since |Δ| loads heavily on small, volatile firms where gross profitability is already known to work best.
evidence: |Δ| loads heavily on small, volatile firms where gross profitability is already known to work best

rationale: Economically coherent and the two conditioners are genuinely distinct (internal-capital stock vs. liquidity flow), but multiplying two already-tested winning conditioners is close to stacking prior results, and the product of two [0,1] ranks compresses most mass toward zero so the effective spread will come from a narrow tail whose stability must be checked.
evidence: product of two [0,1] ranks compresses most mass toward zero

rationale: This is a cosmetic smoothing variant of the archived GrossProfitAtOwnLiquidityTrough (identical conditioner, three-year average of the same numerator), which the objective explicitly discourages, and gross-profitability levels are already known to be highly persistent so a 3-year MA will be ~0.95 correlated with the one-year print.
evidence: a cosmetic smoothing variant of the archived GrossProfitAtOwnLiquidityTrough

rationale: The conditioner is internally inconsistent with its stated distance-to-default story: because (dltt+dlc) can be near zero, small-loss firms with almost no debt receive the most extreme NEG(pi/debt) values and are ranked as the *most* default-proximate, so the sort will be driven by low-leverage micro-caps rather than by firms with creditors to fail.
evidence: small-loss firms with almost no debt receive the most extreme NEG(pi/debt) values

rationale: The depreciation-attribution question is legitimate and the expression matches the hypothesis, but the construct is close to a linear blend of two already-archived trough signals (gross profit at trough and depreciation intensity at trough), so its value is diagnostic rather than as a candidate final signal.
evidence: close to a linear blend of two already-archived trough signals

rationale: A persistent-instability conditioner is a reasonable complement to Signal 1 and is not a rediscovery of anything in the archive, but WC/at volatility is a strong proxy for size and idiosyncratic risk, so a positive result will need to be shown to be more than the well-known concentration of the profitability premium in small, volatile stocks.
evidence: WC/at volatility is a strong proxy for size and idiosyncratic risk

rationale: This is a single-operator variant (RANK→IND_RANK on the conditioner) of the already-evaluated EarningPowerUnderChronicLiquidityVolatility, and since IND_RANK preserves the same monotone non-negative weighting within industries it is far more likely to yield a cosmetic re-estimate than a distinct economic test.
evidence: a single-operator variant ... of the already-evaluated EarningPowerUnderChronicLiquidityVolatility

rationale: The expression is internally consistent and the conjunction of an income-statement and a balance-sheet conditioner has not been tested, but both conditioners are individually archived and the multiplicative rank weight makes it a fairly predictable hybrid of two known results (also note RANK(NEG(pi/at)) is a low-profitability ranking, not the "current pretax loss" the hypothesis asserts).
evidence: the multiplicative rank weight makes it a fairly predictable hybrid of two known results

rationale: A coherent and cleanly specified generalisation of the instability conditioner to an income-statement second moment, though it edges toward the well-documented result that profitability/quality premia are concentrated among high-earnings-volatility, high-limits-to-arbitrage firms, so a positive outcome would be only weakly novel.
evidence: a positive outcome would be only weakly novel

rationale: Internally consistent and the asset-scaled quality composite paired with the volatility conditioner is untested, but it is essentially a stack of two already-validated components (and the reasoning misstates the revenue-scaled composite as "failed" when it produced the archive's strongest FMB slope), so the marginal information is modest.
evidence: essentially a stack of two already-validated components

rationale: The most substantively new proposal in the batch: it relocates the uncertainty source from the balance-sheet residual to the sales process, which is a genuine discriminating test of whether working-capital volatility has merely been proxying for demand volatility, and the expression matches the hypothesis with the correct sign.
evidence: The most substantively new proposal in the batch

rationale: Multiplying the level and the five-year volatility of the same wcap/at variable — both already archived as conditioners and mechanically correlated through scale — is very likely to produce a signal statistically indistinguishable from the volatility-only version, making this an incremental recombination rather than a new mechanism.
evidence: very likely to produce a signal statistically indistinguishable from the volatility-only version

rationale: This is essentially the product of two heavily documented anomalies (net payout yield and profitability/gross-profitability), and because both legs are non-negative ranks the "interaction" is monotone in each argument, making it a near-linear composite of known factors rather than a state-dependent effect — and its low tail conflates "uninformative" cases with genuine sell signals.
evidence: “product of two heavily documented anomalies”

rationale: The soft cash-burn gate on gross issuance is a defensible refinement of the external-financing anomaly with sign and expression consistent, though the unranked, highly skewed raw issuance leg risks outlier domination and the cash-flow gate is partly a distress/profitability proxy that FF5 may absorb.
evidence: “highly skewed raw issuance leg risks outlier domination”

rationale: This is a direct rediscovery of the intersection of two canonical anomalies (Sloan accruals and share-issuance/composite-issuance), combined as a monotone rank product that adds no genuine conditioning beyond stacking two same-signed effects.
evidence: “direct rediscovery of the intersection of two canonical anomalies”

rationale: The signed strain score (leverage rank minus cash-flow rank) genuinely flips the interpretation of net debt flow across states and the expected negative sign is internally consistent for all four quadrants, with the main caveat that the signal collapses toward zero for mid-strain firms so extremes will drive the sort.
evidence: “signal collapses toward zero for mid-strain firms”

rationale: Conditioning buybacks on a multi-year cash-flow trend rather than a level is a reasonable and not-quite-standard refinement, but the mass of zero-repurchase firms creates a degenerate, tie-heavy low leg and the 5-year trend window will cost coverage, so the short side may be poorly identified.
evidence: “mass of zero-repurchase firms creates a degenerate, tie-heavy low leg”

rationale: Internally inconsistent: because both legs are non-negative ranks, dividend cuts by cash-rich and cash-poor firms both map near zero, so the expression cannot deliver the claimed sign flip for cuts and instead just reproduces a monotone dividend-increase × cash-conversion composite of known effects.
evidence: the expression cannot deliver the claimed sign flip for cuts

rationale: This is a one-knob temporal re-parameterization of the archive's CashBurnFundedExternalFinance (same issuance leg, identical cash-burn gate, only 3-year summing plus winsorizing), so it is a cosmetic variant of an already-evaluated signal and its base leg is the well-documented composite/net external financing anomaly.
evidence: “cosmetic variant of an already-evaluated signal”

rationale: The lifecycle (RE/AT) gate is a genuinely different, slower-moving conditioning variable than the archive's cash-flow gates and the sign logic is internally consistent, though both legs individually are well-trodden (issuance anomaly, RE/AT distress-lifecycle) so the incremental content rests entirely on the interaction.
evidence: “both legs individually are well-trodden”

rationale: The second-moment gate is an untried conditioning channel and the signed-leg/non-negative-gate construction is coherent with the stated hypothesis (stable firms shrink toward zero rather than flipping), but cash-flow volatility is strongly correlated with size and distress so the gate may end up proxying for those exposures rather than isolating "fragility amplification."
evidence: “may end up proxying for those exposures rather than isolating ‘fragility amplification’”

rationale: Measuring repurchases as a deviation from the firm's own five-year norm is a substantive fix for the degenerate zero-inflated leg that crippled ImprovingQualityRepurchaser, the gate direction matches the hypothesis, and the two-sided tails give a properly identified sort — main risks are the five-year history requirement eroding coverage and unwinsorized lumpy repurchase spikes.
evidence: “five-year history requirement eroding coverage and unwinsorized lumpy repurchase spikes”

rationale: The financing-mix (pecking-order violation) channel is a real departure from the archive's quantity-based signals, but the finding that the equity component of external financing predicts returns more negatively than the debt component is already established in the net-external-financing decomposition literature, and the expression does not actually condition on raising capital as the hypothesis claims (it relies on rank ties at zero to do so implicitly).
evidence: “already established in the net-external-financing decomposition literature”

rationale: Sign logic is internally consistent and the non-negative two-channel SUMRANK gate is a defensible diagnosis-driven fix for the collapsed signed gate in LeverageStrainedDebtIssuance, but the base leg is just the sign-flipped net debt issuance measure from that same archive entry, so the test is closer to a re-parameterization than a new channel and will likely be highly correlated with it.
evidence: “closer to a re-parameterization than a new channel”

rationale: The second term is verbatim the archive's CashBurnFundedExternalFinance and the first is PayoutCredibilityGate with RANK swapped for IND_ZSCORE, so this is a mechanical linear recombination of two already-tested signals rather than a new mechanism, and the well-behaved -2.8 t-stat leg will likely just be diluted by the weak payout leg.
evidence: “mechanical linear recombination of two already-tested signals”

rationale: The retrenchment (change-based) angle is a genuinely fresh cut on the payout theme and the cut-plus-cash-stress tail matches the negative expected sign, but the hypothesis's second clause is internally inconsistent — a dividend *increase* by a cash-poor firm produces a large negative signal value, which under a negative expected sign predicts outperformance, the opposite of the claimed "unsustainable bluff."
evidence: predicts outperformance, the opposite of the claimed "unsustainable bluff"

evidence: the outcome is largely predictable from the two archived legs

evidence: GROWTH of a three-year cumulative cash flow is ill-behaved when the base crosses zero

evidence: the low-short-term-debt leg is a repackaging of known distress/maturity-structure effects

evidence: MAX will also assign full fragility to cash-rich firms with merely short-dated debt

evidence: “adds little beyond proposal 1 beyond a cosmetic functional-form change”

evidence: cash-flow-statement line items are missing for a large share of firm-years

evidence: “VOL's 5-period window spans five fiscal years”

evidence: cash accumulation is mislabeled as an accrual build

evidence: “wcap includes cash and short-term debt”

evidence: “very close to the published enterprise-multiple anomaly”

rationale: The two "independent" quality legs — a five-year sign count of negative ΔNWC and the five-year trend in wcap/sale — are near-mechanical duplicates of the same underlying series, so the claimed character-versus-momentum distinction is not supported, and everything else is a copy of BalanceSheetConsistencyPlusDirection with a different anchor.
evidence: near-mechanical duplicates of the same underlying series

rationale: A self-admitted no-new-economics rank average of two archived signals that share identical quality inputs (WC-intensity trend and depreciation-intensity trend) and highly correlated anchors, so the diversification premise fails and any gain would be an averaging artifact rather than evidence for a mechanism.
evidence: no-new-economics rank average of two archived signals

rationale: This is a linear rank-sum of two separately published anomalies (book-to-market and Boudoukh–Michaely–Richardson–Roberts net payout yield) with no genuine interaction — the "intersection" story is not what SUMRANK computes, since a firm extreme on one leg alone lands in the tails.
evidence: “no genuine interaction — the ‘intersection’ story is not what SUMRANK computes”

rationale: Adding net repurchases to earnings in the numerator of a market-cap-scaled yield is arithmetically just E/P plus net-payout-yield, i.e. a known-anomaly sum rather than a cross-theme interaction, and the un-COALESCEd prstkc/sstk will silently drop firms that report neither (economically zero-flow firms), biasing coverage inconsistently with the sibling proposals.
evidence: “a known-anomaly sum rather than a cross-theme interaction”

rationale: The conditional construction is thoughtfully sign-aligned, but (i) the hypothesis says off-diagonal cells carry "no signal" while the expression actually assigns cheap-issuers a negative and rich-repurchasers a positive score, and (ii) buyback drift concentrated in high book-to-market firms is a long-published result (Ikenberry–Lakonishok–Vermaelen; Peyer–Vermaelen), so this is close to a rediscovery; the /at inside both INDICATORs is also redundant since only the sign matters.
evidence: “the expression actually assigns cheap-issuers a negative and rich-repurchasers a positive score”

rationale: Economically the most coherent pairing here (enterprise multiple with total net external financing), but both components are published anomalies (Loughran–Wellman; Bradshaw–Richardson–Sloan) and SUMRANK imposes no interaction whatsoever, so the test cannot distinguish the joint mechanism from the additive average of two known effects, while dltis/dltr sparsity will erode coverage.
evidence: “SUMRANK imposes no interaction whatsoever”

rationale: The persistence-of-financing-state dimension is a genuinely non-obvious refinement over one-shot issuance measures and the multiplicative form does concentrate the long leg in the cheap-and-committed corner, but the short leg degenerates into a large mass of exact zeros (all non-repurchasers plus all expensive firms), which risks unstable portfolio composition, and the 5-year TS_SUM plus un-COALESCEd prstkc/sstk will cut coverage materially.
evidence: “short leg degenerates into a large mass of exact zeros”

rationale: The expression's natural direction contradicts the stated story: because the P/B rank multiplies a signed issuance average, the extreme long leg is populated by high-multiple *repurchasers* (large negative product), not by value firms, so the tested spread is glamour-buyback versus glamour-dilution rather than the intended valuation-conditioned dilution effect — and the underlying net-issuance anomaly is already well documented (Pontiff–Woodgate, Daniel–Titman).
evidence: “extreme long leg is populated by high-multiple repurchasers”

rationale: Economically coherent and sign-consistent (the near-complementary indicators plus mirrored ranks reduce algebraically to ~1{net repurchaser} − RANK(ΔP/B), which still places contrarian repurchasers and post-run-up issuers in the correct diagonal corners), and conditioning on the *change* in the multiple rather than its level is a genuine departure from the gen-0 HML-clone designs — though the tester should verify the result is not simply annual return reversal interacted with the well-known net-issuance dummy.
evidence: “verify the result is not simply annual return reversal interacted with the well-known net-issuance dummy”

rationale: The within-firm valuation-rank conditioning is a legitimately novel and well-motivated way to strip the permanent value tilt, but the expression collapses to approximately TS_RANK(B/M) − 1{net issuer}, so roughly half the cross-sectional variation is a plain net-share-issuance dummy (a published anomaly) and the 5-observation TS_RANK is very coarse; the claimed "conditional" interaction is really additive.
evidence: the claimed "conditional" interaction is really additive

rationale: A clean, internally consistent pure interaction (sign driven by the buyback change, magnitude scaled by cheapness) that directly diagnoses why the archived level-based version had a flat slope, but it remains a one-input variant of that archived signal, and using market cap in both the valuation rank and the financing denominator risks a mechanical price-driven correlation.
evidence: it remains a one-input variant of that archived signal

rationale: Sign convention is correct (product is non-negative, high = expensive plus erratic issuance, expected negative) and financing second moments are unexplored here, but issuance volatility is strongly correlated with issuance level and with small young growth firms, so the test may largely rediscover the net-issuance/asset-growth anomaly interacted with size unless that overlap is controlled.
evidence: issuance volatility is strongly correlated with issuance level and with small young growth firms

evidence: coverage motivation does not justify the incoherent long/short asymmetry

rationale: Since RANK(P/B) ≈ 1 − RANK(B/M) and the two five-year counts nearly sum to five, the expression algebraically reduces to ~5·RANK(B/M) + (buyback years) − 5, so the claimed interaction cancels and the signal reintroduces a full-strength cross-sectional value main effect — precisely the HML exposure that produced the archived version's negative FF5 alpha — making this a mirrored restatement of SerialRepurchaser_Cheapness_Persistence rather than a substantive repair.
evidence: HML exposure that produced the archived version's negative FF5 alpha

rationale: This is essentially the archive's FinancingInformativeness_ScaledByCheapness with the continuous cheapness weight replaced by a hard median gate, and the underlying variable is the well-published net-share-issuance/buyback anomaly; the claim that the spread is "value-neutral by construction" is also overstated, since within the cheap half repurchasers still tilt to higher BM than issuers.
evidence: essentially the archive's FinancingInformativeness_ScaledByCheapness with the continuous cheapness weight replaced by a hard median gate

evidence: the stated motivation misreads the archive

rationale: Internally consistent, high-coverage, and the coverage-vs-economics diagnostic is a legitimate motivation, but the core predictor is the known liability/asset-growth anomaly and it overlaps substantially with the archive's IndustryCheap_NetCapitalReturn_Gate, so it should be judged as a robustness test rather than a new mechanism.
evidence: the core predictor is the known liability/asset-growth anomaly

rationale: The conditioning direction is genuinely reversed relative to everything in the archive, non-issuers are correctly parked at zero so the tails are cheap-vs-expensive issuers rather than issuers-vs-non-issuers, and expression, hypothesis and negative sign all line up — though negative-book-equity firms in the P/B ratio need care beyond 1% winsorization.
evidence: negative-book-equity firms in the P/B ratio need care beyond 1% winsorization

evidence: A size-subsample restriction of Signal 1 is a cosmetic variant
