evidence: ZSCORE of an IND_RANK centers the funding leg at the industry median

target_name: Allocation Shift From Research to Shareholders
rationale: The diagnosis (level ratio's large alpha with wrong-signed FMB slope is a maturity/factor-loading sort) is correct and within-firm demeaning is the right decisive test, though the archive's already-failed "Payout Accelerating as Research Decelerates" tests essentially the same change-based harvesting event and suggests the answer will be a null, and the MA-of-a-ratio-of-a-ratio construction is numerically fragile even after winsorization.
evidence: already-failed "Payout Accelerating as Research Decelerates" tests essentially the same

rationale: The claim that gross repayment is "mechanically unrelated to net financing" is false — dltr enters the archive's strongest signal with a negative sign, so this proposal predicts *low* returns for exactly the firms that signal marks as high-return, an unacknowledged sign contradiction; on top of that, dltr/R&D is dominated by leverage scale and debt-maturity structure rather than any crowding-out of the research budget.
evidence: dltr/R&D is dominated by leverage scale and debt-maturity structure

rationale: A legitimate external-validity test that escapes the R&D-reporter universe with a defensible alternative intangible-output proxy and a clean nonnegative weight, but it risks largely reloading on the well-known net share issuance anomaly conditioned by the equally well-known gross-margin-change signal, so the burden is on showing the interaction beats the additive combination of its two published parts.
evidence: burden is on showing the interaction beats the additive combination

target_name: New Claims Per Dollar of Total Intangible Capital
rationale: Changing the scaler from a flow to an intangible capital stock is a substantive rather than cosmetic revision and the coverage expansion to non-R&D intangible-heavy firms is a real test of mechanism generality, but for firms with small intan and zero-coalesced R&D the denominator can be near-zero, so the extreme deciles may be scaler noise rather than dilution — report results with and without a minimum-denominator screen.
evidence: the denominator can be near-zero

target_name: Issuance Into a Doubly Confirmed Research Decline
rationale: This is a mechanical rank-average of the two best already-tested conditioners bolted onto the identical net-issuance leg, so it adds no new economic content and its outcome is largely predictable as a blend of the two parent signals (both ~-2% alpha, t≈-2.5) rather than a test of a new mechanism.
evidence: mechanical rank-average of the two best already-tested conditioners

target_name: Issuance Against Lagged Research Payoff Decay
rationale: The lag has a defensible innovation-timing rationale, but it is a single-operator edit of the gen-2 signal that will push coverage below its already thin 0.042 (a 3-year trend of a 3-year MA lagged 2 years needs ~8 years of xrd history), and the conditioner remains dominated by the sales trend rather than by research productivity per se.
evidence: will push coverage below its already thin 0.042

target_name: Issuance by Firms Buying Innovation Instead of Building It
rationale: Build-versus-buy composition scaled by the firm's own research budget is a genuinely different conditioner from the archive's goodwill-level and intangible-growth tests, though it overlaps conceptually with the gen-0 equity-financed-intangible-expansion and gen-2 goodwill signals and still carries a large tied mass at zero for R&D firms with no goodwill activity.
evidence: still carries a large tied mass at zero

target_name: Issuance Against an Unmonetized Knowledge Stock
rationale: The conditioner is essentially the classic R&D-intensity (Lev–Sougiannis / Chan–Lakonishok–Sougiannis) anomaly with the sign reversed, and it directly contradicts the archive's strongest ratio result (financing per dollar of accumulated intangible capital, t=-4.3), which implies issuance is worst when the knowledge stock is *small*, a conflict the proposal never addresses.
evidence: directly contradicts the archive's strongest ratio result

target_name: Research Decay Priced Only Within Issuers
rationale: Replacing the continuous issuance leg with a participation gate is the correct decisive test of whether the intangible conditioner prices anything independent of the known net-issuance anomaly, and the centered conditioner keeps both extreme legs populated by issuers; the main risk is that the large zero mass of non-issuers bleeds into the extreme quintiles and dilutes the portfolio spread.
evidence: the large zero mass of non-issuers bleeds into the extreme quintiles

target_name: Issuance by Firms With an Erratic Research Commitment
rationale: Second-moment instability of the research program is a distinct economic object from the gen-1 financing-volatility test and is untried here, but VOL(xrd/sale) is strongly confounded with firm size, age and idiosyncratic volatility, so any result will need a check that it is not a repackaged vol/size effect.
evidence: strongly confounded with firm size, age and idiosyncratic volatility

rationale: This is a horizon rescaling of the gen-5 "Issuance by Firms Buying Innovation Instead of Building It" signal (same two legs, same conditioning logic, only 1-year windows swapped for 3-year sums), i.e. a parameter tweak rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the three-year issuance leg also drifts toward the well-documented composite share-issuance anomaly.
evidence: a horizon rescaling of the gen-5 signal

target_name: Proceeds Grew the Balance Sheet, Not the Research
rationale: Use-of-proceeds (asset growth outrunning R&D growth) is a genuinely new conditioning dimension in this archive and is internally consistent with the negative sign, but the conditioner is largely the asset-growth/investment anomaly interacted with the issuance anomaly — two known effects multiplied — and GROWTH(xrd,1) is very noisy for small or newly reported R&D, so any result will need to be shown incremental to CMA and to plain asset growth.
evidence: two known effects multiplied

target_name: Issuance by Firms Both Retreating From and Erratic in Research
rationale: The two conditioners being conjoined were already tested separately and produced nearly identical statistics (alpha -0.023/-0.020, t -2.54/-2.23, Sharpe -0.48/-0.47), which strongly suggests both are near-passive multipliers on a common issuance leg, so their product is an incremental recombination of evaluated material rather than an independent test, and it will mostly shrink effective breadth.
evidence: their product is an incremental recombination of evaluated material rather than an independent test

target_name: Issuing More Than Industry Peers While Research Retreats
rationale: Peer-benchmarking the financing leg is a defensible idea, but as constructed this is a one-operator normalization variant of the already-evaluated "Issuance While Research Has Retreated From Its Own Peak," and IND_ZSCORE destroys the economically meaningful zero point so that below-average issuers (including net repurchasers) in high-issuance industries receive negative scores and are placed in the long leg — a change the hypothesis never addresses.
evidence: IND_ZSCORE destroys the economically meaningful zero point

target_name: Cash Returned by an Improving Innovator
rationale: Algebraically this equals the gen-2 "Issuance Into Decaying Research Productivity" signal minus the raw net-issuance term (since RANK(NEG(x)) ≈ 1 − RANK(x)), so it is heavily collinear with already-evaluated content, and because the residual issuance term itself carries a negative slope the stated positive expected sign is not actually implied by the construction.
evidence: “heavily collinear with already-evaluated content”

target_name: Issuance by Firms With a Short Research Track Record
rationale: Reporting persistence is a conditioner dimension not yet tested and is a useful diagnostic on whether the family is driven by intermittent R&D reporters, but the leg is coarsely discrete (0–5 with heavy ties), likely proxies for firm age and size rather than credibility per se, and the claimed coverage gain is doubtful since TS_COUNT still requires a usable xrd history.
evidence: the leg is coarsely discrete (0–5 with heavy ties)

rationale: This is a mechanical rank-sum of two already-evaluated archive signals with no new economic content, and the weaker leg (buybacks-alongside-research, fmb 1.68, Sharpe 0.005) is likely to dilute rather than extend the spread, so it functions as metric-blending rather than a substantive refinement.
evidence: “mechanical rank-sum of two already-evaluated archive signals”

target_name: Net Cash Returned While Research Grows
rationale: The mechanism — research expansion funded internally by a net returner of capital — is essentially the archive's already-failed "Self-Funded Research Expansion" (fmb -0.50, wrong-signed alpha) with a continuous MIN replacing the indicator, making it an incremental variant of two evaluated signals rather than a new hypothesis.
evidence: “making it an incremental variant of two evaluated signals”

rationale: Explicitly a SUMRANK of two previously evaluated signals chosen because one scores well on FMB and the other on alpha; this is cosmetic metric-optimization on largely overlapping issuance-based information, not a new mechanism.
evidence: “cosmetic metric-optimization on largely overlapping issuance-based information”

target_name: Rescue Equity at a Retreating Research Firm
rationale: A coherent recombination in which the identified weakness (a static, largely industry-driven R&D-level conditioner) is replaced by a firm-relative research-retreat state, and the MIN(sstk, dltr) configuration remains genuinely invisible to net-flow measures — though it is still a recombination of two archived legs and risks simply re-averaging their spreads.
evidence: it is still a recombination of two archived legs and risks simply re-averaging their spreads

target_name: Issuance While the Equity Base Burns Away
rationale: The conditioner is mechanically entangled with the signal leg (net issuance is itself a component of DELTA(ceq)) and, once that is netted out, reduces to accumulated losses per research dollar — i.e. an issuance × profitability/burn interaction close to the archive's gross-margin-per-R&D version and to the well-known issuance and profitability anomalies FF5 already partly spans.
evidence: “conditioner is mechanically entangled with the signal leg”

target_name: Issuance by Firms Whose Intangible Base Was Purchased
rationale: Converting the build-versus-buy conditioner from a noisy annual flow into a bounded stock share of the firm's own intangible base is a substantively motivated fix to a diagnosed tied-mass and turnover problem, and the R&D-stock denominator makes it materially different from the archive's failed gdwl/at version, though it remains within the same mechanism family.
evidence: the R&D-stock denominator makes it materially different from the archive's failed gdwl/at version

target_name: Equity Raised While Dividends Are Maintained
rationale: This is a single-argument substitution (dltr→dvc) into the archived "Rescue Equity at a Retreating Research Firm" template with an identical conditioner, and because sstk is small for most firms (option exercises) MIN(sstk,dvc) will usually collapse to sstk within the dividend-payer subsample, making the signal largely a re-expression of the well-known equity-issuance anomaly conditioned on dividend status.
evidence: “MIN(sstk,dvc) will usually collapse to sstk”

rationale: The stated orthogonality claim is false — MIN(sstk,prstkc) is strongly correlated with the levels of both flows, not with their difference — and since the measure mechanically selects large, cash-rich repurchasers (a group associated with *positive* abnormal returns), the natural direction of the expression works against the negative expected sign.
evidence: MIN(sstk,prstkc) is strongly correlated with the levels of both flows, not with their difference

target_name: Rescue Equity at an Acquisition-Built Firm
rationale: A defensible diagnosis-driven recombination that pairs the archive's strongest portfolio configuration with its most cross-sectionally powerful conditioner, though the reasoning misattributes the archived rescue-equity conditioner (retreat-from-peak, not static R&D/sales) and the result may simply interpolate between two already-tested signals rather than add new information.
evidence: “reasoning misattributes the archived rescue-equity conditioner”

rationale: Replacing signed goodwill change with its absolute magnitude is a substantive, well-motivated construct change (impairment years join acquisition years in the short leg rather than the long leg) rather than a cosmetic tweak, but the gain over the archived signed-goodwill version is likely modest since large positive goodwill changes dominate the right tail either way.
evidence: “gain over the archived signed-goodwill version is likely modest”

target_name: Net Shareholder Funding Per Year of Research
rationale: This is essentially the archived "External Funding Intensity of the Research Program" (IND_RANK of net external financing over MA(xrd,3), fmb −4.09, alpha −1.7%) with the debt legs dropped and a Δxrd term added, so it is a re-scaling recombination of two existing archive members that will be highly collinear with both rather than a new mechanism.
evidence: “re-scaling recombination of two existing archive members”

target_name: Cash Returned Through a Sustained Research Build
rationale: Changing DELTA(xrd,1) to a three-year difference in the archived "Buybacks Alongside Research Expansion" is a horizon parameter tweak, not a substantively different mechanism, and it also mechanically raises the signal's exposure to firm size and growth persistence, which risks a spurious apparent improvement in the long leg.
evidence: “horizon parameter tweak, not a substantively different mechanism”

target_name: Raise Absorbed by Creditors and Dealmaking
rationale: The MIN cap is only binding for issuers, so the entire lower (long) tail collapses to net share repurchases scaled by assets — i.e., the published net-stock-issuance/payout anomaly with no intangible content — and the archive already contains a closely related dollar-scaled net-flow measure ("Shareholder Cash In Minus Research Dollars Added," fmb -4.25).
evidence: “entire lower tail collapses to net share repurchases scaled by assets”

target_name: Diverted Proceeds at a Retreating Research Firm
rationale: This is a near-duplicate of the already-evaluated "Rescue Equity at a Retreating Research Firm" (MIN(sstk,dltr) × identical retreat conditioner, alpha -3.3%, t -3.28) with |Δgdwl| bolted on, and the product of a two-sided financing leg with a non-negative rank amplifies both tails, so the long leg becomes big repurchasers *with* retreating research — the opposite of the stated economics.
evidence: “near-duplicate of the already-evaluated”

target_name: Issuance by Acquisitive Firms Currently Transacting
rationale: Both conditioners are already-evaluated goodwill measures built from the same variable with nearly identical statistics (alpha -2.0%/-2.3%, Sharpe -0.46/-0.50) attached to the identical net-issuance leg, so averaging their ranks is a cosmetic blend rather than a new mechanism.
evidence: “averaging their ranks is a cosmetic blend rather than a new mechanism”

target_name: Raise Shipped Straight Back Out to Claimholders
rationale: Adding dvc to dltr inside the MIN and swapping sstk for net issuance leaves this essentially the archived "Rescue Equity at a Retreating Research Firm," and because dvc is zero for most R&D-reporting firms the incremental economic content of the "dividend recipients" channel is negligible.
evidence: “incremental economic content of the ‘dividend recipients’ channel is negligible”

target_name: Net Cash Returned With Research Expanding
rationale: A single-operator change from the gen-6 signal, but the gross-versus-net payout distinction is economically meaningful and the archive's two bracketing results (alpha without slope, slope without alpha) give a genuine diagnostic reason to test the interpolation, though much of the incremental variation is the known net-issuance effect.
evidence: “much of the incremental variation is the known net-issuance effect”

target_name: Years of Research Bought With Paper
rationale: Well-constructed and internally consistent — the MIN isolates the jointly issued-and-capitalized dollar amount, the R&D-budget denominator is the scaling that produced the archive's strongest slopes, and winsorization plus IND_RANK controls the small-denominator blow-up — with the caveat that stock-financed-acquirer underperformance is itself a documented result, so the novelty rests on the R&D scaling.
evidence: stock-financed-acquirer underperformance is itself a documented result, so the novelty rests on the R&D scaling

rationale: An additive SUMRANK cannot "isolate the subset whose distress is an accounting artifact" as the hypothesis claims (a high score is achievable from either leg alone), and the second leg's expected direction — low retained-earnings/assets earning *higher* returns — contradicts the well-documented distress/RE-to-assets evidence, so the construct is both internally inconsistent and largely a repackaging of the known R&D-intensity premium.
evidence: a high score is achievable from either leg alone

rationale: The expression algebraically decomposes into (liabilities/assets) minus (5-year R&D stock/assets), i.e. a simple linear difference of two already-studied characteristics rather than an interaction, and netting an unrecorded *asset* against liabilities is the wrong balance-sheet adjustment (it should enter the denominator, as proposal 4 correctly does).
evidence: netting an unrecorded asset against liabilities is the wrong balance-sheet adjustment

rationale: The hypothesis is about *debt-service* capacity but the expression subtracts the entire debt *stock* from a one-year cash flow, a stock/flow mismatch in which the debt term dominates numerically, so the signal collapses into a conventional leverage-plus-cash-flow composite with the R&D add-back contributing a third-order tilt.
evidence: a stock/flow mismatch in which the debt term dominates numerically

rationale: This is the one genuinely interaction-by-construction proposal here — it is identically zero for non-R&D firms and largest where high book leverage coexists with a large off-balance-sheet knowledge stock — with a coherent mispricing story and outlier-robust rank differencing, though the tester should verify it is not simply a monotone proxy for R&D-to-assets by controlling for that ratio.
evidence: verify it is not simply a monotone proxy for R&D-to-assets

rationale: The unpledgeable-collateral conditioning of the known debt-issuance anomaly is an economically defensible refinement, but two construction flaws need fixing: COALESCE(xrd,0) leaves all non-R&D firms tied at a common non-zero rank rather than "switched off," and GROWTH of a leverage ratio explodes for firms with near-zero base debt.
evidence: COALESCE(xrd,0) leaves all non-R&D firms tied at a common non-zero rank

rationale: A sensible and internally consistent operationalization of R&D-adjusted profitability that concentrates on firms near the zero-earnings threshold, but it sits close to the published R&D-capitalization/adjusted-earnings literature and duplicates the rank-wedge machinery of the leverage proposal, so it should be judged on whether it adds incremental power beyond xrd/at and pi/at separately.
evidence: duplicates the rank-wedge machinery of the leverage proposal

rationale: The construction is internally consistent and does fix the dead short leg of the parent wedge, but because non-R&D firms are pinned near zero the signal is close to gross profitability (a well-known Novy-Marx anomaly) restricted to R&D firms, so any alpha must be shown to survive controlling for GP itself.
evidence: any alpha must be shown to survive controlling for GP itself

rationale: Sign, scaling (non-negative rank weight times signed industry-demeaned net leverage) and hypothesis all line up, and industry-demeaning plus collateral-scarcity weighting is a defensible, non-trivial refinement over the gen-0 level-based collateral ratio, though xrd/sale is fragile for near-zero-sales firms and the industry-relative leverage effect is partly documented.
evidence: xrd/sale is fragile for near-zero-sales firms

rationale: Mechanically broken long leg: for the majority of firms with xrd always zero, current-minus-five-year-max is exactly 0, which is above the cross-sectional mean and therefore a positive z-score, so the long portfolio fills with high-leverage non-R&D firms rather than the "credible pseudo-distressed innovators" the hypothesis describes.
evidence: the long portfolio fills with high-leverage non-R&D firms

rationale: This is the third rank-wedge in the same family and, like its siblings, the rank difference is near-monotone in R&D-stock-to-assets, so it largely re-expresses the already-tested R&D intensity tilt rather than isolating a distinct accumulated-equity-depletion channel; the authors' own framing concedes it is a near-sibling diagnostic.
evidence: it largely re-expresses the already-tested R&D intensity tilt

target_name: Internal Knowledge Versus Acquired Goodwill Under Debt
rationale: The internal-versus-acquired intangible composition angle is genuinely new relative to the archive, the expression is signed and centered consistently with the stated hypothesis, and the leverage-rank weighting is a real conditioning device — though the composition term is essentially a difference of two separately documented effects (R&D intensity positive, goodwill negative), so an incremental test against those components is warranted.
evidence: an incremental test against those components is warranted

target_name: Working Capital Coverage Of Research Commitment
rationale: Because xrd is an order of magnitude smaller than lct for nearly all firms, the expression collapses to (act−lct)/lct, i.e. the current ratio minus one — a classic liquidity/solvency screen — so the claimed R&D "interaction" is economically negligible and the signal is effectively a rediscovery of a standard ratio.
evidence: the claimed R&D "interaction" is economically negligible

rationale: This is a single-input swap (ib→oancf) on the archive's best existing signal and is largely mechanical rather than substantive, since R&D outlay is already embedded as an outflow inside oancf and the MAX(·,0) floor means that for the majority of cash-positive firms the expression collapses to plain 5-year R&D intensity — a well-known anomaly — so the "mechanism diagnostic" framing is weaker than claimed.
evidence: a single-input swap (ib→oancf) on the archive's best existing signal

rationale: The post-add-back MAX is a genuine nonlinearity rather than a relabeling of the archive's difference signal, the expected negative sign follows naturally from the expression, and it cleanly isolates residual (non-R&D-explained) equity destruction — though it will be heavily correlated with the standard cumulative-loss/distress anomaly and should be judged incremental to that.
evidence: should be judged incremental to that

rationale: Adding COALESCE(xad,0) to the archive's best signal is a cosmetic one-term variant whose economic content barely moves, because xad is reported by a small minority of Compustat firms and is small relative to xrd where both exist, so any change in results will be driven by a thin sliver of consumer-facing names rather than by the stated brand-capital mechanism.
evidence: a cosmetic one-term variant whose economic content barely moves

rationale: The construction is internally consistent (non-negative rank weight times signed, centered inverse-volatility, so non-R&D firms sit near neutral) and second-moment fragility is a genuinely untested leg in this archive, but the signal is close to a mechanical product of two separately documented effects (R&D intensity and earnings-volatility), so incremental power over each leg alone must be demonstrated.
evidence: incremental power over each leg alone must be demonstrated

target_name: Internal Knowledge Cover Per Liability Dollar
rationale: Recasting the goodwill-composition idea as a continuous ratio is a legitimate response to the rank×z-score form's weak FMB slope, but scaling by lt makes the signal substantially a low-leverage/high-R&D composite with an unstable denominator for cash-rich, debt-light firms, so the result may reflect the leverage denominator more than the internal-versus-acquired-intangible distinction it claims to isolate.
evidence: scaling by lt makes the signal substantially a low-leverage/high-R&D composite

rationale: It is a coherent, fully covered continuous benchmark for the wedge family with a sign that matches the expression's natural direction, but it double-counts realized losses (cumulative deficits already depress at and thus inflate lt/at) and is close enough to book leverage plus the accumulated-deficit distress anomaly that it needs to be evaluated against plain lt/at to show the intangible correction adds anything.
evidence: it double-counts realized losses

target_name: Knowledge Solvency Net Of Burn Per Claim
rationale: The construction is internally coherent and monotone in the intended direction (burn hurts through both numerator and denominator), but it is fundamentally a hybrid recombination of two already-evaluated archive signals rather than new economic content, so the marginal information is limited and largely diagnostic.
evidence: it is fundamentally a hybrid recombination of two already-evaluated archive signals rather than new economic content

rationale: This is a pure mechanical industry-demeaning of an already-evaluated archive signal with no change in economic content — a useful robustness check but not a distinct signal proposal, and the archive already contains an IND_ZSCORE variant of the leverage family.
evidence: a pure mechanical industry-demeaning of an already-evaluated archive signal

target_name: Knowledge Capitalized Five Year Earnings Record
rationale: TS_SUM(ib+xrd)/at is a near-linear combination of two long-published anomalies (cumulative profitability/earnings-to-assets and R&D-to-assets), and it is also a level-form restatement of the archive's "Expensing Induced Loss Illusion," so any positive result is uninterpretable as novel cross-theme evidence.
evidence: near-linear combination of two long-published anomalies

rationale: A one-year DELTA of a ratio whose numerator is a five-year sum reduces mostly to R&D-growth minus loss-change plus a large negative loading on asset growth, so the signal is confounded with two documented anomalies (R&D growth, asset growth) rather than isolating the claimed "revision in true solvency."
evidence: the signal is confounded with two documented anomalies rather than isolating the claimed revision in true solvency

rationale: This is the only proposal that introduces genuinely new economic content (research output rather than input), but the positive expected sign sits uneasily with the well-documented negative sales-growth/investment premium and the mixed R&D-plus-liabilities denominator can become very small for cash-rich debt-free firms, so the interpretation will hinge on whether the scaling truly flips the sign.
evidence: positive expected sign sits uneasily with the well-documented negative sales-growth/investment premium

target_name: Cash Tax Verified Return On Knowledge Capital
rationale: Internally inconsistent — txt is accrual-basis total tax expense, not cash taxes paid, so it does not deliver the "hard-to-fake" verification the hypothesis rests on, and cumulative tax expense over a capital base is in practice a rescaled profitability measure, i.e. a rediscovery of the profitability premium.
evidence: txt is accrual-basis total tax expense, not cash taxes paid

target_name: Ranked Internal Knowledge Cover Per Claim
rationale: This is a strictly monotone re-transform of the already-evaluated "Internal Knowledge Cover Per Liability Dollar" (identical quantile sorts, by the proposer's own admission), so it is a cosmetic variant that can only move the FMB slope and adds no new economic content.
evidence: strictly monotone re-transform of the already-evaluated

target_name: Liquid And Knowledge Buffer Per Claim
rationale: Adding cash to the non-goodwill resource base is a coherent and internally consistent economic modification of the cover-ratio family rather than a transform, though the added leg overlaps materially with the well-documented cash-holdings/liquidity return premium and the increment over the parent signal is modest.
evidence: added leg overlaps materially with the well-documented cash-holdings/liquidity return premium

target_name: Knowledge Share Of Total Economic Burden
rationale: The expression is monotone in R&D-stock/(liabilities + cumulative burn), i.e. a bounded rescaling of the knowledge-cover ratios already tested in the archive, so the "composition" framing is a distributional reparameterization rather than a new mechanism.
evidence: bounded rescaling of the knowledge-cover ratios already tested

target_name: Pre Research Cash Flow Cover Of Claims
rationale: The hypothesis (R&D as discretionary rather than committed) genuinely reverses the archive's post-research convention and the expression matches it, but the base term oancf/lt is essentially Ohlson's funds-from-operations-to-total-liabilities distress component, so much of any result will be a rediscovery of known distress/profitability pricing with an R&D add-back wrinkle.
evidence: much of any result will be a rediscovery of known distress/profitability pricing

target_name: Durable Research Floor Versus Rollover Need
rationale: With COALESCE(xrd,0) the five-year minimum is zero for the large majority of firm-years and is an order of magnitude smaller than dlc even for research firms, so the signal collapses to negative short-term-debt-to-assets — a known leverage/distress measure — and the claimed full coverage is a symptom of that degeneracy rather than a virtue.
evidence: the signal collapses to negative short-term-debt-to-assets — a known leverage/distress measure

target_name: Ranked Burn Adjusted Real Intangible Cover
rationale: Denominator and most of the numerator are identical to the already-evaluated "Knowledge Solvency Net Of Burn Per Claim," so once the rank transform is recognized as monotone the only genuine change is subtracting goodwill, making this an incremental variant dressed up as a consolidation test.
evidence: only genuine change is subtracting goodwill, making this an incremental variant

target_name: Funds From Operations Before Research Per Claim
rationale: This is the archive's "Pre Research Cash Flow Cover Of Claims" with a missing-data fallback bolted on, i.e., a coverage patch rather than a new economic mechanism — and substituting `ib` for `oancf` silently changes the construct being measured (net income vs. operating cash flow) in exactly the pre-1987 subsample the test is supposed to validate, so a "survives" result is uninterpretable.
evidence: archive's "Pre Research Cash Flow Cover Of Claims" with a missing-data fallback

target_name: Stock And Flow Knowledge Solvency Screen
rationale: The hypothesis is explicitly conjunctive ("passes both tests"), but SUMRANK is additive and lets a top score on one leg fully compensate for a bottom score on the other — the stated economics would require a MIN/double-sort construction — and as written it is an ensemble average of two already-evaluated archive signals rather than new content.
evidence: SUMRANK is additive and lets a top score on one leg fully compensate

target_name: Knowledge Solvency Against Risk Weighted Claims
rationale: Adding a dollar earnings-volatility term to the claim base is a genuinely new second-moment dimension in an archive of purely first-moment denominators and is economically motivated, though it remains a denominator refinement of an existing high-scoring signal and inherits that family's non-monotonicity when the numerator is negative (a larger denominator then *raises* the score), which should be checked before over-reading the slope.
evidence: a larger denominator then raises the score

target_name: Accrual Build Up Instead Of Research
rationale: This is a fixed-weight linear combination of two well-known published anomalies (Sloan accruals and R&D intensity), both of which already carry the expected negative sign, so a strong result is a rediscovery rather than an interaction — and worse, the `COALESCE(oancf, ib)` fallback makes the accrual term identically zero pre-1987, collapsing the signal to pure negative R&D intensity over a third of the sample.
evidence: fixed-weight linear combination of two well-known published anomalies

target_name: Three Year Research Versus Debt Build
rationale: A pure lookback-window change (5→3 years) on an already-evaluated archive signal is the definition of a cosmetic variant; the coverage gain is real but does not constitute a distinct economic hypothesis and should not consume a generation slot.
evidence: pure lookback-window change (5→3 years) on an already-evaluated archive signal

target_name: Acquired Intangible Share Of True Capital
rationale: The knowledge-stock term in the denominator is a second-order adjustment, so the signal is essentially goodwill-to-assets — a documented acquisition/intangible-composition anomaly — and with `COALESCE(gdwl, 0)` the majority of firms pile up at exactly zero, making the short leg a near-binary "has goodwill" screen rather than a cross-theme composition measure.
evidence: the signal is essentially goodwill-to-assets — a documented acquisition/intangible-composition anomaly

rationale: A three-year cumulation of the archive's already-tested one-year equity-issuance-net-of-R&D signal is essentially a lookback extension, and the three-year change in book equity net of retained earnings is very close to the published composite/net equity issuance anomaly, so the R&D subtraction is doing too little work to make this a distinct test.
evidence: very close to the published composite/net equity issuance anomaly

rationale: Equity issuance plus net debt issuance scaled by assets is the well-documented net external financing anomaly (Bradshaw–Richardson–Sloan), and since the archive already has both legs separately their sum with an R&D offset is more likely a rediscovery plus arithmetic than a new mechanism.
evidence: well-documented net external financing anomaly

target_name: Weakest Link Of Cover And Self Funding
rationale: The conjunction is internally consistent (the NEG correctly orients the financing leg so that high values mean self-funded and the positive sign follows), and joining a stock-cover test to a near-orthogonal flow-financing test via a no-compensation MIN is a substantive economic claim rather than a cosmetic blend, though it does inherit correlation with both parent signals.
evidence: does inherit correlation with both parent signals

target_name: Knowledge Cover Of Claims And Burn
rationale: The non-monotonicity diagnosis is legitimate and well-reasoned, but the resulting expression sits directly between two already-tested archive ratios (knowledge stock per liability dollar and knowledge-net-of-burn per claim), differing only by moving the burn term across the fraction bar, so it is likely to be highly collinear with existing results rather than decisive.
evidence: differing only by moving the burn term across the fraction bar

rationale: Excluding purchased intangibles while adding the unrecorded research stock is a coherent and genuinely new-to-the-archive pair of adjustments, but the resulting quantity is a tangible-plus-knowledge net worth ratio that overlaps materially with the existing knowledge-stock-net-of-debt and pledgeable-collateral signals, capping its expected incremental information.
evidence: the resulting quantity overlaps materially with the existing knowledge-stock-net-of-debt and pledgeable-collateral signals

target_name: Pre Research Earnings Over Risk Weighted Claims
rationale: This simply crosses an already-tested numerator (pre-research earnings over liabilities, embedded in the gen-5 MIN screen) with an already-tested denominator (risk-weighted claims), and any gain from the at·VOL(ib/at) term is hard to distinguish from the known earnings-volatility/low-volatility anomaly rather than the proposed liquidity-buffer channel.
evidence: any gain from the at·VOL(ib/at) term is hard to distinguish from the known earnings-volatility anomaly

rationale: The loss-year conditioning is a genuine tightening of the archive's best cross-sectional idea rather than a cosmetic re-scaling, but it creates a large mass point at exactly zero for consistently profitable firms, which collapses cross-sectional dispersion in the middle and makes the resulting spread essentially a within-loss-maker sort — worth testing, but the degenerate ranking should be diagnosed if results weaken.
evidence: creates a large mass point at exactly zero for consistently profitable firms

target_name: Risk Weighted Cover With Self Funding
rationale: This is a single-leg substitution inside an already-validated MIN structure whose two candidate cover legs (goodwill-netted knowledge cover and burn-adjusted risk-weighted cover) are constructed from largely the same numerator and both scale by liabilities, so it is a cosmetic variant of the champion rather than a substantively different mechanism.
evidence: a cosmetic variant of the champion rather than a substantively different mechanism

rationale: Stacking a third nested MIN on an already-tested two-way conjunction is incremental leg-permutation rather than a new economic mechanism, and because MIN of three ranks drives the extremes toward whichever leg is sparsest it predictably thins and destabilizes the tails — exactly the coverage/composition artifact the objective warns against.
evidence: MIN of three ranks drives the extremes toward whichever leg is sparsest

rationale: R&D-added-back earnings over an intangible-augmented capital base is a direct rediscovery of the published intangible-adjusted profitability/ROIC anomaly (and overlaps the archive's "Expensing Induced Loss Illusion"), and since profitability is an explicit FF5 factor the abnormal-alpha content is likely to be largely spanned.
evidence: a direct rediscovery of the published intangible-adjusted profitability/ROIC anomaly

rationale: The MAX "fails either test" structure is a coherent and correctly signed short-side counterpart to the validated MIN logic and combines two near-orthogonal fragility channels, though the issuance leg is close to the well-known net-equity-issuance anomaly, so the incremental content rests mainly on the goodwill-overhang term.
evidence: the issuance leg is close to the well-known net-equity-issuance anomaly

rationale: Substituting a full-coverage worst-year realization test for the financing leg is a legitimate ablation that isolates whether financing dependence is specifically necessary or whether any orthogonal second screen delivers the Sharpe gain, but it remains one more permutation of an already heavily explored conjunction family and should be the only such variant carried forward.
evidence: one more permutation of an already heavily explored conjunction family

rationale: This is essentially the arithmetic difference of two already-evaluated archive signals (the MIN conjunction with fmb 4.92 and the MAX disjunction with fmb −5.29), so a strong result is close to mechanically guaranteed by construction and teaches nothing new about the economics — it is a portfolio blend dressed as a hypothesis, and it re-uses the goodwill/knowledge-stock terms on both sides, partially cancelling them.
evidence: the arithmetic difference of two already-evaluated archive signals

rationale: Wrapping the archive's existing cover ratio (xrd5 − gdwl)/lt in TS_MIN is a one-operator cosmetic variant, and because the numerator is itself a five-year cumulative sum of a highly persistent quantity, the five-year minimum is close to a mechanically stale, four-year-lagged version of the parent rather than a genuine "durability" measure.
evidence: a one-operator cosmetic variant

rationale: A pure denominator swap (lt → dltt+dlc) on an existing archive ratio, and the swap introduces a construction problem the reasoning ignores: firms with near-zero financial debt produce explosive or undefined ratios whose cross-sectional ordering is essentially arbitrary, so any apparent gain would be a low-debt-firm artifact rather than evidence about claim definition.
evidence: firms with near-zero financial debt produce explosive or undefined ratios

rationale: With xrd coalesced to zero the signal collapses exactly to three-year liability growth scaled by assets for the large non-R&D majority, making it a direct rediscovery of the well-documented asset/liability-growth and net-operating-liabilities anomalies, and the R&D term is too small relative to Δlt to change the ranking for most firms.
evidence: a direct rediscovery of the well-documented asset/liability-growth and net-operating-liabilities anomalies

target_name: Worst Year Post Research Margin Cover
rationale: It is a crossing of two archive parents rather than a new mechanism, but the diagnostic question it poses — whether the worst-year effect comes from operating capacity or from write-down noise in the bottom line — is well-posed, the expression matches the hypothesis, and coverage should be full.
evidence: It is a crossing of two archive parents rather than a new mechanism

target_name: Fails Either Non Issuance Fragility Test
rationale: The stated robustness motivation is legitimate, but the replacement leg is the same liability-growth construct flagged above as a likely rediscovery of the asset-growth anomaly, so this would substitute one known published effect (net equity issuance) for another rather than establishing that the disjunction survives on genuinely cross-theme information.
evidence: rather than establishing that the disjunction survives on genuinely cross-theme information

target_name: Knowledge Share Of Risk Bearing Capital
rationale: This is essentially a denominator swap on the archive's already-strongest ratio ((xrd5−gdwl)/lt, alpha 6.4%, t 4.76), and the stated boundedness claim is only half true — the ratio is capped above at 1 but is unbounded below for goodwill-heavy firms, so the "cannot explode" motivation does not hold as written.
evidence: the ratio is capped above at 1 but is unbounded below

target_name: Funding Mix And Worst Year Conjunction
rationale: This is the fifth leg-substitution in the same MIN-conjunction family (financing, product-market, cover-level partners already tested) and it retains the champion's worst-year leg verbatim while swapping in a knowledge/debt share that duplicates proposal #1, so it is a permutation rather than a new mechanism.
evidence: it is a permutation rather than a new mechanism

rationale: Both numerator and denominator differ substantively from the earnings-volatility-weighted predecessor, and product-market/demand instability as the stress weight on the claim base is an economically distinct channel that the archive has never used, with a natural positive sign and full coverage.
evidence: product-market/demand instability as the stress weight on the claim base is an economically distinct channel

rationale: This is a mechanical MAX of two already-evaluated archive signals and merely swaps the goodwill leg out of the existing "Fails Either Fragility Test," so the cross-sectional slope will be inherited almost entirely from the issuance leg (fmb −5.20) rather than reflecting any new economics.
evidence: the cross-sectional slope will be inherited almost entirely from the issuance leg

rationale: Total liabilities are highly persistent, so TS_MAX(lt,5) ≈ lt for the large majority of firms and this is a near-collinear cosmetic rescaling of the archive's existing "Internal Knowledge Cover Per Liability Dollar" with the identical numerator.
evidence: a near-collinear cosmetic rescaling of the archive's existing

rationale: Another leg swap in the saturated MIN-conjunction family whose new leg (cash/current liabilities) is a plain, well-documented liquidity/cash-holdings measure, and the proposal itself concedes it is a robustness check rather than a new mechanism.
evidence: Another leg swap in the saturated MIN-conjunction family

rationale: This is an equal-weighted rank blend of two of the most heavily documented anomalies (Cooper-Gulen-Schill asset growth and Sloan/Richardson balance-sheet accruals) that are themselves strongly correlated and both largely spanned by the FF5 CMA factor, so it is a rediscovery/repackaging rather than a genuine interaction, and SUMRANK enforces additivity precisely where the hypothesis claims conditionality.
evidence: “a rediscovery/repackaging rather than a genuine interaction”

rationale: The composition idea (accounting growth per dollar of real investment) is reasonably fresh, but the construction is fragile — winsorizing the denominator at 1% still leaves near-zero and negative-accrual cases that make the ratio explode and flip sign non-monotonically, so cross-sectional ranks will be driven by low-capex firms rather than by growth composition; a bounded form (e.g., accruals minus capex, both scaled by assets, or a rank difference) would test the same economics far more cleanly.
evidence: “near-zero and negative-accrual cases that make the ratio explode”

rationale: The conditional design is internally consistent and is a legitimate sharpening test of whether the asset-growth effect concentrates in accrual-led expanders, but it creates a large mass point at exactly zero (all capex-dominated firms) that will dominate middle quantiles and make the long leg consist of accrual-dominated *shrinkers* rather than the "unpenalized" firms the hypothesis describes, and the use of oancf restricts coverage to post-1988.
evidence: “creates a large mass point at exactly zero”

rationale: Two defects: the growth rate of non-cash working capital is undefined/sign-flipping for the many firms with near-zero or negative working capital, and the positive expected sign requires the long leg to be high gross-PP&E-growth firms, which the well-established investment/CMA anomaly says underperform — so the stated sign fights the natural direction of the dominant leg.
evidence: “growth rate of non-cash working capital is undefined/sign-flipping”

rationale: The first leg is essentially the published inventory-growth anomaly (Thomas-Zhang, Belo-Lin), and the second leg is deliberately sign-flipped investment growth, so the composite goes long high-PP&E-growth firms in direct opposition to the documented investment effect — the two legs are likely to offset rather than reinforce, and the "capacity" conditioning would be better expressed as an interaction than as an additive rank sum.
evidence: “the two legs are likely to offset rather than reinforce”

rationale: Cumulating accruals over five years is close to a re-derivation of the net-operating-assets/balance-sheet-bloat anomaly (Hirshleifer et al.), and the negatively signed capex leg contradicts Fairfield-Whisenant-Yohn's finding that long-term operating-asset growth predicts returns with the same negative sign as accruals, so the differencing likely cancels signal instead of isolating composition.
evidence: “close to a re-derivation of the net-operating-assets/balance-sheet-bloat anomaly”

rationale: A legitimate single-input measurement swap (total cash-flow-based accruals vs. working-capital accruals) inside the archive's best-performing bounded-share architecture with correct sign and no scaling pathologies, but it is incremental rather than a new mechanism and overlaps substantially with the CashFlowStatementAccrualShare proposal in the same batch.
evidence: “it is incremental rather than a new mechanism”

rationale: (capx − dp)/ppegt is essentially the net investment rate in PP&E — a direct restatement of the published investment/asset-growth anomaly — and the "under-depreciation as accounting choice" story is unsupported since low dp relative to capx mostly reflects a young asset base, so this is a single trivial ratio rather than a cross-theme interaction.
evidence: “a direct restatement of the published investment/asset-growth anomaly”

rationale: The financing-state gate is economically coherent and sign-consistent, though it edges toward the published result that the accrual anomaly concentrates in external-financing firms, and the hard 5%-of-assets indicator leaves a large mass point at exactly zero that will make the sorted portfolio legs lumpy and composition-unstable.
evidence: hard 5%-of-assets indicator leaves a large mass point at exactly zero

rationale: Conditioning on the *direction* of investment intensity rather than its level is a genuinely different state variable from anything in the archive, the indicator's sign correctly matches the stated hypothesis, and the winsorized continuous accrual leg avoids a degenerate long side — the main risk is noise in Δ(capx/ppent) for asset-light firms.
evidence: “main risk is noise in Δ(capx/ppent) for asset-light firms”

rationale: The Compustat sign conventions work out correctly (NEG of recch+invch+apalch does recover ΔAR+ΔINV−ΔAP) and the Hribar–Collins motivation is the right diagnostic for whether the winning signal is about operating working capital, but it is a measurement refinement of an existing archive signal and cash-flow-statement items will materially cut coverage.
evidence: “it is a measurement refinement of an existing archive signal”

rationale: This is a plain additive rank blend of two already-known anomaly legs (investment growth and cash-flow/profitability growth) with no conditioning or interaction, so it rediscovers the standard investment-times-profitability combination and tells you nothing about the cross-theme mechanism the archive is probing.
evidence: “rediscovers the standard investment-times-profitability combination”

rationale: This is a three-year moving average of the archive's existing winner (TotalAccrualShareOfGrowthActivity) with numerator, denominator and bounding unchanged — a cosmetic smoothing variant whose denominator already contains a 3-year capex average, so the incremental information content is minimal and the "persistence vs. event" question could be answered more cleanly by a persistence indicator or by regressing on the lagged level.
evidence: “a cosmetic smoothing variant”

rationale: Reclassifying acquisition spending from the "real investment" side to the "accounting growth" side is a substantive, falsifiable economic claim about what counts as productive growth rather than a re-parameterization, and the ABS-and-smooth treatment of aqc sensibly guards against sign flips from divestitures — though the result will need care to separate a genuine composition effect from a straight rediscovery of the well-known acquirer-underperformance anomaly.
evidence: “separate a genuine composition effect from a straight rediscovery”

rationale: The expensing-discipline mechanism and the depreciation-flow normalizer are new to this archive and internally consistent (rising soft assets → signal toward +1 → predicted low returns, matching the negative sign), but the numerator is close to a re-derivation of published growth-in-net-operating-assets / soft-assets-ratio measures, so the marginal contribution rests entirely on whether the dp-based denominator adds anything beyond scaling by assets.
evidence: “close to a re-derivation of published growth-in-net-operating-assets”

rationale: Replacing the failed securities-issuance gate with an investment-funding shortfall is a defensible diagnosis-driven repair and the conditioning variable had the archive's strongest FMB slope, but the design is structurally identical to ExternallyFundedAccrualGrowth (winsorized accrual level × binary gate), so the same problem of gated-off firms piling at zero and diluting the tails may recur.
evidence: gated-off firms piling at zero and diluting the tails may recur

evidence: “capx+dp approaches zero for asset-light firms”

evidence: asset-growth gates have destroyed rather than sharpened signal here

evidence: “its value is diagnostic rather than novel”

evidence: “standard industry z-score wrapper applied to the archive's existing best signal”

evidence: the delta is mostly noise in a ratio whose denominator moves with the numerator

evidence: “well-documented published anomaly”

evidence: “economically negligible perturbation of an existing signal”

evidence: “DELTA(che) is dominated by financing and investing activity rather than liquidity buffering”

evidence: the non-negative, unbounded OCF-drawdown term is likely to dominate
