evidence: “the incremental content is modest”

rationale: This is essentially the sum of two well-known published anomalies — cash-based operating profitability (Ball et al.) and (ex-cash) asset growth / net-operating-asset growth (Cooper-Gulen-Schill, Hirshleifer et al.) — and stripping cash from at is a documented refinement, so it is unlikely to carry information beyond RMW/CMA rather than repairing the CMA-overlap problem it claims to fix.
evidence: “essentially the sum of two well-known published anomalies”

rationale: The marginal-productivity-of-capex mechanism is genuinely absent from the archive and the hypothesis matches the expression's direction, but scaling by capex means cross-sectional dispersion is dominated by the denominator, so low-capex firms will populate both tails and the signal risks degenerating into an earnings-change-times-inverse-capex-intensity composite that winsorizing at 1% will not fully discipline.
evidence: “cross-sectional dispersion is dominated by the denominator”

rationale: Persistence of sub-maintenance capex is a genuinely new state variable for this archive, the indicator/TS_SUM construction correctly implements the stated hypothesis with the right sign, and the additive SUMRANK form sensibly preserves the profitability main effect that the multiplicative gates destroyed — though the five-level count is coarse and the signal must be shown to beat a plain low-investment-plus-profitability composite.
evidence: must be shown to beat a plain low-investment-plus-profitability composite

rationale: oancf/oibdp is algebraically one minus accruals-scaled-by-earnings, so the first leg is a restatement of the accrual anomaly rather than a novel profitability-quality dimension, and the ratio is sign-unstable whenever oibdp is small or negative — a defect winsorizing cannot repair, since negative-earnings firms with positive cash flow are ranked as the worst converters.
evidence: oancf/oibdp is algebraically one minus accruals-scaled-by-earnings

rationale: This is a mechanical SUMRANK ensemble of two already-archived signals rather than a new economic mechanism, and it will teach little beyond what a correlation of the two existing return series would show — especially since one leg (realized return on recent capex) has an essentially zero cross-sectional slope, so any alpha gain is portfolio-averaging, not new information.
evidence: “mechanical SUMRANK ensemble of two already-archived signals”

rationale: Matching the profit-change horizon to a three-year cumulative capex denominator is a substantive, well-motivated repair of the parent ratio's small-denominator noise problem rather than a cosmetic reparameterization, though the tails will still be populated disproportionately by low-capex firms and winsorization alone may not fully fix that.
evidence: “tails will still be populated disproportionately by low-capex firms”

rationale: The mechanism is sensible and distinct from the archive, but the expression is internally flawed because Compustat `intan` already includes `gdwl`, so ADD(intan, gdwl) double-weights goodwill; additionally the acquired-intangible share is a slow-moving, near-monotone series whose five-year TS_RANK will be pinned near 1.0 for most acquirers, giving the second leg little cross-sectional variation.
evidence: `intan` already includes `gdwl`, so ADD(intan, gdwl) double-weights goodwill

rationale: Scaling capex by cash on hand is a genuinely different funding-constraint denominator that CMA/asset-growth do not span, and TS_RANK tames the near-zero-denominator explosion, but the second leg is close to an inverse own-history cash-level rank, so the sort risks becoming a cash-holdings-plus-profitability signal (a known premium) rather than the investment-discipline story claimed.
evidence: sort risks becoming a cash-holdings-plus-profitability signal (a known premium)

rationale: This is a near-duplicate of the archived ProfitUpCapexDecelerating — identical profitability-change gate, with only the second leg swapped from capex acceleration to a five-year capex-intensity rank — and it inherits the same multiplicative-gate pathology in which firms with low profit-improvement rank collapse toward zero regardless of investment state, muddying the intended long and short legs.
evidence: This is a near-duplicate of the archived ProfitUpCapexDecelerating

rationale: SG&A intensity is a genuinely untested profitability dimension in this archive that is not what RMW is built on, and the own-history construction is internally consistent with the hypothesis; the main risk is that both legs measure restraint with no profitability level, so the long leg may simply load on shrinking, low-growth firms rather than cash generators.
evidence: long leg may simply load on shrinking, low-growth firms rather than cash generators

rationale: Economically coherent and internally consistent, but it is the third permutation of the same TS_RANK(profitability) − TS_RANK(capx/ppent) template already tested twice in the archive (oibdp/at at 3.74 and sale/ppent at 4.19), so it is very likely to be a highly correlated rediscovery rather than new information about the mechanism.
evidence: third permutation of the same TS_RANK(profitability) − TS_RANK(capx/ppent) template

rationale: The absolute sub-maintenance threshold (capx < dp) is a genuinely different economic condition from the archive's relative-decline indicator, so this is a substantive recombination rather than a cosmetic one, though the capx/dp leg previously delivered essentially zero portfolio alpha and DELTA(capx/dp) is an outlier-prone tie-break term whose scale may swamp the profitability delta unless SUMRANK ranks each argument internally.
evidence: capx/dp leg previously delivered essentially zero portfolio alpha

rationale: This is a one-operator edit of the archive's SelfHistoryProfitCapexWedge and largely duplicates the question already answered by IndustryRelativeDeploymentMismatch (industry-adjusted deployment, fmb 3.45), so the diagnostic value is small relative to its near-certain high correlation with two existing entries.
evidence: one-operator edit of the archive's SelfHistoryProfitCapexWedge

rationale: The expression matches the hypothesis and the negative sign is correct, and since the two joint-event cells are not logical complements the decomposition genuinely tests long/short asymmetry in the archive's best signal, though the coarse 0–5 count with heavy mass at zero will produce unstable portfolio breakpoints on the short leg.
evidence: coarse 0–5 count with heavy mass at zero

rationale: Conditioning on discrete gross-PPE contraction events rather than a spending rate is a materially new investment measurement and pairs it with a profitability variable the archive has barely used, with the main risks being that outright capacity shrinkage overlaps the well-known asset-growth/CMA effect and that rare events plus a five-level count leave heavy ties.
evidence: capacity shrinkage overlaps the well-known asset-growth/CMA effect

rationale: Broadening the investment leg to fixed plus working capital is a real economic redefinition rather than a re-denomination, the accrual-free profitability leg is a sensible control, and the only caution is that oancf-minus-total-investment is close in spirit to a free-cash-flow/net-operating-asset construct, so a known-anomaly overlap check is warranted.
evidence: known-anomaly overlap check is warranted

rationale: This is an operator-only re-run of the archive's best signal (SelfHistoryProfitCapexWedge) on identical inputs, and the change is asymmetric in a way that likely hurts rather than helps — the long tail of MIN is nearly the same firms as the top of SUB, while the bottom tail now pools two economically opposite failures (low profitability vs. high capex), so the short leg becomes an uninterpretable mixture and the L-S spread is not a clean test of the "joint state" hypothesis.
evidence: bottom tail now pools two economically opposite failures

rationale: The diagnosis of why peak-distance failed on the slow-moving net PPE stock is honest and applying it to the capex flow is a legitimate magnitude-preserving alternative to TS_RANK, but capx/TS_MAX(capx,5) will pile a large mass exactly at 1.0 for any firm currently at its own spending peak (common under nominal growth), so the same clustering pathology may reappear in weaker form and the second leg remains highly correlated with the archive's TS_RANK capex term.
evidence: will pile a large mass exactly at 1.0

rationale: The second leg is essentially the published asset/PPE-growth anomaly and the first is a change-in-gross-profitability variable, and the identical construction (RANK of a one-year profitability change minus RANK of GROWTH(ppegt)) was already tested as ProductivityGainWithoutCapacityAdd and ContinuousProfitGatedCapacityGrowth, both of which delivered sign-wrong negative FF5 alphas — swapping the profitability numerator is a cosmetic change to a structure the archive has already rejected.
evidence: swapping the profitability numerator is a cosmetic change

rationale: The diagnosis that dividing by cumulative capex let small-denominator firms populate both tails is specific and correct, and separately ranking a three-year profitability gain against a three-year capex intensity scaled by beginning-of-period plant is a substantively different estimator of the same marginal-return mechanism rather than a relabeling, though the investment leg's overlap with the long-horizon investment/CMA factor should be checked in the FF5 alpha.
evidence: overlap with the long-horizon investment/CMA factor should be checked

rationale: Folding a profitability level into the overhead-efficiency leg is a genuine response to OverheadLeanNonDeployer's "both legs measure shrinkage" weakness, but taking TS_RANK of a cross-sectional SUMRANK muddles the interpretation (it now measures whether the firm's peer-relative efficiency is at a five-year high, not whether its efficiency is), and the second leg is byte-identical to the earlier signal, so a strong result will be hard to attribute to the new channel.
evidence: TS_RANK of a cross-sectional SUMRANK muddles the interpretation

rationale: The three-year step-down in capex intensity is a genuinely untested timing functional in this archive — distinct from levels, one-year deltas, trends, and own-history ranks — and pairing it with current profitability gives a coherent "post-build-out harvester" long leg, though the combination of profitability level plus falling investment sits close to a simple RMW×CMA repackaging and should be judged on whether the alpha survives FF5.
evidence: sits close to a simple RMW×CMA repackaging

rationale: This is essentially the arithmetic blend of two already-archived signals (SelfHistoryProfitCapexWedge, fmb 3.74, and UtilizationHarvestWedge, fmb 4.19) sharing an identical capx/ppent leg, so it is a combinatorial recombination rather than a new economic channel and will almost certainly land between its two parents.
evidence: arithmetic blend of two already-archived signals

rationale: Switching the joint indicator from year-over-year changes to deviations from a firm's own three-year norm genuinely converts a flip-count into a state-occupancy/duration measure, which is a defensible economic distinction from DivergenceEpisodeCount, though the overlap with that archived signal is large enough that the incremental information may be modest and highly correlated.
evidence: overlap with that archived signal is large enough that incremental information may be modest

rationale: The archive already contains this mechanism in both ratio form (ThreeYearMarginalReturnOnCapital) and rank-wedge form, and re-denominating the numerator to ΔROA and the denominator to capex-intensity is a scaling variant, not a new mechanism — and the near-zero-denominator explosion for low-capex firms (exactly the population the hypothesis wants to go long) is only partly contained by 1% winsorization.
evidence: re-denominating the numerator to ΔROA and the denominator to capex-intensity is a scaling variant

rationale: The balance-sheet-composition leg is genuinely the first non-flow investment measure in this archive and the trend-vs-trend architecture is validated, but note the mechanical hazard that a falling ppent/at share is largely driven by growth in non-PP&E assets — which the asset-growth anomaly says predicts *low* returns — so the second leg may fight the hypothesized sign.
evidence: falling ppent/at share is largely driven by growth in non-PP&E assets

rationale: A legitimate channel swap on the best-performing episode-count architecture, but the stated advantage is backwards — the shared ppent denominator induces mechanical coupling (a shrinking plant raises both legs), so the joint condition largely reduces to sales growth exceeding capex growth rather than a clean output-versus-investment divergence.
evidence: “the shared ppent denominator induces mechanical coupling”

rationale: The two raw deviations are in incommensurable units and dispersions (ROA deviations of a few percentage points versus capx/ppent deviations an order of magnitude larger), so the un-normalized subtraction will be dominated almost entirely by the capex leg and the signal is not the balanced wedge the hypothesis describes.
evidence: “un-normalized subtraction will be dominated almost entirely by the capex leg”

rationale: The diagnosis is technically correct — because SUMRANK ranks the raw wedge, the capex leg's larger dispersion does dominate the tie-break, so z-scoring is a real repair rather than a monotone relabeling — but this is nonetheless a recombination of the archive's two best entries whose outcome will likely land between them, and the supporting claim that the standardized wedge had "the highest Sharpe in the archive" is false (0.475 vs 0.482).
evidence: “a recombination of the archive's two best entries”

rationale: The argument that net investment (capx−dp) can be negative and therefore loses information under TS_RANK is a genuine measurement point that justifies the z-score form, though the stated premise is wrong — standardization did *not* improve the plain capex wedge (alpha 0.039→0.038, t 4.52→4.32, Sharpe 0.482→0.475) — and VOL of a near-zero net-investment ratio risks unstable denominators despite the winsorization.
evidence: “standardization did *not* improve the plain capex wedge”

rationale: Transplanting the duration-plus-intensity architecture to the working-capital channel is a substantive channel test rather than a re-denomination, the two legs are correctly free of a shared denominator, and the prior working-capital evidence is signed consistently in both directions; the main risks are inventory-driven coverage attrition in service industries and partial overlap with the known inventory-growth anomaly.
evidence: “inventory-driven coverage attrition in service industries”

rationale: "High profitability plus falling leverage" is very close to two of the nine Piotroski F-score components (ROA and ΔLEVER) and adjacent to the debt-issuance/net-external-financing anomaly; the within-firm standardization is a real distinction but not obviously enough of one to escape rediscovery, and the proposal does not address that overlap.
evidence: “very close to two of the nine Piotroski F-score components”

rationale: The two legs are not an interaction but two mechanically linked pieces of the same DuPont identity — ROA = margin × turnover, so TREND(oibdp/at) minus TREND(sale/ppent, inverted) largely reduces to a margin-trend signal and reproduces Fairfield–Yohn's margin-versus-turnover decomposition, while the "investment discipline" leg contains no investment flow at all.
evidence: “not an interaction but two mechanically linked pieces of the same DuPont identity”

rationale: This is a cosmetic re-scaling of GrossProfitPerInventoryDollarHarvest whose stated justification is self-refuting — it cites the margin wedge's Sharpe going "from 0.48 to 0.475," which is a deterioration, and the same holds for its alpha and t-stat — so the premise that standardization is an upgrade is not supported by the archive it cites.
evidence: “a cosmetic re-scaling of GrossProfitPerInventoryDollarHarvest”

rationale: This is a single-window parameter tweak (MA3→MA5) on the archive's leading HarvestStatePersistenceCount, and the five-year-norm deviation form has already been probed via StandardizedOwnHistoryHarvestWedge, making it a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism.
evidence: “a single-window parameter tweak”

rationale: Requiring simultaneous capex restraint and acquisition abstinence is a genuinely tighter policy definition than either archive parent (closing the capex-vs-M&A substitution loophole) and the indicator directions are internally consistent, though the triple-condition count risks mass concentration at zero and the incremental information over the two existing occupancy signals may be small.
evidence: “the triple-condition count risks mass concentration at zero”

rationale: Placing the archive's strongest cross-sectional investment measure (net-of-depreciation investment) inside the occupancy/duration architecture is a coherent and non-redundant combination with correctly signed indicators, and the own-norm framing sensibly avoids the absolute capx<dp threshold that failed twice, though it remains an incremental recombination of two already-validated components.
evidence: “an incremental recombination of two already-validated components”

rationale: Swapping the capex denominator from net plant to total assets is a one-parameter rescaling of the leading signal with no new economic content, and the stated coverage benefit is speculative since coverage is bound by the five-year history and profitability terms, not the capex denominator.
evidence: “a one-parameter rescaling of the leading signal with no new economic content”

rationale: The count leg is effectively persistent low equity issuance, which is close to a direct rediscovery of the well-documented share-issuance/net-external-financing anomaly, and the profitability gate plus capex tie-break may not be enough to establish that any measured alpha is incremental to that known effect.
evidence: “close to a direct rediscovery of the well-documented share-issuance”

rationale: As an ablation it has diagnostic value, but it is nearly the un-standardized MA3 twin of the already-evaluated StandardizedOwnHistoryHarvestWedge and SelfHistoryProfitCapexWedge, and subtracting two raw, differently-scaled ratio deviations without standardization means the high-variance capex/ppent leg will mechanically dominate the wedge.
evidence: “nearly the un-standardized MA3 twin of the already-evaluated”

rationale: This is the third interchange of the tie-break leg in an already-tested pairing (raw MA3 deviation in HarvestStatePersistenceCount, standardized deviation in OccupancyCountStandardizedTieBreak, now the TS_RANK wedge already tested standalone as SelfHistoryProfitCapexWedge), so it is a cosmetic recombination of two archived components that will be near-collinear with both and cannot diagnose anything new.
evidence: “a cosmetic recombination of two archived components”

rationale: Adding an absolute profitability floor is yet another indicator multiplied into the same occupancy count (structurally identical to DualRestraint/DryPowder), but the specific economic claim — that own-norm profitability admits distressed rebounders whose low capex is constraint rather than choice — is untested and falsifiable, with the acknowledged risk that a level gate pulls the long leg toward RMW.
evidence: a level gate pulls the long leg toward RMW

rationale: This is a genuinely new aggregator rather than a re-shuffling of archived legs — MIN of dimensionless proportional deviations enforces conjunction while preserving intensity and cannot be spoofed by the doubly-bad cell — though the unwinsorized capex/ppent-to-own-mean ratio leaves a real outlier tail on the short side that should be checked.
evidence: “leaves a real outlier tail on the short side”

rationale: The asymmetric-reference hypothesis (competitive advantage is relative, capital-allocation policy is firm-specific) is coherent and directly completes the question PeerRestraintOccupancy left open, but it is a single-indicator swap in a heavily reused template and the industry-relative profitability level is the leg most likely to be absorbed by FF5's RMW.
evidence: “industry-relative profitability level is the leg most likely to be absorbed by FF5's RMW”

rationale: Substituting operating cash flow for accrual EBITDA inside the occupancy architecture is a defensible and previously untested measurement choice with a clear economic rationale (harvestable surplus cannot be manufactured by accruals), though it is a one-input swap and the ~0.08–0.11 coverage typical of oancf entries risks an apparent improvement driven by sample selection.
evidence: coverage typical of oancf entries risks an apparent improvement driven by sample selection

rationale: Both legs are already in the archive (NetInvestmentBelowNormOccupancy for the count, NetDisinvestmentHarvestWedge for the TS_RANK wedge) so this is a cosmetic bolt-together, and the stated motivation misdescribes the prior signal's tie-break as volatility-scaled when it in fact used a raw MA3 deviation, undermining the claimed diagnosis.
evidence: “this is a cosmetic bolt-together”

rationale: This is essentially the well-documented earnings-volatility/earnings-stability anomaly repackaged as a profitability information ratio, and the construction is mechanically fragile because a negative mean ROA divided by a tiny volatility produces huge negative outliers while a loss-making but stable firm and a profitable but stable firm are scored on incomparable scales.
evidence: well-documented earnings-volatility/earnings-stability anomaly repackaged

rationale: This is a straight additive rank blend of two of the most heavily published anomalies (Novy-Marx operating profitability and Sloan total accruals) with no genuine conditioning or interaction, so it mostly rediscovers known effects rather than testing a new cross-theme mechanism.
evidence: straight additive rank blend of two of the most heavily published anomalies

rationale: The binary gate does not implement the stated hypothesis — instead of making profitability "not count" for fragile firms, it forces every firm failing the working-capital test to the absolute bottom of the score, so the short leg becomes a pure low-liquidity/distress portfolio and the signal is largely a solvency indicator wearing a profitability label.
evidence: it forces every firm failing the working-capital test to the absolute bottom

rationale: The economic story is reasonable but the multiplicative form on a signed, unbounded ROA is broken at the zero crossing — chronic loss-makers get a count of zero and therefore a score of exactly 0, ranking them above firms with mildly negative smoothed ROA and some profitable years, which inverts the intended ordering in the short leg.
evidence: multiplicative form on a signed, unbounded ROA is broken at the zero crossing

rationale: Both legs lean on known effects (profitability trend and retained-earnings-to-assets), but the pairing is a coherent and non-obvious validation mechanism, the rank aggregation keeps scales comparable and coverage broad, and the expected positive sign matches the expression's natural direction.
evidence: pairing is a coherent and non-obvious validation mechanism

target_name: Interest Adjusted Profit With Debt Coverage
rationale: The two-rank product is well-behaved and the interest-adjusted profit crossed with cash-flow debt coverage is a defensible cross-theme construct, though the reasoning's appeal to the "levered-ROE illusion" is inconsistent with an asset-scaled numerator and the second leg partially duplicates the profitability channel it is supposed to validate.
evidence: levered-ROE illusion is inconsistent with an asset-scaled numerator

rationale: A rank product of high operating profitability and low leverage is essentially the profitability-plus-safety core of the published Quality-Minus-Junk construction, so it rediscovers two well-known standalone anomalies with a trivial multiplicative wrapper rather than testing a new interaction.
evidence: core of the published Quality-Minus-Junk construction

target_name: Profits Not Propped By New Debt
rationale: Conditioning smoothed profitability on the *flow* of debt financing is a coherent and mechanically consistent interaction that goes beyond the level-based leverage gate, though the low-debt-growth leg alone overlaps heavily with the documented debt-issuance/financing anomaly, so the incremental content hinges on the interaction actually paying off.
evidence: low-debt-growth leg alone overlaps heavily with the documented debt-issuance/financing anomaly

rationale: The construction is internally consistent and well-scaled, but the stated motivation ("graded repair of the gen-0 binary solvency gate") refers to a signal not present in the archive, and the long leg's preference for high net working capital runs against the documented negative pricing of working-capital/net-operating-asset levels, which should be flagged as a sign risk rather than a fatal flaw.
evidence: preference for high net working capital runs against the documented negative pricing

rationale: This is a cosmetic variant of the archived "Improving Profits With Earned Capital" signal — same two ingredients with TREND swapped for its own level and SUMRANK swapped for MUL — and both legs (profitability, retained earnings/assets) are individually published anomalies, so it is an ablation dressed up as a new hypothesis.
evidence: cosmetic variant of the archived "Improving Profits With Earned Capital" signal

rationale: The proposal explicitly describes itself as Piotroski-style and combines exactly the F-score's profitability, Δleverage and Δliquidity components, making it a direct rediscovery of a long-published anomaly; the nested SUMRANK also silently double-weights profitability relative to the two change legs.
evidence: direct rediscovery of a long-published anomaly

rationale: The multiplicative operating-times-financial-leverage penalty is a genuinely distinct mechanism from single-dimension leverage conditioning and is monotone and bounded after ranking, but the expected sign puts the signal on a collision course with the documented positive operating-leverage premium (Novy-Marx), which should be treated as the key diagnostic if the slope comes out flat or wrong-signed.
evidence: expected sign puts the signal on a collision course with the documented positive operating-leverage premium

target_name: Profit Coverage Of Near Term Claims
rationale: A clean, well-motivated single-ratio ablation of the two winning composites, and the industry adjustment is justified since current-liability intensity is sector-driven, though EBITDA-to-current-liabilities is close to standard distress/coverage screens (Beaver-style cash-flow-to-debt) and unwinding the rank-product may simply reintroduce the outlier sensitivity that ranking was there to control.
evidence: EBITDA-to-current-liabilities is close to standard distress/coverage screens

rationale: Internally consistent and a legitimate complementarity-versus-redundancy test of the two independently successful legs with equalized weighting, but it is an incremental merge of two archive winners whose result is likely to sit mechanically between the parents, so its diagnostic value hinges entirely on the leg correlation being reported alongside the alpha.
evidence: it is an incremental merge of two archive winners

rationale: This is a cosmetic three-year-smoothing variant of the archive's best signal, and the archive already contains two cases where MA-smoothing the profitability leg (Profits Not Propped By New Debt, Stable Financing Durable Profits) collapsed alpha to roughly zero, so the prior on smoothing helping here is weak and the design choice has effectively been tested.
evidence: archive already contains two cases where MA-smoothing the profitability leg collapsed alpha

rationale: The stated mechanism is an externally priced implied borrowing rate, but xint/lt is dominated by the interest-bearing share of the liability stack rather than by the rate charged, so the expression largely recomputes the debt-mix channel already captured by dlc/lt while the hypothesis claims a distinct information source.
evidence: xint/lt is dominated by the interest-bearing share of the liability stack

rationale: The conjunctive logic is coherent and the control is clean, but MIN of two uniform ranks is very highly correlated with their product, so this is a near-cosmetic functional-form variant of the parent with little expected incremental information and added tie/compression problems in the extreme buckets.
evidence: near-cosmetic functional-form variant of the parent

rationale: The sales-benchmarked current-liability growth leg is the batch's only genuinely new flow mechanism and is economically sensible, but note the direction contradicts the working-capital accrual anomaly (rising current liabilities lower accruals, which Sloan associates with higher future returns) and lct growth is strongly correlated with total asset growth, so the test must control for both to be interpretable.
evidence: lct growth is strongly correlated with total asset growth

rationale: The stated distinction is spurious because oibdp is definitionally close to sale − cogs − xsga, so this is a near-tautological restatement of the archive's existing "Rollover Risk Adjusted Profitability" winner dressed up as a cleaner-profit hypothesis (and the numerator is itself the published Novy-Marx operating profitability factor).
evidence: near-tautological restatement of the archive's existing "Rollover Risk Adjusted Profitability" winner

rationale: Replacing dlc/lt with dlc/act is an economically substantive change (self-retirement capacity rather than claim composition) that unifies the two independently successful quality legs into one comparison, the sign convention is internally consistent, and inputs are dense — though it will be highly correlated with a plain current-ratio/liquidity screen and thus with the existing gen-2 composite.
evidence: highly correlated with a plain current-ratio/liquidity screen

rationale: The construction is a mechanical splice of two already-evaluated archive signals, and the counted condition (annual EBITDA exceeding total current liabilities) is a bar most firms never clear, so the five-year count risks being degenerate at zero for the bulk of the cross-section and mainly picking up asset-light industry membership rather than persistence.
evidence: mechanical splice of two already-evaluated archive signals

rationale: Double industry-neutralization of the winning rank-product is a legitimate and cheap conditioning-set test whose stated motivation (sector rather than firm selection driving the legs) is coherent, but it is a wrapper on an existing signal rather than a new mechanism, so its upside is limited to a robustness verdict.
evidence: a wrapper on an existing signal rather than a new mechanism

rationale: This is the batch's only genuine single-quantity interaction of the two themes — cash-flow variability scaled by near-term claims as a crude distance-to-distress — it is dimensionally coherent and sign-consistent, and it is distinct from the archive's failed capital-structure-volatility attempt, though it will partly overlap the known earnings-volatility anomaly.
evidence: it will partly overlap the known earnings-volatility anomaly

rationale: A first difference of the winning quality leg is a mechanical rather than conceptual innovation and overlaps known debt-maturity/net-debt-issuance anomalies, but the flow-versus-level question is cleanly posed, the sign is consistent, and a null result is genuinely informative for closing off flow variants.
evidence: a mechanical rather than conceptual innovation

target_name: Dual Profit Measure With Term Funding
rationale: This is essentially the average of two already-tested signals that share the identical NEG(dlc/lt) quality leg, so the expected gain is a rank-averaging smoothing artifact rather than new economic content, and the "complementary measurement error" story is asserted rather than tested.
evidence: essentially the average of two already-tested signals

rationale: The worst-case TS_MAX operator is a legitimate and sign-consistent reframing of the archive's best quality leg, but because dlc/lt is highly persistent the five-year maximum will be strongly collinear with the already-tested level, limiting incremental information.
evidence: five-year maximum will be strongly collinear with the already-tested level

rationale: Coherent and correctly signed consolidation of the two strongest archive quality legs, though the claim of near-orthogonality is overstated since both legs are built from current assets and current liabilities, and one leg is a coarse 0–5 count that will contribute mostly ties.
evidence: both legs are built from current assets and current liabilities

rationale: EBITDA-to-total-debt is a standard credit metric that is close to a rediscovery of the profitability-plus-low-leverage quality composite, and because both legs share oibdp in the numerator the "interaction" largely double-counts profitability rather than isolating debt capacity, with low- and zero-debt firms driving the extreme ranks even after winsorising.
evidence: the “interaction” largely double-counts profitability rather than isolating debt capacity

rationale: The re-scaling of EBITDA volatility to assets is a genuine diagnosis-driven fix of the archive's size-contaminated volatility leg, and the additive SUMRANK correctly implements the stated substitutability of stability and funding safety, though the result will sit close to conventional quality/low-earnings-volatility exposure.
evidence: the result will sit close to conventional quality/low-earnings-volatility exposure

rationale: The industry-neutralisation is a defensible targeted response to the margin signal's high-alpha/low-slope/low-Sharpe pathology, but simultaneously swapping the liquidity leg from dlc/lt to dlc/act makes it a three-way recombination of existing archive entries whose attribution will be ambiguous, and the archive already showed IND_RANK did not improve the asset-scaled version.
evidence: the archive already showed IND_RANK did not improve the asset-scaled version

rationale: This uses the identical three legs and identical inputs as the archived "Funding Pressure Adjusted Profitability" (fmb 3.12, alpha 4.0%) with only the aggregation operator swapped from SUMRANK to a rank product, which is a cosmetic re-specification rather than a substantively different mechanism, and rank products of correlated quality legs behave very similarly to rank sums in the extreme buckets.
evidence: only the aggregation operator swapped from SUMRANK to a rank product

rationale: The cash-based profitability leg is a well-known published anomaly (Ball et al. cash operating profitability) and the rollover-risk leg is already the archive's workhorse, so the contribution is a single-leg substitution rather than a new mechanism, but the substitution is economically motivated (claims are settled in cash, not accruals), internally consistent in sign, and the coverage risk is correctly identified as the key diagnostic.
evidence: the contribution is a single-leg substitution rather than a new mechanism

rationale: Because both legs share the sales denominator, the rank product is close to a monotone decomposition of oiadp/lct — i.e. essentially the already-tested "Profit Coverage Of Near Term Claims" (fmb 2.00, alpha 0.6%, negative Sharpe) — so the stated novelty of "dimensional consistency" is precisely what collapses it back onto a prior weak result.
evidence: essentially the already-tested “Profit Coverage Of Near Term Claims”

rationale: Scaling short-term debt by the illiquid (non-current) asset base is a genuinely distinct normalisation from the archive's dlc/lt and dlc/act, the maturity-mismatch mechanism is coherent and sign-consistent with the expression, and the main hazard (near-zero non-current assets for asset-light firms) is acknowledged and largely neutralised by the rank transform.
evidence: near-zero non-current assets for asset-light firms

rationale: Replacing the persistent profitability level with its one-year change is a legitimate and diagnostically informative test of whether the family is a static quality tilt or genuinely conditions news, though profitability changes are themselves a documented anomaly and the far lower autocorrelation of the flow leg makes a weakened alpha the likely outcome.
evidence: profitability changes are themselves a documented anomaly

rationale: The gate is internally inconsistent with its own hypothesis because dlc is already a component of lct, so act − (lct + dlc) double-counts short-term debt rather than measuring "liquid resources exceeding every near-term claim," and stripped of that framing it is a threshold tweak to the archived gen-4 "Profitability Plus Safe Firm Premium" specification.
evidence: act − (lct + dlc) double-counts short-term debt

target_name: Profit State And News Safely Funded
rationale: This is an average of two already-tested signals against the identical maturity leg — level×NEG(dlc/lt) (alpha 4.0%, t=3.55) and delta×NEG(dlc/lt) (alpha 3.3%, t=3.03) — so the expected result is mechanically bracketed by its two parents, and the outer RANK around SUMRANK is a redundant monotone wrapper; it is a cosmetic recombination rather than a new economic hypothesis.
evidence: a cosmetic recombination rather than a new economic hypothesis

rationale: An untested pairing of two archive legs whose diagnostic purpose (does the profit-change leg need maturity safety specifically or generic slack?) is legitimate and the expression matches the hypothesis, but it remains leg-swapping within a saturated family and both parents' alphas set a low ceiling on incremental information.
evidence: it remains leg-swapping within a saturated family

rationale: The stated coverage defence is incorrect — SUMRANK needs both inputs, so the sparse oancf leg (0.08 in the gen-0 test) will bind the whole signal's coverage rather than being cushioned by the dense maturity leg, and the likely outcome is the archive's best-performing leg diluted and its sample halved, which is uninterpretable as evidence about cash-based safety.
evidence: the sparse oancf leg (0.08 in the gen-0 test) will bind the whole signal's coverage

rationale: The construction is internally consistent and the argument that a ratio-change captures both numerator and denominator improvement is fair, but the two legs share oibdp so a large part of the product is a squared profitability term, and the deleveraging channel it adds resembles "Profits Not Propped By New Debt," which produced negative alpha.
evidence: a large part of the product is a squared profitability term

rationale: R&D intensity is a genuinely new channel for this archive and the funding-safety interaction is economically coherent, but xrd/sale is a long-published anomaly proxy, COALESCE-to-zero creates a large tied mass at the bottom of the rank, and R&D intensity is negatively correlated with contemporaneous oibdp/at so the SUMRANK may partly cancel the profitability leg it is meant to reinforce.
evidence: COALESCE-to-zero creates a large tied mass at the bottom of the rank

rationale: Unlike the rest of the batch this fuses the liquidity and debt legs into a single scale-free net-financial-position quantity rather than averaging ranks, giving it a distinct functional form and a monotone economic interpretation, though it is close to the standard net-debt construct and its incremental value over the existing NWC/lt leg (alpha 4.1%) is uncertain.
evidence: it is close to the standard net-debt construct

rationale: A clean, internally consistent measurement correction (since Compustat's oibdp is net of xrd via xsga, the add-back is arithmetically valid) that directly tests whether the gen-6 breakthrough is an expensing artefact rather than a two-anomaly blend, though it edges toward the well-documented intangible-adjusted-profitability literature.
evidence: it edges toward the well-documented intangible-adjusted-profitability literature

rationale: Economically coherent and diagnostically useful, but it is only a funding-leg swap between two legs already extensively tested in the archive, so it is a recombination rather than a new construct and its incremental information is limited to which quality dimension dominates.
evidence: it is only a funding-leg swap between two legs already extensively tested in the archive

rationale: Replacing the R&D flow with a five-year knowledge stock is a defensible and standard refinement (close to the known R&D-capital anomaly), but the stated justification is internally wrong — scaling the stock by `at` creates a shared denominator with the oibdp/at profitability leg rather than breaking one — and undepreciated cumulative spend mostly re-ranks the same firms as current intensity.
evidence: scaling the stock by `at` creates a shared denominator with the oibdp/at profitability leg

rationale: The test cannot discriminate what it claims, because xsga in Compustat generally subsumes xrd (so the SG&A leg partly reproduces the R&D leg mechanically) while simultaneously suffering the exact cancellation problem the author criticised in the parent — oibdp is computed net of xsga, so ranking profitability and SG&A intensity together offsets — and organisation-capital-from-SG&A is itself a published anomaly.
evidence: xsga in Compustat generally subsumes xrd

rationale: A legitimate and well-motivated sector-bet diagnostic for a leg known to be heavily industry-clustered, but it is a robustness variant of the parent rather than a new mechanism, and its main value is confirmatory rather than exploratory.
evidence: it is a robustness variant of the parent rather than a new mechanism

rationale: The intangible-adjusted return-on-financed-capital numerator is a genuinely new measurement construct, but the proposal changes three things at once relative to the breakthrough (R&D add-back, invested-capital denominator, and a swap of the funding leg from debt maturity to working capital), so any result will be uninterpretable as to which change drove it.
evidence: the proposal changes three things at once

rationale: This is the internally consistent capitalisation the expensing hypothesis actually implies (add-back in both numerator and capital base), it is not a duplicate of either the numerator-only or stock-as-separate-rank archive entries, and it usefully removes the mechanical tilt toward heavy spenders — though the reviewer should expect it to *weaken* results if the archive's gains came from that tilt rather than from productivity.
evidence: it is not a duplicate of either the numerator-only or stock-as-separate-rank archive entries

rationale: This is "Committed Research Programme Profits" with xrd added back to the profit leg, i.e. two already-tested, same-channel R&D proxies (add-back and continuity count) stacked on the same side of the composite, so it is a cosmetic recombination whose outcome is close to mechanically implied by the two parent results.
evidence: two already-tested, same-channel R&D proxies ... stacked on the same side of the composite

rationale: A five-year minimum of research intensity is a genuinely different statistic from the count or the cumulative stock and directly operationalises the "commitment" claim, but with COALESCE zero-filling the floor collapses to zero for any firm with a single gap year, so in practice the leg will be a heavily tied near-binary variable highly correlated with the already-tested TS_COUNT version.
evidence: the leg will be a heavily tied near-binary variable

target_name: Knowledge Stock And Safe Funding Only
rationale: As a deliberate ablation it is the right attribution test and is honestly framed, but on its own R&D-to-assets is a long-published anomaly, so a strong result would be substantially a rediscovery rather than a new cross-theme finding.
evidence: on its own R&D-to-assets is a long-published anomaly

rationale: A clean one-change test of whether the liquidity leg can be added to the maturity leg without collapsing the Fama-MacBeth slope, but it is close to "Funding Pressure Adjusted Profitability" with only the R&D add-back swapped in, so the incremental information over the two parents is modest.
evidence: it is close to "Funding Pressure Adjusted Profitability" with only the R&D add-back swapped in

rationale: The stated diagnosis — that the hard-claims leg's strong slope but weak alpha reflected a weak profitability partner — is testable and the substitution is a single controlled change, but the whole batch now consists largely of permutations around the same ~5% alpha family and the marginal payoff from further leg-swapping is diminishing.
evidence: the whole batch now consists largely of permutations around the same ~5% alpha family

rationale: A legitimate functional-form test (conjunctive triple product versus the archive's compensatory SUMRANK) with a clear diagnostic motivation, though it is a close relative of Knowledge Stock Backed Profits and the triple rank product compresses discrimination, so the likely outcome is a firmer slope at the cost of the R&D-driven alpha.
evidence: the triple rank product compresses discrimination

rationale: Because act is typically several times dlc, NEG((dlc-act)/lt) is numerically dominated by act/lt and is therefore close to the working-capital-to-liabilities leg already tested in Working Capital Backed Profitability and Net Liquid Position After Debt, so the stated "net rollover pressure" interpretation does not match what the expression actually ranks.
evidence: the stated "net rollover pressure" interpretation does not match what the expression actually ranks

rationale: The five-year R&D stock and the five-year minimum R&D/sales are both monotone functions of sustained research intensity and will rank firms very similarly, so nesting them mainly halves the effective weight on the profitability leg rather than adding a separable "continuity" dimension; the divergence in parent slope/alpha statistics is weak evidence of low correlation.
evidence: nesting them mainly halves the effective weight on the profitability leg

rationale: A clean one-change test on Self Financed Knowledge Capital with a coherent owner-financed-moat story, but xrd now enters both legs (current spend in the numerator, five-year sum in the quality leg), so part of the "interaction" is a mechanical R&D-squared term rather than a genuine profitability-times-safety conjunction.
evidence: part of the "interaction" is a mechanical R&D-squared term rather than a genuine profitability-times-safety conjunction

rationale: The stated repair does not follow from the expression: the tie mass at zero comes overwhelmingly from COALESCE-zeroed non-reporters, whose three-year minimum is still exactly zero, so shortening the window is a cosmetic parameter tweak on the best-alpha archive signal rather than a fix to the degeneracy it claims to address.
evidence: a cosmetic parameter tweak on the best-alpha archive signal rather than a fix

rationale: Structurally distinct from the archive's pure rank products — it preserves the profitability main effect and applies the conditional premium to knowledge capital rather than to profitability, which is a real content change over Profitability Plus Safe Firm Premium — with the caveat that all rollover-dependent firms tie at zero in the bonus channel.
evidence: all rollover-dependent firms tie at zero in the bonus channel

rationale: This is a direct rediscovery of the well-documented gross-profitability-plus-value composite (Novy-Marx 2013 combined with HML / Asness-Frazzini "quality at a reasonable price"), and multiplying two uniform [0,1] ranks is dominated by their average, so the claimed pure-interaction content is largely illusory.
evidence: This is a direct rediscovery of the well-documented gross-profitability-plus-value composite

rationale: The INDICATOR gate assigns roughly half the sample an exact value of zero, which is not "off" but is instead placed above every profitable firm with negative earnings yield — degenerate breakpoints and a ranking that contradicts the stated distress story.
evidence: assigns roughly half the sample an exact value of zero

rationale: Since rank(P/B) is monotonically the complement of rank(B/M), this difference of ranks is exactly an equal-weighted additive value+profitability composite, so the "disagreement measure, not a relabeled value or quality score" reasoning is internally false and the signal duplicates proposal 1.
evidence: the signal duplicates proposal 1

rationale: Conditioning value on the five-year slope of ROA rather than its level is a defensible value-trap-versus-recovery distinction that is not a standard published anomaly, though the rank-product form again behaves mostly additively and the slow-moving trend may dilute the effect.
evidence: rank-product form again behaves mostly additively

rationale: Gross-profits-to-enterprise-value is itself a published anomaly (Novy-Marx 2013), the raw unranked ratio will dominate the [0,1] margin-rank multiplier so the "interaction" is cosmetic, and negative or near-zero enterprise values will produce sign-flipping outliers.
evidence: Gross-profits-to-enterprise-value is itself a published anomaly

rationale: Internally consistent (product of two positively oriented ranks with a correctly negative expected sign) and usefully aimed at the short leg, but note that price-to-sales deflated by margin is approximately price-to-earnings, so it risks partially recovering the classic earnings-yield effect.
evidence: risks partially recovering the classic earnings-yield effect

rationale: The gated geometry is internally consistent and the liability-side profit-coverage leg is a genuine addition beyond RMW, but oibdp/(dltt+dlc+xint) has an unstable near-zero denominator for low-leverage firms that will likely dominate the z-score and needs explicit winsorization or a leverage floor, and the underlying idea sits close to the published distress/value-trap literature.
evidence: has an unstable near-zero denominator for low-leverage firms

rationale: (oancf − ib)/at is the negative of total accruals, so the signal is the Sloan (1996) accruals anomaly restricted to high book-to-market firms — a well-documented interaction (accruals are strongest in value/low-quality segments) rather than a new cross-theme mechanism.
evidence: the signal is the Sloan (1996) accruals anomaly

rationale: A one-year change in ROA applied inside a high book-to-market gate is essentially the ΔROA component of Piotroski's (2000) F-score strategy, which was published precisely as fundamental-signal screening within value stocks, so this is a rediscovery rather than a repair.
evidence: this is a rediscovery rather than a repair

rationale: The expression, gate direction, and positive expected sign are mutually consistent and the glamour-side mirror is a legitimate diagnostic that isolates where the value–profitability interaction is generated, though it is a symmetric variant of a Piotroski-style ΔROA screen and its incremental content over the cheap-side version may be thin.
evidence: it is a symmetric variant of a Piotroski-style ΔROA screen

rationale: Holding profitability high and letting log book-to-market generate the spread reduces the signal to the classic value effect on a profitable subsample — the proposal itself concedes it retains HML exposure, so it is near-guaranteed to be absorbed by FF5 and is too trivial a construction to be worth a slot.
evidence: reduces the signal to the classic value effect on a profitable subsample

rationale: This combines two well-published anomalies — intangible/R&D-adjusted book-to-market (Park; Eisfeldt-Kim-Papanikolaou) and gross profitability (Novy-Marx) — and the claim that the restated valuation leg cannot be absorbed by HML is unsupported since cumulative-R&D-adjusted B/M is very highly correlated with raw B/M for the large majority of firms where COALESCE sets R&D to zero.
evidence: cannot be absorbed by HML is unsupported

rationale: This is a cosmetic variant of the archived DeepValueTrapScreen — same gate-times-profitability geometry, same grading channel, with only a highly correlated cheapness proxy (EBITDA/P vs OCF/P) substituted and the threshold simultaneously moved from 0.7 to 0.6, so it neither isolates one design choice nor introduces a new economic mechanism.
evidence: This is a cosmetic variant of the archived DeepValueTrapScreen

rationale: Still the same template as the archived winner, but replacing equity-based cheapness with a strictly-positive enterprise-yield gate addresses a genuine confound (leverage) that all prior archive gates share, and the expression cleanly matches the stated hypothesis.
evidence: addresses a genuine confound (leverage) that all prior archive gates share

rationale: The level-vs-persistence question is worth asking, but every other archive use of INDICATOR takes a cross-sectional rank/quantile as its second argument, so INDICATOR(RATIO(oiadp,at), 0.02) is likely to be read as a ~2nd-percentile threshold and return 1 for nearly all firms, making TS_SUM a near-constant with almost no cross-sectional dispersion.
evidence: making TS_SUM a near-constant with almost no cross-sectional dispersion

rationale: Gating on sales-to-price and then sorting on operating margin selects almost exactly the high-earnings-yield firms, so the long leg is a rediscovery of the E/P anomaly dressed as a two-channel interaction, and the archive already found the closely related P/S-times-margin construction unproductive.
evidence: the long leg is a rediscovery of the E/P anomaly

rationale: The dividend-yield gate is a genuinely fresh valuation channel, but the grading term (oiadp − dvc)/at is numerically dominated by ROA since dvc/at is typically an order of magnitude smaller, so the expression does not actually measure payout coverage as the hypothesis claims and reduces to yield-gated profitability.
evidence: the expression does not actually measure payout coverage

rationale: Capital intensity of profits is a legitimately novel and plausibly FF5-orthogonal grading channel, but dp/oibdp flips sign whenever operating profit is negative — common among cheap value firms and far more than 2% of the gated sample — so NEG(WINSOR(...)) will systematically award top scores to loss-making firms, contradicting the stated mechanism.
evidence: will systematically award top scores to loss-making firms

rationale: A defensible orthogonal-leg fusion of the archive's two partial successes with a broader gross-profit-to-price gate, but it is fundamentally an additive recombination of already-tested components rather than a new mechanism, and SUMRANK of a coarse 0–5 persistence count with a continuous burden ratio risks the discrete leg dominating the composite ordering.
evidence: an additive recombination of already-tested components rather than a new mechanism

rationale: This is explicitly a single-operator construction variant of archived CheapWithLowCapitalConsumption (indicator swapped for continuous rank) with no new economic content, exactly the cosmetic re-parameterization the objective warns against.
evidence: single-operator construction variant of archived CheapWithLowCapitalConsumption

rationale: A well-diagnosed repair that puts the unstable leverage quantity in the numerator over a near-always-positive denominator, though "cheap plus low financial-distress burden" is close to the well-worn safe-value/Piotroski-leverage screen and only modestly extends the archive's burden-ratio family.
evidence: close to the well-worn safe-value/Piotroski-leverage screen

rationale: The net-cash-to-market-cap valuation channel is genuinely distinct from every book-, earnings-, and cash-flow-yield gate in the archive, and the profitability interaction is economically necessary rather than decorative since net-cash cheapness is dominated by cash-burning firms; the main risk is that the long leg concentrates in small, illiquid, cash-rich names.
evidence: the long leg concentrates in small, illiquid, cash-rich names

rationale: The diagnosis (strong alpha, flat slope) is honest and the added profitability leg is substantive rather than cosmetic, but averaging a second rank into the archive's best-alpha signal is as likely to dilute that alpha as to supply a slope, and payout-sustainability screens on high-yield stocks are close to established dividend-safety practice.
evidence: averaging a second rank into the archive's best-alpha signal is as likely to dilute that alpha

rationale: Value combined with R&D intensity is a direct rediscovery of the well-published R&D-to-market / intangible-adjusted-value anomaly (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis, Eisfeldt et al.), and the COALESCE-to-zero convention creates a large mass point so the signal effectively reduces to "cheap R&D reporters vs. everyone else."
evidence: a direct rediscovery of the well-published R&D-to-market / intangible-adjusted-value anomaly

rationale: Economically coherent and sign-consistent, but (GP−dp−xint)/GP is just 1 minus the sum of the two already-archived burden ratios inside the identical cheap gate, so it is closer to a re-parameterization than a new mechanism — and the claim that it is "free of sign flips" is wrong, since firms with negative gross profit get a large positive (good) score from the same deductions.
evidence: just 1 minus the sum of the two already-archived burden ratios

rationale: Treating dividends as a prior "claim" that destroys equity value is economically incoherent (dividends accrue to the equity holder, and the archived dividend result was conditional on a high-yield gate, not a generic burden), and the four-term aggregate is explicitly assembled by sign-fitting to in-sample archive t-stats rather than from a prior.
evidence: Treating dividends as a prior "claim" that destroys equity value is economically incoherent

rationale: Level-plus-flow of claims on gross profit is a defensible pairing with a correct diagnosis of why the gen-3 SUMRANK fusion failed, though it remains a recombination of two archived grading channels under the same gate and inherits their negative-gross-profit denominator instability.
evidence: it remains a recombination of two archived grading channels under the same gate

rationale: This is essentially gross-profit-to-price (Novy-Marx's valuation-ratio version of gross profitability) with depreciation and interest netted out — a known published value ratio, not a cross-theme interaction, and it abandons the interaction mandate entirely to test a single univariate yield.
evidence: a known published value ratio, not a cross-theme interaction

rationale: A genuine mechanism-location test that runs the validated burden channel in the opposite valuation state with an internally consistent expected sign and a construction directly comparable to the cheap-gate signals, so either outcome is informative about whether the effect is distress-specific.
evidence: A genuine mechanism-location test

rationale: Pairing the net-cash gate (strong FMB, weak alpha) with the capital-consumption channel (weak FMB, reliable alpha) is a sensible attempt to reconcile the two evidence types, but the grading leg is monotone-equivalent to an archived one, and the stated microcap fix is doubtful since dp/GP proxies asset intensity rather than cash burn and inverts for negative-gross-profit firms.
evidence: dp/GP proxies asset intensity rather than cash burn and inverts for negative-gross-profit firms

rationale: A coherent generalization of the archive's best flow signal into a net-payout-to-capital measure, but it is close to the known net-external-financing anomaly, it retains the negative-gross-profit denominator inversion the proposal set elsewhere admits is a defect, and it enters dvc with the opposite sign to the two archived dividend-gated signals without reconciling that tension.
evidence: it is close to the known net-external-financing anomaly

rationale: This is a pure horizon-tuning variant of CheapDeleveragingFromProfits — one operator argument changed — which is exactly the cosmetic re-parameterization the objective asks researchers to avoid, and its diagnostic value does not justify a full evaluation slot.
evidence: a pure horizon-tuning variant of CheapDeleveragingFromProfits

rationale: Value-gated net share issuance is a thin wrapper on the well-documented net-stock-issuance/composite-issuance anomaly, and the construction is mechanically flawed because raw DELTA(csho) is contaminated by splits and stock dividends and the gross-profit denominator flips sign for loss-making cheap firms.
evidence: raw DELTA(csho) is contaminated by splits and stock dividends

rationale: The denominator swap is motivated by a real and correctly diagnosed inversion in the gross-profit-scaled burden family, making it a legitimate robustness test rather than a cosmetic tweak, though the grading leg reduces to a fairly standard capital-intensity/leverage measure and the expected incremental insight is modest.
evidence: the expected incremental insight is modest

rationale: The stated mechanism is undermined by the arithmetic: raw operating earnings yield has an order of magnitude more cross-sectional dispersion than the effective borrowing rate, so the signal will be dominated by plain E/P — a canonical value anomaly — contradicting the claim that neither leg carries the signal, and zero-debt firms make the promised "full coverage" false.
evidence: the signal will be dominated by plain E/P — a canonical value anomaly

rationale: A sensible test of whether the dividend gate's reliable alphas come from payout safety or general earning power, and the revenue scaling avoids the negative-denominator problem, but the archived dividend-gated signals all show strong alphas with null Fama-MacBeth slopes, so this likely reinherits a gate-driven, grading-leg-independent result.
evidence: archived dividend-gated signals all show strong alphas with null Fama-MacBeth slopes

rationale: The conditioning leg is essentially the published net-external-financing / composite-issuance anomaly (Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan, Daniel-Titman) and, within this archive, a mechanical dollar sum of the two already-tested legs (CheapDeleveragingFromProfits and CheapSelfFundedEquityBase) that debt flows will numerically dominate, so it is closer to a repackaging than a new mechanism.
evidence: essentially the published net-external-financing / composite-issuance anomaly

rationale: This is a denominator swap on the immediately preceding proposal, and deflating the financing flow by market cap puts 1/price in both the gate and the signal, so any measured edge is partly a mechanical value/size repackaging rather than evidence about the financing channel.
evidence: any measured edge is partly a mechanical value/size repackaging rather than evidence about the financing channel

rationale: The timing-of-credit-repricing channel is a legitimate extension of the archive's cross-market idea, but DELTA(xint/debt) falls mechanically when debt is raised late in the fiscal year, so the computed quantity is heavily contaminated by debt issuance — the very thing the archive's deleveraging signal treats with the opposite sign.
evidence: DELTA(xint/debt) falls mechanically when debt is raised late in the fiscal year

rationale: A sign-flipped gate on the same construction as proposal 1, testing what is already well documented — that issuance and asset-growth/external-finance effects are concentrated in high-multiple firms — and it overlaps heavily with FF5's CMA and the share-issuance anomaly.
evidence: testing what is already well documented
