evidence: an incremental blend of two archive signals

rationale: This is the most economically distinct proposal in the batch — it tests whether the family's power comes from the level or the improvement of hidden-asset cash yield — though it closely re-runs the already-evaluated LaggedIntangiblePaybackProfit design with a different profit construct, and the three-year-stale conditioning weight will cost coverage and timeliness.
evidence: the three-year-stale conditioning weight will cost coverage and timeliness

rationale: The proposed "bounded share" weight is a near-monotone rescaling of the already-winsorized intangible-stock-to-assets weight used in StockWeightedPreInvestmentCash (t=3.64), so this is a cosmetic normalization variant unlikely to produce information the archive does not already contain.
evidence: a cosmetic normalization variant unlikely to produce information the archive does not already contain

rationale: Reframing the mechanism as cash conversion of gross profit is a genuinely different economic question from capital yield, but the deflator (revt − cogs) can be near zero or negative, which inverts the ratio's sign for exactly the distressed intangible-heavy firms the hypothesis cares about and is only partly mitigated by 1% winsorization.
evidence: the deflator (revt − cogs) can be near zero or negative, which inverts the ratio's sign

rationale: This is an incremental third-deflator extension of the archived DualDeflatorPreInvestmentYield that simultaneously swaps the conditioning weight from the current-flow to the installed-stock version, so any change in performance is unattributable, and it imports the gross-profit deflator without the positivity gate that the very next proposal argues is necessary (firms with negative revt−cogs get sign-inverted ranks), while the nested SUMRANK silently gives the asset deflator double the weight of the other two.
evidence: any change in performance is unattributable

rationale: A clean, single-dimension test that holds the deflator and the conditioning weight fixed at their best archived settings and varies only the profit construct, with an economically stated error-orthogonality rationale and a clear diagnostic payoff; the main reservation is that oancf and oibdp pre-investment yields are highly correlated in practice, so the incremental gain is likely modest and coverage will be capped by the cash-flow-statement item at ~0.09.
evidence: coverage will be capped by the cash-flow-statement item at ~0.09

rationale: A legitimate single-change variation of StockWeightedPreInvestmentCash that isolates the conditioning weight, but three years of SG&A will numerically dominate booked intangibles plus three years of R&D and advertising for most firms, so the weight will largely collapse onto the Eisfeldt–Papanikolaou organization-capital measure already tested in OrganizationCapitalValidated, making this closer to a reweighting of an existing result than a new mechanism.
evidence: the weight will largely collapse onto the Eisfeldt–Papanikolaou organization-capital measure

rationale: The minimum-over-five-years intensity weight is a genuinely new and economically motivated conditioning variable (commitment/durability rather than level or vintage) applied as the only change relative to PreInvestmentCashEarningPower, and it is distinct from the archived TroughPreInvestmentCashYield, which applied TS_MIN to the yield rather than the weight; note the weight mechanically re-enters the numerator through the R&D/advertising add-back, so a positive result should be checked against a version with the add-back removed.
evidence: the weight mechanically re-enters the numerator through the R&D/advertising add-back

rationale: The positivity gate is a real, correctly specified fix for a genuine sign-inversion defect in GrossProfitCashConversionIntangible rather than a cosmetic tweak, and zeroing gated firms leaves them near the middle of an industry-demeaned score; the simultaneous upgrade of the conditioning weight to the installed-stock version does confound the diagnosis slightly, so attribute any improvement cautiously.
evidence: the simultaneous upgrade of the conditioning weight to the installed-stock version does confound the diagnosis slightly

rationale: This stacks three untested-in-combination changes at once and is largely a superset of Proposals 1–3, so it can neither be attributed nor learned from — if it wins, the source of the gain is unknown, and if it loses, the redundancy among highly correlated pre-investment yield constructs is the likely but unverifiable cause; a consolidation candidate should be built only after the component tests report.
evidence: it can neither be attributed nor learned from

rationale: A legitimate one-dimension consolidation of two independently validated components (tri-deflator yield × broad hidden-capital weight), but it is a factorial recombination of archived pieces with limited new economic content, so it should be judged strictly on whether alpha exceeds the 6.3% incumbent rather than treated as a new mechanism.
evidence: a factorial recombination of archived pieces with limited new economic content

rationale: Internally consistent and cleanly controlled (only the weight changes), and the TS_MIN commitment floor has a real turnover-stability rationale distinct from a stock measure, but like Signal 1 it is another weight swap on the same yield blend and the two proposals largely compete for the same marginal information.
evidence: another weight swap on the same yield blend

rationale: A well-motivated breadth/robustness test that holds the mechanism fixed while replacing oancf with oibdp to lift coverage from ~0.089 to ~0.145, and it is genuinely informative either way since a comparable alpha rules out a cash-flow-statement-era artifact.
evidence: holds the mechanism fixed while replacing oancf with oibdp

rationale: This is the single most valuable proposal here because it is a clean ablation of the mechanical numerator-weight correlation that plausibly inflates the entire archive family, though reviewers should note that the stripped-down version is close to cash-based operating profitability interacted with R&D intensity, both well-documented, so a "modest drop" result still leaves a rediscovery question.
evidence: clean ablation of the mechanical numerator-weight correlation

rationale: Multiplying by a 0/1 indicator collapses the interaction into a plain cash-profitability sort on an intangible-intensity subsample with all other firms pinned at exactly zero (a design that already failed in the archive as ReturnOnIntangibleCapital, fmb 0.32), so the "conditional" structure is nominal and the surviving content is the known cash-based operating profitability anomaly.
evidence: Multiplying by a 0/1 indicator collapses the interaction into a plain cash-profitability sort

rationale: The algebra does what the hypothesis claims — raw minus industry-adjusted intensity recovers an industry-constant weight — making this a genuinely diagnostic decomposition of firm-level versus sector-level mismeasurement, with the caveat that the whole construction hinges on IND_ADJ being exact industry demeaning and that an industry-constant multiplier applied to an already industry-z-scored yield produces an unhedged sector-amplitude tilt whose FF5 alpha must be interpreted accordingly.
evidence: an unhedged sector-amplitude tilt whose FF5 alpha must be interpreted accordingly

rationale: The IND_ADJ construction correctly yields the industry-mean broad hidden-capital weight as the hypothesis claims, but because that weight is constant within industry the signal reduces to industry-scaled cash profitability — a mechanical splice of the two best archive weights whose alpha may simply reflect an unhedged sector-amplitude tilt on a known profitability anomaly.
evidence: alpha may simply reflect an unhedged sector-amplitude tilt on a known profitability anomaly

rationale: Multiplying the archive's firm-level intensity weight by the archive's industry-mean intensity weight is a cosmetic recombination of two already-evaluated variants with no new economic content, and the product compounds the fat tails of both (the "complementarity vs. redundancy" framing is a curve-fitting rationale, not a hypothesis).
evidence: a cosmetic recombination of two already-evaluated variants with no new economic content

rationale: This is the one proposal that genuinely discriminates between the firm-mispricing and sector-tilt interpretations of the leading result, the positive-part gate is correctly implemented so no sign flip occurs, and its only weakness is the unwinsorized excess-intensity tail and the loss of effective breadth from zero-weighting half the panel.
evidence: unwinsorized excess-intensity tail and the loss of effective breadth from zero-weighting half the panel

rationale: The diagnosis that a gross-profit deflator is near-collinear with an oibdp numerator is plausible and the breadth question is worth answering, but the proposal simultaneously drops the third lens and swaps the conditioning weight, so any improvement over the 1.7%/t=1.41 benchmark will be uninterpretable.
evidence: simultaneously drops the third lens and swaps the conditioning weight

rationale: This is the most substantively different weight in the batch — investment composition rather than scale, bounded on [0,1], and not a variant of any archived intensity ratio — with the caveats that dp≈0 firms create an ill-defined 0/0 case and that the measure will partly proxy for asset-lightness/industry membership anyway.
evidence: dp≈0 firms create an ill-defined 0/0 case

rationale: The expression is internally consistent (it equals max(firm intensity, industry mean)) and the asymmetry argument is coherent, but the industry-mean floor will dominate the cross-sectional variation, making this very highly correlated with the already-evaluated IndustryIntensityWeightedYield leader and largely redundant with Signal 3 in the same batch.
evidence: highly correlated with the already-evaluated IndustryIntensityWeightedYield leader and largely redundant

rationale: The expression is internally consistent (SUB(x, IND_ADJ(x)) is indeed the industry-constant mean, and both amplifiers are non-negative so the positive expected sign holds), and pairing a sector disclosure friction with a firm-level forecast-difficulty friction is economically defensible, but it is still a mechanical product of the archive's two best weights and risks simply concentrating in the intersection of pharma/software and high-volatility firms at ~0.08 coverage.
evidence: it is still a mechanical product of the archive's two best weights

rationale: This is the batch's most valuable diagnostic because it directly tests whether the uncertainty channel survives once the unhedged cross-industry amplitude — the main credibility weakness of the 7.1% leader — is stripped out, and the positive-part times volatility weight is correctly non-negative so the expected sign is coherent; the cost is that zeroing all below-peer firms concentrates the spread in a narrow above-peer subsample.
evidence: zeroing all below-peer firms concentrates the spread in a narrow above-peer subsample

rationale: Changing the volatility window from five years to three, with every other component held fixed, is a hyperparameter tweak of an already-evaluated signal rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the coverage gain at stake (0.080 vs 0.089) is too small to justify a generation slot.
evidence: a hyperparameter tweak of an already-evaluated signal rather than a substantively different mechanism

rationale: The drift of the hidden-to-visible capital ratio is a genuinely new conditioning state relative to the archive's level and persistence weights and the positive-part gate keeps the sign coherent, but the design is exposed to two contaminations the test must diagnose — a shrinking tangible denominator (at − intan) mechanically inflating the weight for distressed or acquisitive firms, and overlap with the published abnormal-R&D-increase anomaly.
evidence: a shrinking tangible denominator mechanically inflating the weight for distressed or acquisitive firms

rationale: Despite the framing, both factors are intangible-intensity proxies differing only in aggregation level and deflator, so this is precisely the "recombination of two intensity ratios" the proposal's own sibling concedes was rejected earlier, and boundedness of the second term does not make the pair economically independent.
evidence: the proposal's own sibling concedes was rejected earlier

rationale: Replacing the cardinal industry-mean weight with its rank is a monotone reweighting and therefore low-novelty — the archive already applied the same bounding logic at the firm level — but the sector-concentration concern behind a 7.1% alpha driven by a handful of industries is legitimate, so this earns its place as a robustness test rather than a discovery.
evidence: a monotone reweighting and therefore low-novelty

rationale: Internally consistent and sign-coherent, but it is only a rank-blend of two amplifiers already tested separately in the archive (intensity×VOL at 7.3% and intensity×accrual-wedge at 6.5%), so the expected information gain is modest and the 5-year VOL term will again depress coverage to ~0.08.
evidence: only a rank-blend of two amplifiers already tested separately in the archive

rationale: A clean, correctly-specified product of the two highest-alpha amplifiers at full coverage (industry-mean intensity and the accrual wedge) with genuinely disjoint inputs, though it remains a recombination of archived components rather than a new economic channel.
evidence: remains a recombination of archived components rather than a new economic channel

rationale: This differs from proposal 2 only in replacing the cardinal industry-mean intensity with its rank — a substitution already isolated in the archived BoundedSectorRankWeightedYield — making it a cosmetic variant whose result is largely predictable from the two existing tests.
evidence: a cosmetic variant whose result is largely predictable from the two existing tests

rationale: The most structurally distinct proposal in the batch and the equity-anchoring story is coherent, but deflating hidden capital by ceq mechanically injects leverage into the amplifier, so a positive result will be hard to separate from a leverage/distress tilt and from the closely related archived HiddenToVisibleCapitalYield.
evidence: deflating hidden capital by ceq mechanically injects leverage into the amplifier

rationale: A defensible consolidation of the 7.8% incumbent with a less noisy friction proxy, but note the rank-sum friction index has a strictly positive floor and therefore does not gate low-friction firms toward zero, so the stated "conjunction" is weaker than claimed and the triple interaction raises overfitting risk at generation 9.
evidence: rank-sum friction index has a strictly positive floor and therefore does not gate low-friction firms

rationale: Well-specified and answers a genuinely important question (firm-level mispricing versus sector-amplitude bet) at full coverage, though the archived SectorNeutralUncertaintyAmplified already partially answered it, so this is incremental confirmation rather than a new mechanism.
evidence: the archived SectorNeutralUncertaintyAmplified already partially answered it

rationale: This is a straight additive rank composite of two textbook published anomalies (operating profitability/RMW and asset growth/CMA), and SUMRANK imposes no interaction at all — a firm scores well on either leg alone, directly contradicting the stated "high only when both conditions hold" claim.
evidence: SUMRANK imposes no interaction at all

rationale: Internally inconsistent accounting — inventory build is already deducted inside oancf, so subtracting DELTA(invt) double-counts working capital, and what remains after that error is essentially the well-known free-cash-flow-to-assets / cash-based profitability measure.
evidence: subtracting DELTA(invt) double-counts working capital

rationale: A legitimate and internally consistent conditional test (the zero-mass for unprofitable firms sits at the z-score mean as claimed), though the arbitrary 5% ROA cutoff creates a large point mass that will drive much of the cross-sectional slope and the underlying asset-growth effect is itself heavily published.
evidence: arbitrary 5% ROA cutoff creates a large point mass

rationale: The divergence between multi-year profitability and capex-intensity trends is a genuinely cross-theme, second-derivative quantity not reducible to either level anomaly, though both trend components have published antecedents (profitability trend; abnormal capital investment) and the five-year window will cost coverage and make the signal very slow-moving.
evidence: five-year window will cost coverage and make the signal very slow-moving

rationale: The marginal-ROIC concept is appealing but the construction is unstable — a small, always-positive denominator means asset-light firms with trivial capex get explosive scores that 1% winsorization will not tame, and after that noise the signal is largely a rescaled earnings-change (a known anomaly) rather than the intended profitability-investment interaction.
evidence: small, always-positive denominator means asset-light firms with trivial capex get explosive scores

rationale: This is a rank difference of two separately published anomalies — cash-based operating profitability and net external financing (Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan) — so it is an additive re-packaging rather than a conditional or interactive test of the stated "profitable growers get funded and overpriced" channel.
evidence: an additive re-packaging rather than a conditional or interactive test

rationale: This is a one-for-one input substitution (oancf→ebitda) inside the archived `profit_weighted_low_reinvestment` expression with the identical economic story, i.e. a cosmetic coverage-tuning variant rather than a new mechanism, and the stated goal ("preserve the mechanism while tripling the sample") concedes as much.
evidence: a cosmetic coverage-tuning variant rather than a new mechanism

rationale: A weakest-link gate on high profitability and low asset growth is close to a direct double-sort on RMW and CMA, the very factors in the FF5 benchmark, and "asset growth net of cash" is a documented refinement (net operating asset growth), so the incremental content over published anomalies is thin.
evidence: incremental content over published anomalies is thin

rationale: The inventory-to-sales channel is an economically distinct, faster-moving form of investment discipline that is not spanned by capex/asset-growth legs already in the archive, and both legs are consistently sales-scaled so the interaction is coherent — though the margin leg will be strongly industry-driven and the inventory leg overlaps partly with the known inventory-growth and accrual anomalies.
evidence: margin leg will be strongly industry-driven

rationale: The labor-hiring-rate anomaly (Belo–Lin–Bazdresch) is well published so the investment leg alone is a rediscovery, but conditioning it on profitability to test whether the mechanism is expansion appetite generally versus capital-specific is a legitimate discriminating test; coverage and staleness of Compustat `emp` are the main practical risks.
evidence: coverage and staleness of Compustat `emp` are the main practical risks

rationale: With a positive-signed profitability rank multiplied into the score but a negative expected sign, the profitability leg pushes directly against the hypothesis — the extreme portfolios become "profitable expanders" short versus "unprofitable non-investors" long, so the test confounds the intended overpricing effect with a large reverse-RMW bet rather than isolating the short leg as claimed.
evidence: the profitability leg pushes directly against the hypothesis

rationale: The substantive novelty is the gross-PP&E capacity-growth leg rather than the persistence framing, since for slow-moving inputs a moving average of the product is numerically close to a product of moving averages, so the turnover-reduction rationale is weaker than stated but the variant is still a defensible, distinct member of the family.
evidence: The substantive novelty is the gross-PP&E capacity-growth leg

rationale: The diagnosis (FMB slope of 4.06 with zero FF5 alpha implies a cross-industry capital-intensity tilt) is sound and worth resolving, but swapping RANK for IND_RANK in an otherwise identical expression is the textbook cosmetic variant the objective warns against rather than a substantively different construction.
evidence: the textbook cosmetic variant the objective warns against

rationale: The level-to-change reframing is a genuinely distinct state-change mechanism, but the construction is partly self-referential — a jump in EBITDA mechanically shrinks capx/MAX(ebitda,dp), so the "reinvestment drop" leg will partially reproduce profitability momentum already captured by the first leg, and a level-vs-change horse race would be needed to interpret any result.
evidence: will partially reproduce profitability momentum already captured by the first leg

rationale: Net-to-gross PP&E as a cumulative-non-replacement stock is a real cross-theme quantity that is neither a one-year flow nor an FF5 loading, and the stated conditioning logic (old capital means harvesting only when profitable, obsolescence otherwise) is internally consistent with the multiplicative form; the main risk is that the ratio is dominated by depreciation-schedule and industry heterogeneity rather than managerial restraint.
evidence: ratio is dominated by depreciation-schedule and industry heterogeneity rather than managerial restraint

rationale: The investment leg is close to Titman-Wei-Xie abnormal capital investment (capex benchmarked to the firm's own recent history), so novelty rests entirely on the profitability gate, and a 5-observation TS_RANK yields only five distinct values, which will blunt cross-sectional resolution.
evidence: a 5-observation TS_RANK yields only five distinct values

rationale: Margin level interacted with change in asset turnover is the DuPont decomposition studied by Soliman (2008), whose central published result is precisely that ΔATO positively predicts returns, so this is a direct rediscovery dressed in new language.
evidence: this is a direct rediscovery dressed in new language

rationale: This mechanically averages two investment legs already tested in the archive under the same margin gate, so it will almost certainly deliver an alpha between the two parents and cannot cleanly answer the stated independence question — a correlation check or a residualized second leg would be far more informative than a blended composite.
evidence: cannot cleanly answer the stated independence question

rationale: This is an explicitly acknowledged cosmetic re-parameterization of the archive winner `profitable_capex_own_history_low` (same profitability gate, same own-history capex-intensity leg, only TS_RANK swapped for a current/MA5 ratio), so it tests measurement resolution rather than any new economic content and will be near-collinear with the existing signal.
evidence: an explicitly acknowledged cosmetic re-parameterization of the archive winner

rationale: Fully firm-demeaning both legs is a coherent and internally consistent response to the diagnosed style-absorption problem, though it overlaps materially with the gen-0 `margin_up_capex_down_trend` (profit rising while capex falls) and differs mainly in using own-mean deviations and a product instead of trends and a difference, so incremental information is uncertain.
evidence: overlaps materially with the gen-0 `margin_up_capex_down_trend`

rationale: Net debt issuance scaled by cash flow is a direct restatement of the well-documented net-debt-issuance/external-financing anomaly and largely duplicates the archive's `outside_capital_per_internal_dollar` (which already put DELTA(dltt) over max(oancf,dp) with a profitability gate and produced t=0.43 alpha), so it is a rediscovery on two fronts.
evidence: largely duplicates the archive's `outside_capital_per_internal_dollar`

rationale: Acquirer underperformance and the acquisition component of asset growth are established published anomalies, and because aqc is zero for most firm-years the RANK leg collapses to a near-binary acquirer indicator with a massive tie block, making the "conditional" interaction effectively a profitability sort within non-acquirers.
evidence: the RANK leg collapses to a near-binary acquirer indicator with a massive tie block

rationale: Pairing an SG&A-intensity change with own-norm capex restraint is a genuinely new construct that avoids the RMW-loading level gate, but the sign is not obviously safe — a falling SG&A/sales ratio is mechanically produced by sales growth and is elsewhere read as underinvestment in intangibles — so the expected positive sign rests on a contestable premise.
evidence: the expected positive sign rests on a contestable premise

rationale: Normalizing capex intensity by its own five-year maximum is a near-monotone transform of the archive winner's TS_RANK leg and is also highly redundant with proposal 1 in this same batch, so it cannot cleanly discriminate among own-history benchmarks and adds little beyond a third parameterization of an already-tested mechanism.
evidence: a near-monotone transform of the archive winner's TS_RANK leg

rationale: A single-operator extension of the archive's best signal, but the industry-demeaning of the own-norm capex deviation is economically motivated (idiosyncratic restraint vs. sector capex cycle) and directly targets the diagnosed FMB-strong/alpha-weak pattern, so it is a defensible if incremental test rather than a cosmetic rescaling.
evidence: a defensible if incremental test rather than a cosmetic rescaling

rationale: The inventory-intensity leg edges toward the well-documented inventory-growth anomaly (Thomas–Zhang, Belo–Lin), but recasting it as an own-norm deviation interacted with a profit windfall is a legitimate and clearly stated test of whether the mechanism is capex-specific or general operating-asset restraint.
evidence: a legitimate and clearly stated test of whether the mechanism is capex-specific

rationale: The two legs are mechanically linked — above-norm EBITDA largely produces above-norm cash balances — so the product is closer to a squared profitability-windfall signal than to a measure of a deliberate retention-versus-reinvestment policy, and the cash-holdings level effect (Palazzo 2012) is itself a known anomaly.
evidence: the product is closer to a squared profitability-windfall signal

rationale: The hypothesis claims a screen ("requiring that revenue still be expanding") and the type is declared conditional, but SUMRANK implements a purely additive tilt in which a large profitability deviation can fully offset outright revenue contraction, so the expression does not do what the economics asks and also imports an uncontrolled sales-growth tilt.
evidence: SUMRANK implements a purely additive tilt

rationale: A well-motivated repair of the archive's worst failure that replaces scale-driven headcount growth with own-norm labor intensity, though it partially overlaps with the profitability leg (falling employees per sales dollar mechanically accompanies margin expansion) and will read in part as a labor-productivity signal.
evidence: it partially overlaps with the profitability leg

rationale: Both legs are driven by the same underlying fact of a stagnant capital base — a firm that stops investing automatically shows above-norm sales-to-gross-PPE and below-norm capex-to-net-PPE — so the "joint occurrence" claim is undermined by mechanical denominator overlap and the signal risks being a doubled low-investment bet rather than utilization × restraint.
evidence: the "joint occurrence" claim is undermined by mechanical denominator overlap

rationale: This is a pure recombination of three already-evaluated archive legs (gross-margin windfall, industry-demeaned own-norm capex restraint, sales-growth MIN screen) with no new economic content, and stacking the three best-performing components in a strict triple conjunction mostly selects on prior in-sample noise while shrinking the effective long portfolio.
evidence: a pure recombination of three already-evaluated archive legs

rationale: A legitimate but modest horizon variant of the archive winner `own_norm_profit_up_capex_down` — the 3y-vs-5y MA crossover genuinely separates regime shifts from project lumpiness, though the two windows overlap heavily so the test has less discriminating power than claimed and the profitability leg is left unchanged.
evidence: the two windows overlap heavily

rationale: Well-constructed and internally consistent — both legs are same-unit asset-scaled own-norm deviations so the subtraction is economically meaningful (essentially the own-norm deviation in EBITDA-minus-capex per asset), and testing magnitude against the family's ubiquitous rank-product form answers a structural question the archive cannot; the main risk is that un-ranked raw deviations leave the FMB slope outlier-sensitive despite winsorization.
evidence: un-ranked raw deviations leave the FMB slope outlier-sensitive

rationale: The "profit windfall" leg is not a profitability measure at all — (oancf − ib)/at is negative total accruals, so the signal rewards firms whose *earnings fall relative to cash flow*, which both contradicts the stated hypothesis of a cash-backed profit improvement and largely rediscovers the Sloan accruals anomaly in change form.
evidence: the "profit windfall" leg is not a profitability measure at all

rationale: A coherent moderation hypothesis that is deliberately informative against `asset_light_margin_rents`, but multiplying by a strictly positive rank imposes a standalone monotone tilt toward capital-intensive firms rather than a clean interaction test, so a positive or negative result will be hard to attribute to moderation versus the level effect of asset heaviness.
evidence: hard to attribute to moderation versus the level effect of asset heaviness

rationale: A defensible dynamic recasting of the archive's high-slope R&D-mix signal, but the ratio's denominator means a rising xrd/(capx+xrd) deviation can be driven purely by falling capex — partially re-encoding the restraint leg rather than isolating a reallocation-toward-innovation decision — and xrd coverage near 0.07 will limit portfolio reliability.
evidence: a rising xrd/(capx+xrd) deviation can be driven purely by falling capex

rationale: Because the own-norm deviation of (capx−dp)/ppent equals the deviation of capx/ppent minus the deviation of dp/ppent, and dp/ppent is highly persistent so its deviation is near zero, this leg is mechanically almost identical to the archived winner's restraint leg — a cosmetic variant rather than the claimed isolation of "expansion" capex.
evidence: mechanically almost identical to the archived winner's restraint leg

rationale: The claimholder moderator is a genuinely new dimension for this family and the sign logic is internally consistent, but the third rank leg embeds the well-documented low-net-debt/high-cash-holdings premium as a standalone effect, so any alpha gain will need to be shown not to come from that leg alone (and triple rank multiplication risks a concentrated, unstable long side).
evidence: embeds the well-documented low-net-debt/high-cash-holdings premium as a standalone effect

rationale: This is essentially the already-tested additive netting (unreinvested_windfall_in_asset_units, fmb 1.88 / talpha 2.35) with z-scoring and a different capex scaler, and the z-scoring destroys the very unit-commensurability that made the asset-unit netting economically interpretable — a re-run rather than a substantively different construction (also mislabeled interaction_type "ratio" for a difference).
evidence: essentially the already-tested additive netting

rationale: Symmetrically industry-demeaning both legs is a single-operator extension of an archived variant, but it tests a well-posed economic question — whether the sector-cyclical component of profitability improvement is signal or noise relative to FF5 — and the expected sign follows correctly from the expression.
evidence: a single-operator extension of an archived variant

rationale: A clean complementary diagnostic to the gen-5 smoothed-restraint result that isolates which leg must be fresh versus durable, though the MA3-minus-MA5 windfall uses overlapping windows and will be a weak, slow-moving trend measure, so a muted cross-sectional slope is a real risk.
evidence: will be a weak, slow-moving trend measure

rationale: Averaging two ranked readings of the same latent earning-power improvement is a legitimate measurement-error reduction rather than screen-stacking, and the diagnosis (equal alphas, very different Sharpes) supports it — but since both constituents are already archived, the expected information gain is incremental and the result may simply land between them.
evidence: both constituents are already archived, the expected information gain is incremental

rationale: A legitimate complementarity test of two separately-validated archive legs, but it is combinatorial rather than new economics, and it stacks a third rank onto a moderator (net debt/assets) that already collapsed the cross-sectional slope to 1.52 in `harvest_that_accrues_to_equity` — likely a non-monotone, low-leverage/cash-holdings style tilt that industry-demeaning the other two legs cannot repair.
evidence: stacks a third rank onto a moderator ... that already collapsed the cross-sectional slope

rationale: This is a single-operator ablation of an existing archive signal (adding IND_ADJ to the net-debt leg only) rather than a substantively different construction; the attribution question it poses is worth answering, but the answer is largely predictable — capital structure is heavily industry-determined, so demeaning will mostly strip the sector tilt and leave a weaker, mechanically similar version of a signal whose FMB slope was already insignificant.
evidence: a single-operator ablation of an existing archive signal

rationale: The moderator RATIO(xint, ebitda) is sign-unstable — for negative or near-zero EBITDA the ratio flips negative and NEG() then assigns the *highest* rank to exactly the distressed firms the hypothesis wants to exclude, so the expression's natural direction contradicts the stated mechanism; interest coverage is also a well-worn distress/leverage proxy rather than a novel claimholder measure.
evidence: interest coverage is also a well-worn distress/leverage proxy

rationale: Wrapping one IND_ADJ around the capex leg of `capex_shortfall_given_a_windfall` is a cosmetic variant, not a new mechanism, and it introduces a subtle inconsistency the reasoning misses: after industry demeaning, the zero assigned to non-windfall firms is no longer the centre of the conditional distribution, so masked firms will systematically drift into one tail in industries with above- or below-average capex deviations.
evidence: a cosmetic variant, not a new mechanism

rationale: NEG((Δceq − ib)/at) is the clean-surplus net payout / net equity issuance measure — a direct rediscovery of the well-documented net-issuance and net-payout-yield anomalies (Daniel–Titman, Pontiff–Woodgate, Boudoukh et al.) — and the reasoning's claim that it is "not a financing-anomaly proxy" is exactly backwards; it will also be contaminated by write-offs, dividends-in-kind and other clean-surplus violations.
evidence: a direct rediscovery of the well-documented net-issuance and net-payout-yield anomalies

rationale: A coherent, parsimonious two-leg combination of two independently validated modifications (durability on the profitability leg, peer-demeaning on both), with a well-posed question about whether sector purity survives when the windfall is measured as a persistent rather than transitory improvement — though it remains an incremental recombination rather than a new mechanism, and IND_ADJ of an already own-norm-demeaned quantity risks double-differencing away most of the surviving variation.
evidence: IND_ADJ of an already own-norm-demeaned quantity risks double-differencing away most of the surviving variation

rationale: This is a strictly monotone (outer RANK) re-encoding of the archived `peer_relative_harvest_with_slack`, so it re-proposes an already-evaluated signal with identical firm ordering and, as the author concedes, identical portfolio statistics — a diagnostic on FMB regressor distribution, not a new economic signal.
evidence: re-proposes an already-evaluated signal with identical firm ordering

rationale: Averaging the slack and asset-vintage moderators is a genuinely different construction from either archived triple product, though the archive is internally contradictory about the sign of ppent/ppegt (`profitable_old_capital_base` treats low net-to-gross as the good state, `harvest_with_young_capital_runway` the opposite) and the vintage leg carried essentially no cross-sectional slope (fmb 0.14), so noise reduction is speculative.
evidence: the archive is internally contradictory about the sign of ppent/ppegt

rationale: A weakest-link gate is not a monotone transform of the product and so constitutes a substantively different aggregation of the same three legs, giving a clean test of whether the alpha lives in the extreme corner or in joint moderate satisfaction — though it remains a functional-form experiment on well-trodden legs rather than new economics.
evidence: a functional-form experiment on well-trodden legs rather than new economics

rationale: Pairing the archive's best-slope profitability leg with its best-alpha moderator is the obvious and defensible next step and is not a rediscovery, but it is an incremental recombination of two evaluated signals, and the claimed benefit of the inert outer RANK applies only to the FMB regression, not to the alpha.
evidence: an incremental recombination of two evaluated signals

rationale: Decomposing net-debt-to-assets into a cash-coverage moderator is a real attribution test that can distinguish a distributable-cash mechanism from a low-leverage style tilt, and the depreciation floor sensibly handles debt-free firms, though cash-holdings premia are themselves a documented anomaly that could partly account for any gain.
evidence: cash-holdings premia are themselves a documented anomaly that could partly account for any gain

rationale: The expression multiplies a leg whose standalone expected sign is positive (peer-relative profitability improvement) by an investment leg expected negative and then asserts an unambiguously negative composite sign, so the predicted direction is not implied by the construction; moreover profitable-high-investment underperformance is essentially the published q-theory investment anomaly conditioned on profitability.
evidence: the predicted direction is not implied by the construction

rationale: This is the archived min_gate_peer_harvest_slack with the net-debt moderator swapped for a mechanically near-identical cash-to-debt measure (net debt already nets out cash), and the stated justification is factually wrong — the net-debt product form delivered the largest alpha (7.0%, peer_relative_harvest_with_slack), not the 6.1% cash-coverage version — so the proposal is a cosmetic variant built on a misread of the archive.
evidence: a mechanically near-identical cash-to-debt measure

rationale: A single, economically motivated leg substitution (3y-vs-5y durable rents for the 1y windfall) inside the archived gate, testing whether the durability leg's strong slopes survive the aggregation that produced the strong alphas — incremental but a legitimate and interpretable one-factor-at-a-time test.
evidence: incremental but a legitimate and interpretable one-factor-at-a-time test

rationale: Adding the peer-relative revenue-growth screen as a fourth floor condition is a genuine extension rather than a restatement, and the pre-registered interpretation of a degradation (moderators are substitutes / over-restriction) makes the test informative either way, though the long leg risks becoming a narrow, unstable intersection.
evidence: the long leg risks becoming a narrow, unstable intersection

rationale: The asymmetric structure — rank the harvest interaction first, then cap it by slack — poses a real aggregation question that neither the symmetric three-way gate nor the triple product answers, and the expression correctly implements the stated hypothesis on a common rank scale.
evidence: poses a real aggregation question that neither the symmetric three-way gate nor the triple product answers

rationale: Substituting a level (structurally low reinvestment rate) for a deviation (below own norm) is an economically meaningful distinction between a standing policy and a mispriced surprise, and comparing gate versus the archived product form of the same legs cleanly attributes the difference, though the leg is close to the well-known asset-growth/investment anomaly in industry-adjusted dress.
evidence: Substituting a level for a deviation is an economically meaningful distinction

rationale: A strict two-leg ablation of an already-archived three-leg gate is low in novelty, but it is the missing attribution baseline separating aggregation effects from the claimholder moderator and is the most parsimonious candidate for a final reported signal, so it is worth the cheap test.
evidence: A strict two-leg ablation of an already-archived three-leg gate is low in novelty

rationale: Mean-ROA-scaled-by-ROA-volatility is essentially the standard "earnings stability" leg of published quality/QMJ and earnings-volatility anomalies rather than a new interaction, and dividing by a five-year volatility that can be near zero makes the cross-sectional ranking hostage to a handful of denominator outliers that 1% winsorization only partly tames.
evidence: essentially the standard "earnings stability" leg of published quality/QMJ

rationale: This is a mechanical crossing of two canonical anomalies (profitability and Sloan accruals), and the hard indicator is internally incoherent because zeroing the industry rank places accrual-inflated firms at the middle of the signal distribution — above genuinely low-ROA but cash-confirmed firms — so the sort no longer tests the stated conditional hypothesis.
evidence: zeroing the industry rank places accrual-inflated firms at the middle of the signal distribution

rationale: The expression is a plain additive rank sum of profitability and negative leverage — two heavily documented, already-priced characteristics — and it does not implement the stated "unlevered profitability" concept at all, since no unlevering or conditioning actually occurs.
evidence: it does not implement the stated "unlevered profitability" concept at all

rationale: Scaling current EBITDA/assets by a five-year count of profitable years is a coherent profitability-times-track-record interaction with a defensible extrapolation mechanism, though it overlaps materially with Piotroski-style persistence screens and creates an awkward discontinuity where loss-making firms with zero profitable years collapse to exactly zero rather than to the bottom of the sort.
evidence: loss-making firms with zero profitable years collapse to exactly zero

rationale: The expected sign is backwards on the second leg: a rising net-working-capital-to-assets trend is mechanically growth in working-capital accruals, which the accrual and net-operating-asset literature shows predicts *lower* future returns, so the composite pits gross profitability against a component with a documented opposite-sign loading.
evidence: The expected sign is backwards on the second leg

rationale: Using the five-year minimum ROA as a downside "profitability floor" alongside cash-flow coverage of liabilities is a defensible and reasonably distinct construction, but it remains an additive rank composite of two quality/distress measures and min-ROA will be highly collinear with mean ROA, so the incremental content over a standard profitability sort needs to be demonstrated.
evidence: min-ROA will be highly collinear with mean ROA

rationale: Both legs are essentially profitability scaled by a balance-sheet stock (oiadp/at and oibdp/lt are highly correlated), so the "bottleneck" MIN is a cosmetic operator swap on the archive's already-tested SelfFinancedProfitPower/TroughProfitSolvency rank-composite of profitability and profit-to-liability coverage rather than a genuine new interaction.
evidence: a cosmetic operator swap on the archive's already-tested SelfFinancedProfitPower/TroughProfitSolvency

rationale: EBITDA-less-interest over total liabilities is a textbook debt-service-coverage/credit-quality metric (an Ohlson/Piotroski-style ingredient), and since xint is small relative to oibdp the measure is dominated by oibdp/lt, making it a single-ratio profitability-scaled-by-liabilities sort very close to the archive's oancf/lt leg rather than a cross-theme interaction.
evidence: the measure is dominated by oibdp/lt

rationale: The working-capital-intensity leg is close to the known net-operating-assets/accruals anomaly, but the sign orientation is correct and consistent with that literature, and conditioning profitability on operating-cycle cash intensity is a coherent, non-trivial interaction — the main risks are sale-in-denominator instability for low-revenue firms and coverage loss from act/lct.
evidence: sale-in-denominator instability for low-revenue firms and coverage loss from act/lct

rationale: The Δleverage leg is close to the documented debt-issuance/net-external-financing anomaly, so part of the return is likely already spanned, but the expected sign is internally consistent and interacting financing direction with profitability is a legitimate and reasonably distinct test of "self-funded" operating strength.
evidence: part of the return is likely already spanned

rationale: Financing-policy stability is a plausibly less-mined channel than earnings stability and the expression matches the hypothesis, but a standard deviation estimated from three annual leverage observations is extremely noisy and will largely proxy for asset growth/issuance activity, so the effective information content may be thin.
evidence: Financing-policy stability is a plausibly less-mined channel than earnings stability

rationale: The effective-interest term xint/lt has an order-of-magnitude smaller cross-sectional dispersion than oiadp/at (and is downward-biased and noisy because lt includes non-interest-bearing liabilities), so the spread will correlate near-unity with a plain ROA sort — a rediscovery of the profitability anomaly dressed as a cost-of-capital spread.
evidence: a rediscovery of the profitability anomaly dressed as a cost-of-capital spread

rationale: This is a mechanical stacking of the two best archive signals' conditioners onto the same profitability leg rather than a new mechanism, and multiplying three highly correlated funding-pressure ranks will mostly shrink cross-sectional dispersion and coverage without testing anything the parents' correlation could not reveal directly.
evidence: a mechanical stacking of the two best archive signals' conditioners

rationale: The decomposition logic is stated correctly (the NEG((act−lct)/sale) long leg does load on high current liabilities, so isolating lct/at is a coherent attribution test), though the resulting conditioner is close to a plain leverage-level screen of the type that has already repeatedly failed in this archive.
evidence: a plain leverage-level screen of the type that has already repeatedly failed in this archive

rationale: Replacing a static coverage stock with liquid assets scaled by a committed cost flow is a genuinely different economic construct (cost-structure endurance rather than accounting liquidity) and the expression matches the hypothesis, with the main caveats being xsga availability and near-zero denominators for low-overhead firms, both partly mitigated by industry ranking.
evidence: xsga availability and near-zero denominators for low-overhead firms

rationale: Stripping the liquid-asset denominator out of the archive's strongest conditioner cleanly separates maturity concentration from liquidity, the sign is correct and zero-debt handling is sensible, with the only reservation that short-term-debt-share return predictability is itself a semi-established credit-risk finding so the incremental novelty rests on the interaction with profitability.
evidence: short-term-debt-share return predictability is itself a semi-established credit-risk finding

rationale: By the proposal's own admission this holds economic content fixed and changes only the aggregation operator, which is precisely the cosmetic variant the objective warns against, and MIN of two ranks discards the upper-tail information that gives the rank product its dispersion.
evidence: this holds economic content fixed and changes only the aggregation operator

rationale: A legitimate and cleanly specified attribution test that isolates whether the archive winner's alpha comes from the R&D add-back or the liquidity leg, but the low prior on yet another leverage-level conditioner (and its near-duplication of LowNearTermClaimsProfit's economic content) limits its standalone value.
evidence: its near-duplication of LowNearTermClaimsProfit's economic content

rationale: This is a mechanical crossing of two already-tested archive legs (the xrd add-back profitability of IntangibleProfitLowLeverage/WithSlack and the dlc/act conditioner of RolloverRiskAdjustedProfit) that will almost certainly "work" by construction while testing no new economic claim — the stated super-additivity story (R&D is cut first under rollover pressure) is not identified by a simple rank product.
evidence: a mechanical crossing of two already-tested archive legs

rationale: The rationale is internally inconsistent — revt−cogs−xsga differs from the already-tested oiadp only by depreciation (it is essentially oibdp, also already used in the archive), so it does not remove accruals or special items as claimed and is ~0.9+ correlated with the existing profitability leg, making this a cosmetic variant of RolloverRiskAdjustedProfit built on a published (Novy-Marx) profitability measure.
evidence: it does not remove accruals or special items as claimed

rationale: Isolating the non-debt residual of current liabilities scaled as payables-days is a genuinely untested cell and reconciles the WorkingCapitalLightProfit sign puzzle, but the expected sign is contestable — the net-operating-asset/accrual literature and trade-credit bargaining-power evidence both imply high payables should predict *higher* returns, so the NEG() direction may be backwards.
evidence: the expected sign is contestable

rationale: Change in short-term debt is close to a catalogued anomaly (the net-external-financing / change-in-current-debt family), so novelty is limited, but the specific question — whether the *change* in the fragile maturity bucket adds to the level effect after Δtotal-debt failed — is a coherent and cheaply diagnostic follow-up.
evidence: “Change in short-term debt is close to a catalogued anomaly”

rationale: Relocating the stability concept from a leverage variable that carries no alpha to the one funding variable that does is a defensible substantive change, but a 3-observation volatility of dlc/act is mechanically increasing in its level, so any positive result risks being a noisy proxy for the already-established level effect rather than evidence for funding stability per se.
evidence: “risks being a noisy proxy for the already-established level effect”

rationale: Replacing the stock-of-liquid-assets conditioner with a flow-coverage measure is the most economically distinct proposal in this batch and addresses a real gap (asset-light firms with thin balance sheets but ample cash generation), though the reviewer should note that both legs embed operating income, so the signal partly compounds profitability with an inverse-leverage tilt and the denominator becomes unstable for near-debt-free firms.
evidence: “both legs embed operating income”

rationale: This is the archived PayableStretchProfit with the conditioner's rank orientation reversed and the expected sign flipped to match its realized negative alpha — a mechanical in-sample sign fit on an already-evaluated construction rather than a new hypothesis test.
evidence: “a mechanical in-sample sign fit on an already-evaluated construction”

rationale: (lct−dlc)/lct is just 1 − dlc/lct, a denominator swap on the already-tested ShortDebtShareProfit (NEG dlc/lt, α=3.4%, t=3.5) and highly collinear with it, so the "mix vs. level" framing does not make this substantively different from an archived winner.
evidence: “a denominator swap on the already-tested ShortDebtShareProfit”

rationale: This is the only proposal opening a genuinely untested channel (accounting conservatism rather than funding structure) with a coherent mechanism and full coverage, though the reviewer should be aware that dp/(at−act) is heavily contaminated by asset age, goodwill/intangible-heavy denominators, and is partly a mechanical restatement of EBITDA-based profitability.
evidence: “heavily contaminated by asset age, goodwill/intangible-heavy denominators”

rationale: (act−dlc)/lct decomposes into act/lct minus dlc/lct, both of which are already-tested conditioners in the archive (IntangibleProfitWithSlack, RolloverRiskAdjustedProfit, SurvivalHorizonProfit uses the identical act−dlc numerator), so this is a recombination of known ingredients rather than a new economic channel.
evidence: “a recombination of known ingredients rather than a new economic channel”

rationale: The Δact/at leg rewards firms accumulating current assets, which is the long leg of the well-documented working-capital accruals/asset-growth anomaly and predicts *low* returns, so the stated positive expected sign is in tension with the expression's dominant known component; the Δdlc leg meanwhile duplicates ShrinkingRolloverExposure.
evidence: “the stated positive expected sign is in tension with the expression's dominant known component”

rationale: The conditioner is byte-identical to the archive's best performer (RolloverRiskAdjustedProfit, NEG dlc/act) and only the profitability denominator changes, making this a one-input tweak of an evaluated signal, with the added hazard that at−act goes to zero for asset-light firms and produces unstable, outlier-driven ratios.
evidence: “byte-identical to the archive's best performer”

rationale: The stated logic is backwards — since oibdp = oiadp + dp, replacing EBIT with EBITDA *introduces* a mechanical positive link between the two legs (dp raises both) rather than breaking it, so a positive result would be uninformative about the conservatism-versus-cash-earnings question the test claims to settle.
evidence: “a positive result would be uninformative about the conservatism-versus-cash-earnings question”

rationale: The within-firm change in depreciation intensity is a coherent, economically motivated identification of the discretionary-conservatism mechanism (essentially the Beneish DEPI logic, but as an interaction with profitability rather than a standalone manipulation flag), and the sign convention matches the expression; the main risk is noise from capex timing and acquisitions in the denominator.
evidence: “the main risk is noise from capex timing and acquisitions in the denominator”

rationale: The coverage-repair motivation is legitimate, but EBITDA − Δ(act−lct) is not "the same economic quantity" as MIN(EBITDA, OCF) — it drops the cash-validation/conservatism operator entirely and, because act includes cash and lct includes dlc, it penalizes cash accumulation and short-term debt paydown, contaminating the accrual adjustment it is meant to make.
evidence: “it drops the cash-validation/conservatism operator entirely”

rationale: A defensible but low-information refinement: TS_MIN(ROA,3) is highly correlated with contemporaneous ROA so the test is close to a reparameterization of the gen-4 winner, and the claim that the persistence limb is untested overstates matters given MA(ROA,3) and TS_MIN(ROA,5) both already appear in the archive.
evidence: “close to a reparameterization of the gen-4 winner”

rationale: The negative-change-in-net-working-capital leg is a direct restatement of Sloan's working-capital accrual anomaly (and its profitability interaction is the standard earnings-quality/quality-minus-junk construction), so this is rediscovery rather than a new cross-theme mechanism, and using act−lct rather than non-cash/non-debt working capital adds measurement contamination.
evidence: “a direct restatement of Sloan's working-capital accrual anomaly”

rationale: The gross-asset denominator is a reasonable idea in principle, but the design does not do what the rationale claims — it changes both the profitability denominator and the conditioner relative to the gen-4 result, so it cannot identify whether that result is an asset-age artifact, and TS_SUM(dp,5) added to total assets is a crude, monotone-ish adjustment likely to leave the industry-rank leg nearly unchanged.
evidence: “it cannot identify whether that result is an asset-age artifact”

rationale: A defensible composite of the archive's two strongest independent channels, but the double-subtraction of `dp` (once inside the cash leg's `oancf - dp`, once implicitly rewarded in the `dp/(at-act)` conditioner) creates an offsetting mechanical link that will partly cancel rather than reinforce the two effects, so the "complementarity" claim is weaker than stated.
evidence: creates an offsetting mechanical link that will partly cancel

rationale: This is a cosmetic smoothing variant of ConservativeDepreciationProfit (already at fmb_tstat 5.09, ls_talpha 3.30) with no new economic content — a three-year moving average of the same conditioner is exactly the kind of measurement tweak the objective asks researchers not to substitute for a substantive improvement.
evidence: “a cosmetic smoothing variant of ConservativeDepreciationProfit”

rationale: The conditioner is identical to the already-tested RolloverRiskAdjustedProfit and the only change is subtracting `dp` a second time from an income measure that is already after depreciation — an arbitrary, uncalibrated stress charge that mostly re-ranks firms by capital intensity rather than by accounting conservatism, so it neither cleanly "internalizes" the gen-4 channel nor constitutes a distinct hypothesis.
evidence: “The conditioner is identical to the already-tested RolloverRiskAdjustedProfit”

rationale: A legitimate and cheap decomposition test of an untested cell (dltt/act) that discriminates between the callability and total-claim-burden mechanisms, though it is largely a component of the already-tested lt/act conditioner and the framing admits a null result is the informative outcome, which caps its standalone value.
evidence: “it is largely a component of the already-tested lt/act conditioner”

rationale: A within-firm time-series position measure of leverage is a genuinely distinct object from every cross-sectional or one-year-change conditioner in the archive and plausibly nets out permanent business-model leverage, though the claim that it is the "only" untested construction is overstated and the five-year window's coverage cost needs watching.
evidence: “the five-year window's coverage cost needs watching”

rationale: A reasonable consolidation of the two highest-alpha ingredients, but dlc/act and the previously paired lt/act are components of the same liquidity-versus-claims construct, so the assumed imperfect correlation is optimistic and the likely outcome is a marginal rather than reinforcing gain.
evidence: components of the same liquidity-versus-claims construct

rationale: A defensible additive-index merge of the archive's two strongest conditioners (depreciation conservatism and rollover exposure) that plausibly avoids rank-product compression, but it is an incremental recombination of already-tested components whose likely outcome is an interpolation between the two parents rather than a new mechanism.
evidence: an incremental recombination of already-tested components

rationale: The numerator mixes a genuine depreciation *rate* with an R&D *intensity* term over a long-term-asset denominator that is tiny for exactly the asset-light R&D firms the add-back targets, so the conditioner will be dominated by an R&D/PPE explosion — effectively rediscovering the published R&D-intensity anomaly already probed by IntangibleProfitWithSlack/IntangibleProfitLowLeverage rather than generalizing conservatism.
evidence: the conditioner will be dominated by an R&D/PPE explosion

rationale: Since act typically dwarfs oibdp for the vast majority of firms, dlc/(act+oibdp) will be near-collinear with the already-tested dlc/act in RolloverRiskAdjustedProfit, making this a cosmetic reparameterization rather than the substantive redefinition of "resources" the reasoning claims.
evidence: making this a cosmetic reparameterization

rationale: A legitimate factorial cell whose value is diagnostic rather than exploratory — the two legs are known to select partly opposing populations, so the test genuinely resolves whether the final construction should use restored or reported profitability — but it is still a mechanical recombination of two archived components.
evidence: it is still a mechanical recombination of two archived components

rationale: Pairing the highest-alpha profitability leg with the highest-alpha conditioner is a sensible completion of the factorial, though it is the most predictable of the recombinations and both parents already sit at the ~4.2% alpha ceiling, so a genuine breakout is unlikely.
evidence: the most predictable of the recombinations

rationale: This is the only proposal that changes the economic mechanism rather than the parameterization — an interaction between second-moment earnings risk and callable claims — and it is a clean discriminating test of risk-compensation versus mispricing, though the standalone earnings-volatility leg overlaps a published anomaly and a 3-observation annual VOL is statistically noisy.
evidence: a 3-observation annual VOL is statistically noisy

rationale: This is a mechanical splice of three archive signals — QualityIndexProfit with the profitability leg swapped for the already-tested R&D-restored version — with no new economic content beyond what IntangibleProfitConservatism and IntangibleProfitRollover jointly established, so it is effectively a rediscovery/cosmetic recombination rather than a new hypothesis.
evidence: a mechanical splice of three archive signals

rationale: Beyond being a four-component kitchen-sink of already-tested legs (dp intensity, dlc/lt from ShortDebtShareProfit, act/lct from IntangibleProfitWithSlack), the nested SUMRANK silently weights conservatism at 50% and each funding component at 25%, which contradicts the stated "three separable aspects" framing and makes any result uninterpretable as a test of dimensionality.
evidence: the nested SUMRANK silently weights conservatism at 50%

rationale: The floor-vs-level question is a legitimate persistence test, but it is asked here by stacking three previously validated components at once (TS_MIN from ProfitFloorConservatism, R&D restoration, and the two-part quality index), so a change in alpha cannot be attributed to the floor construction — the clean version would vary only TS_MIN against an existing archive baseline.
evidence: a change in alpha cannot be attributed to the floor construction

rationale: This is the only proposal that fixes a real measurement asymmetry rather than reshuffling legs — capitalizing the R&D stock in the denominator directly tests whether the intangible premium is productivity or a mechanical numerator inflation — though the construction is internally half-consistent (full current-year spend is added back with no amortization charge against the capitalized stock) and the R&D-capitalization idea itself is well-trodden in the literature.
evidence: the construction is internally half-consistent

rationale: Filling the {stability}×{conservatism} cell of the 2×2 is a defensible isolated design test given FragileEarningsRollover worked, but note it discards the profitability level entirely, so a positive result may simply reload the well-known low-earnings-volatility quality anomaly interacted with an asset-age/capital-intensity proxy, and the hypothesis text sloppily calls high dp intensity "aggressive depreciation" where the rest of the archive calls it conservative.
evidence: may simply reload the well-known low-earnings-volatility quality anomaly

rationale: This is explicitly the same economic content as proposal 1 with only the aggregation operator changed — a textbook cosmetic variant, and one whose rank-product form is already the dominant construction throughout the archive, so it adds no information the existing pairwise multiplicative signals have not already provided.
evidence: a textbook cosmetic variant

rationale: This is structurally identical to the archived QualityIndexProfit with both legs swapped for their already-tested upgraded versions, so it is a recombination of known components rather than a new mechanism, and SUMRANK-averaging a strong conservatism leg with a rollover leg whose standalone alpha (4.8%) already exceeds the index's is more likely to dilute than to add.
evidence: a recombination of known components rather than a new mechanism

rationale: This is a legitimate internal-consistency repair — MA(xrd,5) is exactly the straight-line amortization matching a five-year TS_SUM stock, so numerator and denominator now use the same capitalization convention — and it is genuinely diagnostic, since for steady-state R&D spenders the numerator collapses back toward reported EBIT and thus cleanly isolates whether the intangible premium is an addback artifact.
evidence: a legitimate internal-consistency repair

rationale: The hypothesis claims both gross-basis corrections are applied to the profitability ratio, but the expression's denominator (at + R&D stock) never restores accumulated depreciation, so the stated "consistent definition of invested capital" is not what the expression computes; it is also a two-component swap on the already-tested AgeAdjustedProfitConservatism/PolicyRate pair.
evidence: is not what the expression computes

rationale: This is FloorRestoredProfitConservatism (fmb 6.30, Sharpe 0.461) with the net-base depreciation rate swapped for the gross-base version already tested in PolicyRateConservatismProfit — a single-component substitution whose likely outcome is a small interpolation between two known results, i.e., a cosmetic variant rather than a new economic test.
evidence: a single-component substitution

rationale: The pairing of tax-expense validation with a gross-base depreciation policy rate is a coherent and previously untested cell with a real economic tension (heavy book depreciation should suppress book-tax conformity), but tax/assets is close to a rescaled pretax profitability measure and edges toward the known book-tax-difference / tax-expense-surprise literature, so its incremental content is uncertain.
evidence: a coherent and previously untested cell with a real economic tension

rationale: Stability of the depreciation rate is a genuinely different construct from its level or direction and is a useful interpretive discriminator, though the reviewer should note that VOL over only three annual observations of an age-contaminated net-base ratio will mechanically penalize firms with trending (aging or acquisitive) asset bases, and prior volatility-conditioner cells in this archive have produced weak or negative alphas.
evidence: VOL over only three annual observations of an age-contaminated net-base ratio

rationale: The product of two industry z-scores is sign-degenerate — an unprofitable, expensive glamour firm (both z-scores strongly negative) receives a large positive score and enters the long leg, directly contradicting the stated claim that such firms are "penalized symmetrically," and the underlying profitable-value combination is itself a well-worn published composite.
evidence: The product of two industry z-scores is sign-degenerate

rationale: A coherent state-conditional value signal whose gating is genuinely non-linear rather than a rescaling, though the 5% hurdle is arbitrary, the zeroed-out group is a bottom score rather than the claimed "neutral" one, and the economics are close to standard value-trap screening.
evidence: the zeroed-out group is a bottom score rather than the claimed "neutral" one

rationale: Gross-profits-to-enterprise-value is an established practitioner/academic factor (the EV-scaled cousin of Novy-Marx gross profitability and Gray-Vogel EBIT/TEV), and as a single accounting ratio it is a rediscovery rather than a cross-theme interaction.
evidence: an established practitioner/academic factor

rationale: Same sign-degeneracy defect as the other z-score product — expensive firms with deteriorating profitability produce large positive values and would be held long, flatly contradicting the reasoning's claim that they are shorted, and the ib/mktcap leg is additionally ill-behaved for loss-making firms.
evidence: expensive firms with deteriorating profitability produce large positive values and would be held long

rationale: Since rank(P/B) is a monotone inversion of rank(B/P), this "expectation-error gap" is arithmetically just an equal-weighted additive quality-plus-value rank composite — a standard construction relabeled with a mispricing story rather than a true interaction.
evidence: just an equal-weighted additive quality-plus-value rank composite

rationale: The MIN operator implements a genuine conjunction that an additive composite cannot replicate and the expected sign follows directly from the expression, but it is conceptually close to a standard profitability-by-value double sort and discards information about the stronger leg, so the incremental content over existing composites needs to be demonstrated empirically.
evidence: discards information about the stronger leg

rationale: This is a cosmetic re-parameterization of the archived CashFlowYield_Weighted_By_MarginImprovement — identical multiplicative structure (IND_RANK of a profitability TREND times a signed IND_ZSCORE valuation yield) with only the numerator (oancf→oibdp) and trend window (5→3) changed, so it tests sample depth rather than a new mechanism.
evidence: a cosmetic re-parameterization of the archived CashFlowYield_Weighted_By_MarginImprovement

rationale: The debt-aware construction on both legs is economically coherent and plausibly less spanned by HML/RMW, but the EV denominator can go small or negative for net-cash firms, flipping the sign of the valuation leg in a way 1% winsorization will not fully control, so the sign discipline is fragile.
evidence: the EV denominator can go small or negative for net-cash firms

rationale: The earnings-quality-as-moderator channel is genuinely distinct from the level-of-profitability legs used so far and the sign discipline is clean, though it sits close to the well-documented accrual/value overlap (cash-flow-to-price subsuming both accruals and book-to-market), and the accrual weight and the (ib+dp)/P yield share the ib and depreciation terms, so the two legs are not fully independent.
evidence: the two legs are not fully independent

rationale: The product of operating margin and sales-to-EV is, up to the rank transform, just operating-profit-to-enterprise-value — a long-published multiple (EBIT/EV) — so the stated claim that this "avoids restating an earnings multiple" contradicts what the expression actually computes, and it duplicates the EV-yield-times-profitability content of the SolvencyAdjustedProfit proposal.
evidence: just operating-profit-to-enterprise-value — a long-published multiple

rationale: Using the second moment of operating profitability as the conditioning weight is a substantively different channel from the level and trend weights already tested and directly addresses the value-trap diagnosis of generation 0, though a five-year VOL on annual data is noisy and will likely cut coverage toward the 0.08 range that already hampered the best gen-0 signal.
evidence: a five-year VOL on annual data is noisy and will likely cut coverage

rationale: Dividend yield gated by profitability is essentially the commercially ubiquitous "sustainable/quality yield" screen, and the construction is internally inconsistent: dvc is zero for the large non-payer population, so the z-scored yield leg puts all non-dividend firms in the short leg, meaning the spread is payers-vs-non-payers rather than the cheap-vs-expensive comparison the hypothesis describes.
evidence: the spread is payers-vs-non-payers rather than the cheap-vs-expensive comparison

rationale: Three-year-smoothed free-cash-flow yield is a standard, widely published valuation ratio rather than a cross-theme interaction — subtracting capex inside the numerator is simply the definition of FCF, not an investment-discipline conditioning — and oancf availability will additionally truncate the sample.
evidence: “a standard, widely published valuation ratio rather than a cross-theme interaction”

rationale: The INDICATOR→SIGN swap is a substantive repair rather than cosmetics — it converts a degenerate one-sided gate (which produced no computable long-short stats) into a two-sided spread that actively shorts cheap-but-accelerating firms — though it remains a close descendant of the archived gen-0 signal and its short leg is deep-value stocks, which may fight the FF5 value factor.
evidence: its short leg is deep-value stocks, which may fight the FF5 value factor

rationale: This is a conjunctive value × asset-growth double sort, i.e. essentially the classic B/M and asset-growth anomalies combined, and the claim that MIN "cannot be replicated by any linear mix of HML and CMA loadings" confuses a nonlinear construction rule with factor exposure — the resulting portfolio will load heavily on both HML and CMA regardless.
