evidence: this ratio is dominated by −(capx+aqc)/market cap

rationale: Incremental EBITDA per dollar of lagged capex is a genuinely different construct from investment level or growth — it is a marginal-productivity measure rather than a quantity — the sign logic and the winsorized small-denominator handling are internally consistent, and the value leg's role as a conditioner is economically coherent rather than a repackaged quality-times-value composite.
evidence: “a genuinely different construct from investment level or growth”

rationale: The economic mechanism is the same rich-valuation-plus-empire-building story as the archived Expensive_Externally_Funded_Empire (which already delivered strong FMB but a weak, wrong-signed portfolio spread), and the proposal swaps both legs without diagnosing why that FMB/alpha divergence occurred; separately, COALESCE(gdwl,0) inside DELTA will manufacture spurious first-time-reporting jumps.
evidence: swaps both legs without diagnosing why that FMB/alpha divergence occurred

rationale: Replacing the investment level with capex acceleration is a defensible refinement that shifts the signal from chronically capital-intensive firms to the turn in spending, and the diagnosis of which gen-0 signal was sign-consistent is accurate, but a second difference of an annual ratio is noisy and will cost coverage, so the gain over the parent signal is uncertain.
evidence: “a second difference of an annual ratio is noisy and will cost coverage”

rationale: The expression is internally coherent and the sign logic of the two-sided SIGN gate is correct, but it is a bundled double-tweak (RANK→IND_RANK, capx→capx+aqc) of the archived Signed_Capex_Discipline_Gated_Earnings_Yield that confounds attribution and risks reproducing the parent's near-zero alpha rather than diagnosing why the gated earnings yield failed to survive FF5.
evidence: risks reproducing the parent's near-zero alpha rather than diagnosing why

rationale: A second-moment notion of capital-allocation discipline is genuinely distinct from the level/change/acceleration constructions already archived and is not spanned by CMA, though the volatility leg is mechanically small for asset-light or near-zero-capex firms, so the spread should be checked for a size/asset-lightness tilt rather than a true stability effect.
evidence: volatility leg is mechanically small for asset-light or near-zero-capex firms

rationale: This is another leg-swap of the archived Own_History_Peak_Valuation_And_Investment (P/B→P/S, capx→capx+aqc) whose parent already had marginal, sign-inconsistent portfolio evidence, and TS_RANK over five annual observations is too coarse to give the "self-timing" construct much resolution.
evidence: “parent already had marginal, sign-inconsistent portfolio evidence”

rationale: The human-capital investment channel is untested in this archive and the sign logic is consistent, but the hiring-rate leg is a well-known published anomaly (Bazdresch–Belo–Lin employee growth), so the proposal's value hinges entirely on the interaction with market value per employee, and `emp` is a stale, sparsely reported field that will likely depress coverage.
evidence: “emp is a stale, sparsely reported field that will likely depress coverage”

rationale: Inventory growth in excess of sales growth is verbatim one of the Lev–Thiagarajan/Abarbanell–Bushee fundamental signals with the same predicted negative sign, so the reasoning's claim that this leg is "distinguishable from known anomalies" is simply wrong and the signal is largely a known anomaly scaled by a conventional price-to-sales rank.
evidence: “verbatim one of the Lev–Thiagarajan/Abarbanell–Bushee fundamental signals”

rationale: This is an industry z-score wrapper applied to an archived signal with no change to the mechanism — the definition of a cosmetic variant — and it is also not a cross-theme interaction at all, while the near-zero/negative TS_SUM(capx,5) denominator remains an unaddressed source of the very asset-lightness sorting it claims to fix.
evidence: “an industry z-score wrapper applied to an archived signal”

rationale: A clean single-variable ablation of the archive's best-performing gate structure with a coherent distributable-liquidity story and sign-consistent construction, though the net-cash-to-price leg overlaps substantially with the known net-leverage/net-debt-to-price effect, so any gain must be shown to come from the interaction rather than the leverage tilt.
evidence: “any gain must be shown to come from the interaction rather than the leverage tilt”

rationale: Converting the discrete one-year funding gate into a five-year persistence score is a substantive (not cosmetic) upgrade that directly addresses turnover and transitory-capex-pause contamination while preserving the two-sided sign structure that produced the archive's only clean alpha.
evidence: “a substantive (not cosmetic) upgrade”

rationale: Replacing SIGN with RANK destroys the two-sided structure the hypothesis relies on — the product becomes strictly non-negative, so the short leg is no longer cash-rich burners but low-cash low-surplus firms — and what remains is close to the already-tested Cheapness_Times_Self_Funded_Surplus with only cosmetic substitutions (ceq→che, oancf→ebitda) that previously delivered the wrong sign.
evidence: “Replacing SIGN with RANK destroys the two-sided structure”

rationale: A well-posed attribution test that holds the funding-state gate fixed while swapping the valuation leg, and is distinct from the archived capex-deceleration-gated earnings yield, giving an interpretable read on whether the alpha comes from the gate or the cash-to-price channel.
evidence: holds the funding-state gate fixed while swapping the valuation leg

rationale: The mechanism swap is legitimate and the choice of gross rather than net PP&E is well reasoned, but gross PP&E declines for only a small minority of firms, so the gate will be badly unbalanced (a thin, likely distress-tilted long leg) and the signal risks collapsing into an interacted asset-growth/investment anomaly.
evidence: the gate will be badly unbalanced

rationale: This is essentially a free-cash-flow/cash-flow-to-price yield with a cash-to-price term added — both long-published value anomalies — and the stated defense fails because adding a balance-sheet stock to an annual flow in one numerator is dimensionally incoherent and makes the ratio's units scale-dependent rather than genuinely cross-theme.
evidence: This is essentially a free-cash-flow/cash-flow-to-price yield

rationale: This is a mechanical fusion of two archived designs (magnitude coverage from Cash_Value_Times_Internal_Funding_Coverage plus the multi-year smoothing of Cash_Value_Times_Chronic_Self_Funding) rather than a new mechanism, and averaging a winsorized ratio whose denominator can approach zero leaves the un-ranked second leg's scale, not its economics, driving the spread.
evidence: a mechanical fusion of two archived designs

rationale: The switch from an industry-z-scored skewed level to a within-firm directional gate is a defensible repair and the hypothesis matches the expression's sign, but the gate is partly mechanically redundant with the cash-to-price leg (a rising runway is largely rising cash) and the che/(capx+aqc) ratio's near-zero denominators make its three-year mean unstable.
evidence: the gate is partly mechanically redundant with the cash-to-price leg

rationale: This is a clean, well-identified ablation that strips profitability out of the winning gate to test whether the archived alpha is investment restraint or an RMW-flavoured tilt, the gate is genuinely two-sided at an economically meaningful reference point, and the sign logic is internally consistent.
evidence: a clean, well-identified ablation that strips profitability out of the winning gate

rationale: The external-finance-dependence gate is a new channel for this archive but leans on the well-documented net-external-financing/composite-issuance anomaly, and the claim that it is "two-sided" is weak since ebitda exceeds new equity plus debt issuance for the large majority of firms, so the short leg will be small and tilted toward unprofitable microcaps.
evidence: the claim that it is "two-sided" is weak

rationale: SIGN(GROWTH(revt)−GROWTH(ppegt)) is essentially the same state variable as the archive's GROWTH(sale/ppegt), which already delivered a significantly wrong-signed FF5 alpha (−3.9%, t=−3.08) under the same positive prior, so the proposal re-tests a direction the archive has already contradicted without addressing why.
evidence: the proposal re-tests a direction the archive has already contradicted

rationale: Swapping RANK for IND_RANK on one leg of the archive's best signal is precisely the cosmetic variant the objective warns against; it is a robustness check rather than a new economic hypothesis and should be run as a diagnostic on the existing signal, not proposed as a distinct candidate.
evidence: precisely the cosmetic variant the objective warns against

rationale: A clean, well-specified one-leg ablation of the archive's best signal (organic-vs-acquisitive deployment) that isolates whether the valuation channel must be the unvalued cash hoard, though as a pure attribution swap it is unlikely to improve on the gen-4 result and risks being read as a cosmetic variant if it merely reproduces it.
evidence: risks being read as a cosmetic variant if it merely reproduces it

rationale: The serial-acquirer framing gives the three-year smoothing genuine economic content and the bounded term avoids the denominator instability that plagues averaged coverage ratios, but it remains an incremental smoothing of the gen-4 winner and inherits the undefined-when-capx+aqc≈0 problem for asset-light firms.
evidence: inherits the undefined-when-capx+aqc≈0 problem for asset-light firms

rationale: The bounded three-destination reformulation is a legitimate test of whether the effect is anti-acquisition or pro-owner, but it sits in mild tension with the archive's own payout-for-capex-substitution logic by pooling dividends and capex as jointly "good," so a null result will be hard to attribute cleanly between the two channels.
evidence: a null result will be hard to attribute cleanly between the two channels

rationale: Moving from the acquisition flow to the industry-adjusted goodwill stock is a substantively different, slower-moving state variable with a coherent impairment-risk mechanism, though goodwill intensity is close to a published intangible/impairment anomaly and COALESCE(gdwl,0) will lump genuine non-reporters with true zero-goodwill firms.
evidence: COALESCE(gdwl,0) will lump genuine non-reporters with true zero-goodwill firms

rationale: Netting a single year's acquisition outlay from the cash stock is a small perturbation of plain cash-to-price — a well-known published anomaly — and it abandons the cross-theme interaction structure entirely while the claimed dimensional coherence still subtracts an annual flow from a balance-sheet stock.
evidence: a small perturbation of plain cash-to-price

rationale: The conjunctive MIN is a genuinely different combination rule from the additive/multiplicative forms already tested and both validated states share an economic zero, but the two inputs have very different scales and upper ranges, so the MIN will mechanically be dominated by the bounded composition term for most healthy firms and the "weakest test" interpretation is weaker than claimed.
evidence: the MIN will mechanically be dominated by the bounded composition term

rationale: Because MIN(SIGN, ratio) already equals the ratio whenever the funding test passes and a constant when it fails, the ADD version produces the identical cross-sectional ordering except within the failing (short) group, making this much closer to an aggregation tweak of the archived Weakest_Discipline_Test than the "orthogonal cells" framing claims, and the stated rationale about incomparable ranges is factually wrong since both legs are already bounded in [-1,1].
evidence: much closer to an aggregation tweak of the archived Weakest_Discipline_Test

rationale: This is a genuine information-adding refinement of the archive's strongest signal — it preserves the economic zero of the earned-versus-raised comparison while re-ordering firms within each side by intensity, and the |internal|+|external| denominator is a defensible bounded normalization (worth checking behavior when EBITDA is negative and external flows are negative, where the sign convention is economically ambiguous).
evidence: the sign convention is economically ambiguous

rationale: The multi-year cumulation of the sources test is economically sensible and distinct from the archived uses-side persistence signal, but taking SIGN of the three-year sums discards exactly the "fraction of years" gradation that made chronic self-funding work (an MA of annual signs would be the better test), and the supporting reasoning misreports a drop in fmb_tstat from 4.27 to 3.98 as a gain.
evidence: taking SIGN of the three-year sums discards exactly the "fraction of years" gradation

rationale: Replacing the sparse, non-monotone goodwill stock with five-year cumulative acquisition cash flow is a correctly diagnosed repair that should restore coverage and a true zero point while retaining the slow-moving deal-history concept; the main risk is that an un-winsorized IND_ZSCORE of a heavily zero-inflated, right-skewed variable lets a few mega-acquirers dominate the spread.
evidence: a few mega-acquirers dominate the spread

rationale: The dominant leg is negative share-count growth, i.e. the well-published net share issuance anomaly, and since acquisition-financed issuance shows up in csho growth the two terms partially double-count the same event while being on non-comparable scales (a growth rate minus an assets-scaled outlay), so the signal likely just reloads a known anomaly interacted with cash-to-price.
evidence: the two terms partially double-count the same event

rationale: Scaling both outlay legs by market cap makes the second factor mechanically correlated with the RANK(cash/price) leg through the shared price denominator, so the construct largely squares a valuation tilt (and its capx/price term is itself the known investment-to-price anomaly) rather than isolating the deal-scale mechanism the hypothesis describes.
evidence: construct largely squares a valuation tilt

rationale: The expression matches the hypothesis and both legs are correctly bounded on a common [−1,+1] scale with a shared economic zero, but it is only an equal-weight sum of two already-archived second legs, so the likely outcome is an intermediate blend rather than new information — its value rests entirely on the paired comparison with the MIN version.
evidence: only an equal-weight sum of two already-archived second legs

rationale: The self-financing gate already exists in the archive in three forms (one-year sign, three-year-sum sign, and continuous intensity), and MA(SIGN,·) versus SIGN(TS_SUM,·) is a cosmetic smoothing variant of the same construct that is near-certain to be highly correlated with the existing 4.6–4.9 t-stat results without testing a new economic claim.
evidence: a cosmetic smoothing variant of the same construct

rationale: The dollar-weighted five-year mix is a defensible fix to the zero-inflated, skewed industry z-score of cumulative deal spend and is internally consistent, but it will be heavily collinear with the archived three-year moving-average mix (alpha 4.4%, t 4.15), so any gain is likely marginal rather than mechanistic.
evidence: any gain is likely marginal rather than mechanistic

rationale: The diagnosis is correct — the earlier MIN paired a winsorized-but-unbounded coverage ratio with a bounded mix, so the minimum was decided by scale rather than by economics — and placing both legs on a common bounded scale makes the conjunction claim genuinely testable against the additive form, though the incremental economic content over the two standalone legs remains modest.
evidence: the minimum was decided by scale rather than by economics

rationale: This is the only proposal opening a genuinely untested (short-horizon, reversible) investment dimension and its sign convention is coherent, but the second leg is close to the published inventory-growth anomaly (Thomas–Zhang) and the COALESCE(invt,0) convention forces all inventory-free firms to an exact zero that sits in the middle of the second leg's distribution, contaminating the interaction with a large, economically heterogeneous mass point.
evidence: COALESCE(invt,0) convention forces all inventory-free firms to an exact zero

rationale: Lagging an already-tested leg by one year on annual accounting data is a staleness diagnostic rather than a new signal, and because fiscal-year data are already stale at portfolio formation the most likely result is a mechanically attenuated copy of the archived organic-versus-acquisitive signal, which teaches little about the underlying mechanism.
evidence: a mechanically attenuated copy of the archived organic-versus-acquisitive signal

rationale: A coherent but largely mechanical stacking of three already-evaluated legs (the winning sources+uses sum plus the inventory leg), and the re-z-scoring of the two flow ratios changes the winner's construction, so any gain will be hard to attribute — worth one run, but it is consolidation rather than new economics.
evidence: any gain will be hard to attribute

rationale: This is a horizon swap that substitutes one already-tested leg (five-year deployment mix) for another already-tested leg (one-year mix) inside an already-tested composite, i.e. a cosmetic variant whose likely outcome is bracketed by results already in the archive.
evidence: a cosmetic variant whose likely outcome is bracketed by results already in the archive

rationale: The conditioning leg is the published hiring-rate/employment-growth anomaly (Bazdresch-Belo-Lin) with its standard sign, multiplied by the cash-to-price anomaly, so the signal is a product of two known effects rather than a new mechanism — and the "flat headcount preserves optionality" story conflates disciplined restraint with genuine demand decline.
evidence: a product of two known effects rather than a new mechanism

rationale: A legitimate financing-free ablation of Signal 1 that would sharpen attribution of slope versus alpha, but the raw bounded mix ratio (sd ≈ 0.3) is added to a unit-variance z-score, so the inventory channel will silently dominate and the "two operating channels" framing overstates the balance actually computed.
evidence: the inventory channel will silently dominate

rationale: The winsorize-before-industry-z fix is a genuine diagnosis-driven repair of the deal-history leg's skew problem, but the claim that the two legs are economically distinct is weak since both are acquisition-intensity measures at different horizons, and the raw-versus-z-scored scale mismatch again lets the legacy leg dominate.
evidence: both are acquisition-intensity measures at different horizons

rationale: This is the most informative proposal in the set because it takes a sign stance on capacity growth that deliberately opposes the published asset-growth/CMA prior yet is directly motivated by the archive's strongly negative capacity-shrinkage result, so the outcome is diagnostic either way — though the same raw-versus-z-score scale imbalance means the growth leg, not the deployment mix, will drive the spread.
evidence: the growth leg, not the deployment mix, will drive the spread

rationale: This is a pure normalization tweak of the archived Cash_Value_Times_Operating_Discipline_Composite (and a two-leg subset of Cash_Value_Times_Three_Channel_Discipline, which already z-scores both of these legs), so it adds no new economic content and merely reshuffles leg weights in a family already showing signs of weight-tuning overfit.
evidence: a pure normalization tweak of the archived Cash_Value_Times_Operating_Discipline_Composite

rationale: The three channels (bounded financing ratio, bounded deployment mix, own-history inventory) are exactly those of the archived Cash_Value_Times_Three_Channel_Discipline, differing only in whether two legs are z-scored, making this a cosmetic re-weighting rather than a substantively different hypothesis.
evidence: a cosmetic re-weighting rather than a substantively different hypothesis

rationale: Replacing the uniform-by-construction TS_RANK with a bounded, magnitude-preserving deviation-from-own-mean is a defensible measurement change (not just a rescaling) that cleanly separates "inventory concept" from "leg dispersion," though it remains an incremental refinement within a saturated family and the two legs' effective weights are still asserted rather than verified.
evidence: the two legs' effective weights are still asserted rather than verified

rationale: By the proposal's own logic the raw aqc-sum/assets penalty is an order of magnitude smaller than the z-scored mix, so the signal collapses toward the already-archived Cash_Value_Times_Organic_Versus_Acquisitive_Outlay — a near-rediscovery whose "repair" is again just relative scaling.
evidence: the signal collapses toward the already-archived Cash_Value_Times_Organic_Versus_Acquisitive_Outlay

rationale: Own-history capacity utilization is a genuinely new operating channel in this archive (distinct from the failed one-year sales/ppegt growth leg paired with a replacement-cost value leg), the sign logic is internally consistent, and the coverage argument versus inventory is economically motivated rather than cosmetic.
evidence: Own-history capacity utilization is a genuinely new operating channel in this archive

rationale: A coherent coverage-robust three-channel construction whose value lies mainly in being the controlled contrast to the inventory version, but it is largely redundant with Proposal 5 in this same batch and inherits the unverified raw-versus-z-scored weighting assumption of the gen-7 parent.
evidence: it is largely redundant with Proposal 5 in this same batch

rationale: This is essentially the well-documented value×accrual-quality combination (Piotroski-style earnings-quality screening of B/M; Desai-Rajgopal-Venkatachalam), and the multiplicative rank form is a near-monotone composite rather than a true conditional screen — plus if RANK is centered rather than [0,1], the product would rank expensive high-accrual firms as high as cheap clean ones.
evidence: This is essentially the well-documented value×accrual-quality combination

rationale: EBITDA/EV and cash conversion are both individually familiar, but the capital-structure-neutral multiple paired with a three-year OCF/EBITDA screen is a defensible and reasonably specific value-trap filter, though the conversion ratio is unstable for near-zero or negative EBITDA and needs a sign/denominator guard.
evidence: the conversion ratio is unstable for near-zero or negative EBITDA

rationale: The MIN operator is a genuinely non-additive functional form whose conjunctive logic matches the stated hypothesis, though in practice it will correlate heavily with a simple value+quality average and compresses/ties the tails, so the incremental content over a standard double-sort is the open empirical question.
evidence: “compresses/ties the tails”

rationale: Despite being labeled cross-theme, this is a purely additive average of cash-earnings yield with two Altman-Z distress components (RE/AT, WC/AT), i.e., a rediscovery of value-screened-for-distress composites with no interaction at all, and the hypothesis's conditional language is not what the expression computes.
evidence: “a rediscovery of value-screened-for-distress composites with no interaction at all”

rationale: The ratio is non-monotone across the sign of earnings — a loss-making firm with volatile ROA scores near zero (mid-rank) while a stable loss-maker scores very negative — so the expression does not implement the stated "stable earnings make a yield more valuable" hypothesis, and winsorizing at 1% does not fix the sign discontinuity from near-zero denominators.
evidence: “the expression does not implement the stated ‘stable earnings make a yield more valuable’ hypothesis”

target_name: Industry Sales Yield With Margin Improvement
rationale: Sales-to-price (Barbee) and gross profitability (Novy-Marx) are known individually, but conditioning within-industry cheapness on a five-year gross-margin trend is a reasonable and testable directional-quality refinement; verify that IND_RANK returns non-negative values so the product does not reward the doubly-bad corner.
evidence: “the product does not reward the doubly-bad corner”

rationale: The construction is internally consistent and the rank-difference does isolate a depreciation-to-price wedge that is plausibly orthogonal to HML, though the reviewer should be aware the surviving content is close to a capital-intensity/dp-to-price tilt that CMA may partially absorb.
evidence: “close to a capital-intensity/dp-to-price tilt that CMA may partially absorb”

rationale: This is structurally the same ZSCORE(WINSOR(yield))×INDICATOR template as the archived Solvency-Gated Enterprise Earnings Yield with only the gate swapped, and the gate itself is a direct restatement of the published Sloan balance-sheet accrual anomaly (with a crude, cash-and-debt-unadjusted accrual definition).
evidence: “structurally the same ... template as the archived Solvency-Gated Enterprise Earnings Yield”

rationale: Differencing GP/P against AT/P mechanically nets out the price scaling and leaves something very close to gross-profits-to-assets, i.e. a rediscovery of Novy-Marx gross profitability that RMW largely spans, contradicting the claim that FF5 leaves it unpriced.
evidence: “a rediscovery of Novy-Marx gross profitability that RMW largely spans”

rationale: Self-described as a "near-controlled contrast" with the archived gated-value signal, it reuses the identical yield×indicator template with a level-to-change tweak on the gate — a cosmetic variant unlikely to flip an alpha that was negative for portfolio-composition reasons, and its gate overlaps heavily with the accrual gate proposed alongside it.
evidence: unlikely to flip an alpha that was negative for portfolio-composition reasons

rationale: Substituting a time-series (own-history) valuation rank for cross-sectional cheapness is a genuinely different design that plausibly escapes HML spanning, and the margin gate is coherently specified — though the margin-trend leg echoes the archived industry sales-yield signal and the TS_RANK window units should be verified.
evidence: “the TS_RANK window units should be verified”

target_name: Dividend Yield Per Unit Of Leverage
rationale: This is essentially the long-published dividend-yield anomaly divided by a bounded leverage ratio, it collapses to a large zero mass for non-payers (biasing coverage and portfolio composition), and the stated rationale references a prior signal not in the archive.
evidence: “essentially the long-published dividend-yield anomaly divided by a bounded leverage ratio”

rationale: This is a monotone re-ranking of the archive's existing "Obligation-Netted Fundamental To Price" with WINSOR swapped for IND_RANK — a cosmetic variant of an already-evaluated signal rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the stated goal (diagnosing whether the alpha is tail-driven) is a robustness check, not a new hypothesis.
evidence: “a cosmetic variant of an already-evaluated signal”

target_name: Net Cash Cheapness With Real Gross Profit
rationale: The net-cash-to-price valuation leg is a genuinely different balance-sheet channel from the earnings- and book-based legs already tested and the conditioning story is coherent with monotone non-negative ranks, though the product will likely be dominated by the well-documented gross profitability leg, so the incremental content over Novy-Marx is uncertain.
evidence: “product will likely be dominated by the well-documented gross profitability leg”

rationale: This is a near-duplicate of the archive's failed "Weakest-Link Cheap And Profitable" — same MIN-of-two-ranks construction with ib+dp→ebitda and oancf/at→oancf/lt substituted — so it re-tests an already-rejected conjunctive design with a highly correlated coverage proxy.
evidence: “re-tests an already-rejected conjunctive design”

rationale: The persistence-count formulation of accrual conservatism is a legitimately novel quality state distinct from the level-based accruals anomaly, but the reasoning is internally wrong — a zero count collapses the product to exactly zero for a potentially large mass of firms, destroying the valuation ordering there — so the construction is less continuous than claimed.
evidence: “a zero count collapses the product to exactly zero”

rationale: The short-side framing and liabilities-to-price valuation leg are a reasonable economic complement to the long-side proposals and the sign is internally consistent, but the construct is close to the published distress anomaly and liabilities-to-price is mechanically correlated with book-to-market, whose unconditional sign runs opposite to the expectation.
evidence: whose unconditional sign runs opposite to the expectation

rationale: This is the third instance of the same MUL(IND_RANK cheap yield, IND_RANK margin-dynamics) template already tried unsuccessfully in the archive with only the quality leg swapped (trend/level → volatility), and a five-observation annual VOL is a very noisy stability estimate; it also cites a "volatility-deflated yield" predecessor not present in the archive.
evidence: “same MUL ... template already tried unsuccessfully in the archive”

target_name: All-Obligation Netted Cheapness With Gross Profit
rationale: Substituting total liabilities for interest-bearing debt destroys the economic content the hypothesis claims — since (che − lt) is negative and lt-dominated for almost all firms, the "cheapness" leg becomes essentially a *low*-liabilities-to-price (i.e., anti-value, low-leverage) rank rather than a net-cash yield, making this both internally inconsistent with the stated hypothesis and a one-ingredient cosmetic edit of the archive's existing net-cash-times-gross-profit signal.
evidence: “the ‘cheapness’ leg becomes essentially a low-liabilities-to-price rank rather than a net-cash yield”

target_name: Net Cash Cheapness With Liability Coverage
rationale: Swapping the RMW-spanned gross-profitability leg for cash-flow coverage of liabilities is a genuinely diagnostic, economically motivated change to the archive's best performer that isolates whether the alpha comes from a profitability channel or a balance-sheet-safety channel, though the oancf requirement will cut coverage and any coverage decline should be checked before attributing changes to the mechanism.
evidence: “the oancf requirement will cut coverage”

target_name: Cheap And Not Raising Outside Capital
rationale: The financing leg is a near-direct restatement of the published net-external-financing / net-share-issuance anomaly (Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan, Daniel-Titman, Pontiff-Woodgate), so the interaction is likely to be driven by an already-known standalone effect rather than by the claimed value-quality conditioning, and the proposal offers no test to separate the two.
evidence: “interaction is likely to be driven by an already-known standalone effect”

rationale: High book-to-market interacted with weak operating cash flow is essentially Piotroski's high-BM × financial-strength result (and the well-documented value-premium-concentrated-among-non-distressed finding) with the sign reversed, and it is also largely the mirror image of Signal 2 in the same batch, so it adds little independent information.
evidence: essentially Piotroski's high-BM × financial-strength result

rationale: Asset-composition as a conditioner on book-to-market is a distinct and untested channel here with high coverage and correctly applied industry ranks, but act/at is a coarse, heavily industry- and size-driven proxy that may end up restating asset tangibility rather than the reliability of book value, so the construction is plausible but thin.
evidence: act/at is a coarse, heavily industry- and size-driven proxy

target_name: Five-Year Cash Earnings To Enterprise Claims
rationale: Long-run normalized cash earnings scaled by enterprise value is close to the published enterprise-multiple anomaly (Loughran-Wellman) and to Anderson-Brooks-style multi-year earnings yield, and the stated claim that the denominator is "strictly positive by construction" is false — deep net-cash firms can have mcap + lt − che ≤ 0, producing sign-flipped outliers that WINSOR on the ratio will not cleanly fix.
evidence: close to the published enterprise-multiple anomaly

target_name: Net Cash Cheapness With Accrual-Free Coverage
rationale: This is a one-input substitution (oancf → ib+dp) in an archived signal with identical economics and identical structure — a cosmetic coverage-driven variant rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the accrual-vs-cash distinction it discards is precisely the earnings-quality content the archive's other signals treat as informative.

rationale: The dominant leg is gross-profits-to-market, a well-documented published anomaly (Novy-Marx's "other side of value"), and the second leg (working capital/assets) is a weak, loosely motivated screen, so the min-combination adds only modest incremental content over a known factor.
evidence: gross-profits-to-market, a well-documented published anomaly

rationale: This is a cosmetic variant of the archived Retained Profit Accumulation Yield (MA window 3→2, denominator ME→ME+LT) rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the resulting quantity is close to a standard earnings-to-enterprise-value ratio.
evidence: a cosmetic variant of the archived Retained Profit Accumulation Yield

rationale: EBITDA/EV combined with a subtracted liability-growth flow is dimensionally coherent and economically motivated, though the reviewer should check that the Δliabilities term does not dominate and reduce the signal to a repackaged debt-issuance/asset-growth anomaly.
evidence: Δliabilities term does not dominate and reduce the signal to a repackaged debt-issuance/asset-growth anomaly

rationale: (Current assets − total liabilities)/market cap is exactly Graham's net-current-asset-value (net-net) ratio, a long-published value strategy, so this is a direct rediscovery with no cross-theme content beyond a standard balance-sheet value ratio.
evidence: exactly Graham's net-current-asset-value (net-net) ratio

rationale: Economically sensible and internally consistent, but subtracting depreciation from operating cash flow largely reverses the non-cash add-back and pushes the signal toward a conventional earnings-to-price ratio, so its incremental information over E/P should be verified.
evidence: subtracting depreciation from operating cash flow largely reverses the non-cash add-back

rationale: The construction is internally consistent (a nonnegative yield scaling a signed quality state, as claimed) and the cash-source distinction is a reasonable cross-theme idea, though both legs (cash-to-market, retained-earnings-to-assets) are individually known and the product will be dominated by small, cash-rich firms.
evidence: the product will be dominated by small, cash-rich firms

rationale: Adding back ΔNWC to OANCF simply reconstructs net income plus depreciation, so the signal collapses into the classic Lakonishok-Shleifer-Vishny cash-flow-to-price anomaly, and the stated motivation is internally inconsistent (it claims to pursue the "conservative-cash mechanism" that worked by *subtracting* depreciation, while this construction is strictly less conservative, and the coverage argument is dubious since dp is more widely reported than act/lct).
evidence: the signal collapses into the classic Lakonishok-Shleifer-Vishny cash-flow-to-price anomaly

rationale: This is essentially the archived Self-Financed EBITDA Value with the liability penalty re-scaled, i.e. a cosmetic re-weighting rather than a new mechanism, and the subtraction of a dimensionless Δ(lt/at) (~0.02) from an EBITDA/EV yield (~0.10) imposes an arbitrary, uncalibrated relative weight that will be dominated by the valuation leg anyway.
evidence: a cosmetic re-weighting rather than a new mechanism

rationale: The EV-scaling of cash is a sensible fix to the small/levered concentration problem, but the second leg (MA(oancf/lct)) is recycled from Claim-Covered Dividend Value, which already failed badly (fmb 0.855), and the multiplicative form is sign-unstable because negative operating cash flow flips the product and scrambles the ranking of cash-rich distressed firms.
evidence: recycled from Claim-Covered Dividend Value, which already failed badly

rationale: Penalizing a smoothed earnings yield by the *absolute* non-depreciation accrual residual is a genuinely novel construction (accrual-quality-adjusted E/P rather than the signed Sloan accrual), units are internally consistent since both terms are dollar flows scaled by market cap, and it plausibly separates transparent from opaque cheapness.
evidence: a genuinely novel construction

rationale: The diagnosis of the failed liquidity-recovery signal is sound and the substitution of gross-profit productivity trend is economically better motivated, but "high book-to-market plus improving fundamental profitability" is close to a direct rediscovery of Piotroski's F-score value strategy and of the well-documented value-plus-quality interaction.
evidence: close to a direct rediscovery of Piotroski's F-score value strategy

rationale: Replacing average coverage with a worst-case TS_MIN coverage floor is a substantively different construct (downside solvency, not mean profitability) and the weak-link form differs from the archived multiplicative Through-Cycle signal, though it is still assembled entirely from previously tested legs and a 3-year annual minimum is a noisy estimate of "worst case."
evidence: a 3-year annual minimum is a noisy estimate of "worst case."

rationale: The expression correctly implements a double haircut (depreciation reserve plus the one-sided working-capital-release penalty via MAX(...,0)) and matches the stated hypothesis and positive sign, though it is essentially the intersection of two already-tested archive constructions and will inherit their thin ~0.07 coverage, so the incremental information is modest.
evidence: essentially the intersection of two already-tested archive constructions

rationale: This is a near-mechanical variant of the archived Earned-Cash Discount with the retained-earnings stock swapped for its own already-tested flow (Retained Profit Accumulation Yield), and since Δre/at is essentially dividend-net ROA the signal reduces to the familiar cash-to-price × profitability composite rather than a new mechanism.
evidence: a near-mechanical variant of the archived Earned-Cash Discount

rationale: The revision is diagnostically motivated (rescaling cheapness to all claims to defuse the leverage artifact behind the weak FMB slope) and sign-consistent, but placing lt in both the valuation denominator and the productivity trend creates a mechanical shared-denominator interaction that could confound interpretation of any improvement.
evidence: creates a mechanical shared-denominator interaction that could confound interpretation

rationale: The added VOL(oancf/at,3) term is one to two orders of magnitude smaller than typical price-to-sales values, so the denominator is dominated by P/S and the signal collapses to margin × sales-yield — a rediscovery of the archived Durable Margin Sales Value and Through-Cycle Margin Floor Value that already produced zero portfolio alpha.
evidence: the denominator is dominated by P/S and the signal collapses to margin × sales-yield

rationale: The one-sided burn penalty is internally consistent, dimensionally sound (dollars added to dollars), and preserves the intended positive sign, but because maintenance-adjusted burn is small relative to market cap for most firms the adjustment will only re-rank a distressed minority, limiting expected incremental power over plain cash-to-price.
evidence: the adjustment will only re-rank a distressed minority

rationale: The construction is internally coherent — a nonnegative assets-to-market leg amplifies a signed change in liability share, so the short leg is levering-up asset-cheap firms and the long leg deleveraging ones, consistent with the negative expected sign — and it explores a genuinely different (trap-side) direction than the archive, with the main caveat that Δ(lt/at) overlaps the known debt-issuance/leverage-change anomaly and the value-leg component pulls in the opposite direction.
evidence: Δ(lt/at) overlaps the known debt-issuance/leverage-change anomaly

rationale: This is a narrower re-cut of the already-tested Working-Capital-Release-Adjusted Cash Yield, and it is internally inconsistent because lct includes debt in current liabilities and notes payable whose increases never enter oancf, so the haircut penalizes financing inflows that were never counted in the numerator.
evidence: lct includes debt in current liabilities

rationale: The denominator adds a one-year liability *flow* to a market-cap *stock*, a dimensional mismatch that makes the adjustment negligible for most firms so the signal collapses into a plain change-in-earnings-to-price measure — essentially the already-tested Retained Profit Accumulation Yield template and a well-known earnings-growth-to-price anomaly.
evidence: a one-year liability flow to a market-cap stock

rationale: The one-sided stock-based deficit penalty is economically distinct from the earlier flow-burn and multiplicative-profitability versions of cash-to-price, and the sign logic is coherent, though it reuses the archive's che/(mktcap + max(penalty,0)) template closely enough that incremental information over Earned-Cash Discount is uncertain.
evidence: reuses the archive's che/(mktcap + max(penalty,0)) template closely

rationale: TREND(cogs/sale) is mechanically the negative of the gross-margin trend, so this is the sign-flipped mirror of the archive's sales-yield × margin-quality family (Durable Margin, Through-Cycle Margin Floor) and adds little beyond a known gross-margin-trend value interaction.
evidence: the sign-flipped mirror of the archive's sales-yield × margin-quality family

rationale: This is a pure parameter/aggregation tweak of Maintenance Cash Runway Discount (MA over 2 → TS_SUM over 3 of the identical oancf−dp burn), i.e., a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism.
evidence: a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism

rationale: Sign logic is internally consistent and the deteriorating-turnover trap leg is economically distinct from the failed leverage-change leg of Rising-Claims Asset Trap, though it reuses that same at/mktcap × trend template and the choice of current assets rather than total assets as the turnover base is unmotivated.
evidence: the choice of current assets rather than total assets as the turnover base is unmotivated

rationale: The deficit penalty is sign-inconsistent when applied to a numerator that can be negative — inflating the denominator makes loss-making, deficit-laden firms' cash-flow yields *less* negative and therefore rank *higher*, exactly reversing the intended trap-avoidance mechanism that worked when the numerator was always-positive cash (che).
evidence: inflating the denominator makes loss-making firms' cash-flow yields less negative

rationale: This is a cosmetic respecification of the archived Idle-Asset Value Trap (same at/mktcap × NEG(TREND(productivity)) template with sale/act swapped for gross-profit/at), and the productivity leg alone is close to a known declining-gross-profitability signal.
evidence: a cosmetic respecification of the archived Idle-Asset Value Trap

rationale: The min(oancf, ib+dp) construction is internally coherent and correctly implements the stated conservatism (it binds precisely when working-capital releases inflate cash flow), though it is structurally close to the archived Cash-Bounded Operating Claim Yield and the base leg is essentially the classic cash-flow-to-price anomaly.
evidence: structurally close to the archived Cash-Bounded Operating Claim Yield

rationale: A two-variable stock ratio with no genuine cross-theme interaction that essentially rediscovers the well-documented cash-holdings/net-cash-to-price anomaly, and it sits adjacent to the archived Enterprise Earned-Cash Discount family.
evidence: A two-variable stock ratio with no genuine cross-theme interaction

rationale: This mechanically bolts the deficit denominator from one archived signal onto the archived Liability-Productivity Sales Value expression, and the adjustment misfires in the same direction problem: when the EBITDA/liability trend is negative, shrinking the valuation leg for deficit firms makes the product *less* negative and thus ranks the worst firms higher.
evidence: makes the product less negative and thus ranks the worst firms higher

rationale: The expression is internally consistent with the stated negative sign (cheap assets × large unexplained accrual magnitude), and the absolute-value opacity framing is a defensible departure from the weak signed reconciliation predecessor, though it overlaps conceptually with known accrual-quality/earnings-opacity effects and the multiplicative scaling makes the value leg mostly a magnitude amplifier.
evidence: the multiplicative scaling makes the value leg mostly a magnitude amplifier

rationale: This is essentially an algebraic reparameterization of the archive's already-tested "Deficit-Adjusted Cash Value" (moving the deficit from denominator to numerator), which will be very highly correlated with it and constitutes a cosmetic rather than substantive variant.
evidence: an algebraic reparameterization of the archive's already-tested Deficit-Adjusted Cash Value

rationale: The diagnosis of why the earlier MIN-combination failed is sound and the continuous product creates economically ordered tails, though it remains a value×quality composite in the same family as the previously weak sales-yield interaction signals.
evidence: same family as the previously weak sales-yield interaction signals

rationale: GROWTH(act−che) minus GROWTH(sale) is arithmetically the declining noncash-current-asset turnover the proposal claims not to reuse, making it a near-duplicate of the archived "Idle-Asset Value Trap" and, more broadly, of the well-known accruals/working-capital-growth anomaly.
evidence: more broadly, of the well-known accruals/working-capital-growth anomaly

rationale: Internally consistent and the one-sided truncation is well motivated, but ebitda−oancf embeds cash interest and taxes, so the "unrealized earnings" leg partly proxies for leverage and tax burden rather than accrual quality, and the value×accruals combination is close to established anomaly territory.
evidence: ebitda−oancf embeds cash interest and taxes

rationale: TS_RANK is strictly non-negative, so unlike the TREND version the product can never push cheap firms into the short tail and the composite becomes a monotone rescaling of the sales-yield value signal — which implies a positive slope, directly contradicting the stated negative expected sign.
evidence: the composite becomes a monotone rescaling of the sales-yield value signal

rationale: The symmetric-penalty motivation is a genuine economic distinction from the archived lower-bound claim yield, but ebitda−oancf is dominated by cash interest and taxes rather than accrual misalignment, so the "concordance" interpretation of the numerator is only loosely supported by what the expression actually computes.
evidence: ebitda−oancf is dominated by cash interest and taxes

rationale: This is a mechanical equal-weight rank-sum of two already-evaluated archive signals (Idle-Asset Value Trap and Short-Term Funding Sales Trap) whose legs share a common price-scaled cheapness component, so it is an ensemble rather than a new mechanism and will almost surely land between the two parent results.
evidence: mechanical equal-weight rank-sum of two already-evaluated archive signals

rationale: Pairing the archive's strongest value leg with a genuinely untested standalone current-asset productivity trend is defensible and avoids sign-inversion from multiplying a signed quality term, but the 50/50 rank weighting hands half the signal to a leg with no standalone evidence and risks diluting the parent's alpha.
evidence: the 50/50 rank weighting hands half the signal to a leg with no standalone evidence

rationale: Combining maintenance-cash-supported sales value with an independently ranked (rather than multiplied) easing-funding-pressure leg is a coherent construction and the sign logic is internally consistent, though it is close in spirit to the previous proposal and its incremental information over the archived parent is likely modest.
evidence: close in spirit to the previous proposal

rationale: This is a cosmetic variant of the archived Liability-Productivity Sales Value, differing only by replacing lt with lct in the denominator of the EBITDA-productivity trend, which is exactly the kind of superficial substitution the objective warns against.
evidence: cosmetic variant of the archived Liability-Productivity Sales Value

rationale: Swapping the flow-based maintenance cash margin for the stock-based retained-earnings term in the archived Earned-Cash Discount is a modest but economically motivated change, and the stated sign logic (nonnegative cash yield leg, direction set by the quality term) correctly matches what the expression computes — though it remains a recombination of two well-worn archive components.
evidence: a modest but economically motivated change

rationale: A direct rank-sum of two already-evaluated archive signals with no new economic content; blending a t_alpha 1.81 signal with a t_alpha 2.88 signal is portfolio bookkeeping, not a test of a distinct mechanism.
evidence: two already-evaluated archive signals with no new economic content

rationale: This is the archive's Maintenance-Productive Cash Discount with a single denominator tweak (adding the retained-earnings deficit already tested in Deficit-Adjusted Cash Value), so it is a near-collinear cosmetic merger of two existing signals rather than a new mechanism, even though the construction is internally consistent and the nonnegativity argument is correct.
evidence: single denominator tweak ... cosmetic merger of two existing signals

rationale: It re-specifies the identical two legs of the archive's best signal (Productive Deficit-Adjusted Cash Value) as a raw product instead of a rank sum, which adds no new economic content and introduces a scale-domination problem because a small-magnitude TREND(sale/act) is multiplied by a fat-tailed cash-yield level.
evidence: identical two legs ... as a raw product instead of a rank sum

rationale: Swapping sale for ebitda in the productivity-trend leg of an already-evaluated SUMRANK signal is a mechanical ingredient substitution likely to be highly correlated with the original (and the turnover/margin decomposition it invokes is essentially published DuPont-component evidence), so the incremental information is small.
evidence: mechanical ingredient substitution likely to be highly correlated with the original

rationale: This is a genuinely new pairing of two independently supported legs (deficit-adjusted cash yield and easing short-term funding intensity) with no shared price-scaled denominator and a sign that matches the expression's direction, though it reuses a familiar SUMRANK template and the funding-relief leg has only been validated interacted with sales yield.
evidence: the funding-relief leg has only been validated interacted with sales yield

rationale: Economically coherent and correctly signed, but it differs from the archive's Cash-Uncovered Claim Growth Trap by a single dp term inside the same hinge, which will mostly shift the truncation threshold and produce a signal nearly collinear with the one already tested.
evidence: single dp term inside the same hinge

rationale: This is the mirror image of the already-evaluated Idle-Asset Value Trap within a sales-yield × trend template that the archive has mined repeatedly with weak results, and because sale appears in both factors the "interaction" is partly mechanical rather than a clean value-times-quality conjunction; the turnover-change component also closely tracks published asset-turnover (DuPont) return predictability.
evidence: mirror image of the already-evaluated Idle-Asset Value Trap

rationale: This is a mechanical blend of two already-tested archive winners (Productive Deficit-Adjusted Cash Value and Funding-Safe Deficit Cash Value) that share an identical cash leg, so it is a re-weighting exercise whose result is largely predictable from the correlation of the two parents rather than a new mechanism.
evidence: mechanical blend of two already-tested archive winners

rationale: The cash-provenance leg (cash net of recent liability expansion) and the current-asset productivity leg are economically distinct and non-overlapping, and the construction is sign-consistent with broad coverage, though it is a template substitution on a prior composite rather than a genuinely new mechanism.
evidence: template substitution on a prior composite

rationale: The numerator already penalizes recent total-liability growth, so the NEG(TREND(lct/cogs)) leg substantially double-counts short-term funding expansion, and the overall form is a one-component swap into the archived Funding-Safe Deficit Cash Value template.
evidence: substantially double-counts short-term funding expansion

rationale: Folding both the deficit and the liability-growth penalty into the denominator is a coherent, sign-consistent single-ratio alternative to the two archived adjustments (multiplicative shrinkage rather than subtraction), which is a real structural difference, though the incremental information over the existing deficit-adjusted cash yield may be modest.
evidence: the incremental information over the existing deficit-adjusted cash yield may be modest

rationale: This is a single-input substitution (DELTA(che) for oancf) into the archived Cash-Uncovered Claim Growth Trap, and DELTA(che) is a weaker coverage proxy since cash can rise from financing or asset sales, making it partly a rediscovery of the liability-growth/working-capital accrual anomaly.
evidence: cash can rise from financing or asset sales

rationale: Multiplying two one-sided truncated legs (whose components are both already in the archive, one of them weak) leaves a large mass of exact zeros so the cross-sectional rank degenerates into ties over most of the universe, making any apparent improvement over the parent trap hard to attribute to the added conditioning.
evidence: large mass of exact zeros so the cross-sectional rank degenerates into ties
